questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
For a liquid, the permeability of a sandy soil having a void ratio of 0.60 was determined as 0.14 cm/s. Considering the same liquid and by using Taylor’s equation, the permeability (in cm/s) of this soil corresponding to the void ratio of 0.80 is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Permeability)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • State 1: \(e_1 = 0.60\), \(k_1 = 0.14\) cm/s
    • State 2: \(e_2 = 0.80\)
  • Aim: Find the new permeability \(k_2\) in cm/s.

3. Core Concepts:

Taylor's Equation (Kozeny-Carman):

\[k \propto \dfrac{e^3}{1+e}\]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Ratio equation:
    \[\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{e_2^3/(1+e_2)}{e_1^3/(1+e_1)}\]
  2. Compute intermediates:
    Numerator: \(\dfrac{0.80^3}{1.80} = \dfrac{0.512}{1.8} = 0.2844\)
    Denominator: \(\dfrac{0.60^3}{1.60} = \dfrac{0.216}{1.6} = 0.1350\)
  3. Calculate \(k_2\):
    \[k_2 = 0.14 \times \dfrac{0.2844}{0.1350} = 0.14 \times 2.107 = 0.295 \approx 0.29 \text{ cm/s}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.29 cm/s  |  Accepted key range: 0.28 to 0.32

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
To obtain undisturbed clay soil sample, an Area Ratio of 10 % needs to be achieved for a thin walled sampling tube. If the outer diameter of the tube is 50.8 mm, the inner diameter (in mm) is _______
(rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Exploration (Area Ratio)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Area ratio: \(A_r = 10\%\)
    • Outer diameter: \(D_o = 50.8\) mm
  • Aim: Find the inner diameter \(D_i\) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Area Ratio Formula:

\[A_r (\%) = \dfrac{D_o^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2} \times 100\]

A low \(A_r \le 10\%\) ensures the sample is 'undisturbed'. \(D_i\) must be slightly less than \(D_o\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply formula:
    \[0.10 = \dfrac{50.8^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2} = \dfrac{2580.64 - D_i^2}{D_i^2}\]
  2. Isolate \(D_i\):
    \[0.10 \cdot D_i^2 = 2580.64 - D_i^2\]
    \[1.10 \cdot D_i^2 = 2580.64 \implies D_i^2 = 2346.04\]
  3. Solve:
    \[D_i = \sqrt{2346.04} = 48.44 \approx 48.4 \text{ mm}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 48.4 mm  |  Accepted key range: 48.2 to 48.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: As per the Rankine’s earth pressure theory, which of the following statements is/are FALSE?
options: For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
structuredOptions.html: For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
structuredOptions.html: For the active earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
structuredOptions.html: For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ + \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.
structuredOptions.html: For the passive earth pressure, the inclination of failure plane is \( (45^\circ - \phi/2) \) with respect to the major principal plane.

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theory

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall & Comprehension
  • Given Data: Statements regarding the inclination of the failure plane relative to the major principal plane in Rankine's earth pressure theory.
  • Aim: Identify which statements are FALSE.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: Failure occurs on a plane oriented at angle \(\theta_f\) from the major principal plane:
    \[\theta_f = 45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2} \quad \text{for ALL stress states at failure}\]
  • Active State: Soil mass expands horizontally. Vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) = major principal stress (\(\sigma_1\)); horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\) = minor principal stress (\(\sigma_3\)).
    Major principal plane = horizontal plane.
    Failure plane inclination from major principal plane = \(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\).
  • Passive State: Soil mass compressed horizontally. Horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\) becomes major principal stress (\(\sigma_1\)); vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) becomes minor principal stress (\(\sigma_3\)).
    Major principal plane = vertical plane.
    Failure plane inclination from major principal plane = \(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\).

4. Solution Method:

Check each option against the rule that the angle with respect to the major principal plane is always \(45^\circ + \phi/2\):

  • (A) Active pressure angle is \(\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to major principal plane. → TRUE
  • (B) Active pressure angle is \(\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to major principal plane. → FALSE
  • (C) Passive pressure angle is \(\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to major principal plane. → TRUE
  • (D) Passive pressure angle is \(\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to major principal plane. → FALSE

Note: Textbooks often state the passive failure plane is at \(\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to the horizontal. However, since the horizontal is the minor principal plane in the passive case, the angle relative to the major principal plane remains strictly \(\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\).

6. Final Answer:

Correct options (False statements): (B); (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
An infinite slope with slope angle \( \beta = 22^\circ \) consists of soil with the following properties:
Unit weight \( \gamma = 15.72 \) kN/m³
Cohesion \( c' = 12 \) kPa
Angle of internal friction \( \phi' = 15^\circ \)
The critical height of the slope (in m) is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stability of Slopes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Slope angle: \(\beta = 22^\circ\)
    • Unit weight: \(\gamma = 15.72\) kN/m³
    • Cohesion: \(c' = 12\) kPa
    • Angle of internal friction: \(\phi' = 15^\circ\)
  • Aim: Find the critical height of the slope (\(H_c\)) in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Infinite Slope Stability (\(c\)-\(\phi\) soil):
    \[F_s = \dfrac{c' + \gamma z \cos^2\beta \tan\phi'}{\gamma z \cos\beta \sin\beta}\]
  • Critical Height: Set \(F_s = 1\) and \(z = H_c\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Rearrange for \(H_c\):
    \[\gamma H_c(\tan\beta - \tan\phi') = \dfrac{c'}{\cos^2\beta}\]
    \[H_c = \dfrac{c'}{\gamma \cos^2\beta (\tan\beta - \tan\phi')}\]
  2. Compute trigonometric values:
    \(\cos(22^\circ) = 0.92718 \implies \cos^2(22^\circ) = 0.85967\)
    \(\tan(22^\circ) = 0.40403\)
    \(\tan(15^\circ) = 0.26795\)
    \(\tan\beta - \tan\phi' = 0.40403 - 0.26795 = 0.13608\)
  3. Final Calculation:
    \[H_c = \dfrac{12}{15.72 \times 0.85967 \times 0.13608} = \dfrac{12}{1.8389} = 6.53 \text{ m}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6.53 m  |  Accepted key range: 6.40 to 6.80

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A circular pile of 600 mm diameter and 6 m length is embedded in a saturated clayey soil. Undrained cohesion of the soil is 80 kPa. Unit weight of the soil is 19.20 kN/m³. The adhesion factor is 0.54. If the diameter of the pile is doubled to 1200 mm (keeping the length constant), the ratio of pile capacity of 1200 mm diameter pile to that of 600 mm diameter pile is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations (Pile Capacity)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pile 1: \(D_1 = 0.6\) m, \(L_1 = 6\) m
    • Pile 2: \(D_2 = 1.2\) m, \(L_2 = 6\) m
    • Undrained cohesion: \(c_u = 80\) kPa
    • Adhesion factor: \(\alpha = 0.54\)
  • Aim: Ratio of pile capacity of 1200 mm pile to 600 mm pile.

3. Core Concepts:

Ultimate Pile Capacity in Clay (\(\phi_u = 0\)):

\[Q_u = c_u N_c A_b + \alpha c_u A_s\]

where \(N_c = 9\) (Skempton's factor), \(A_b = \dfrac{\pi}{4}D^2\), \(A_s = \pi D L\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. General capacity equation:
    \[Q_u(D) = 9(80)\dfrac{\pi}{4}D^2 + 0.54(80)(\pi)(D)(6) = 180\pi D^2 + 259.2\pi D\]
  2. Pile 1 (\(D = 0.6\) m):
    \[Q_{u1} = 180\pi(0.36) + 259.2\pi(0.6) = 64.8\pi + 155.52\pi = 220.32\pi \text{ kN}\]
  3. Pile 2 (\(D = 1.2\) m):
    \[Q_{u2} = 180\pi(1.44) + 259.2\pi(1.2) = 259.2\pi + 311.04\pi = 570.24\pi \text{ kN}\]
  4. Ratio:
    \[\dfrac{Q_{u2}}{Q_{u1}} = \dfrac{570.24\pi}{220.32\pi} = 2.59\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.59  |  Accepted key range: 2.50 to 2.65

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A group of 25 circular piles is arranged in 5 × 5 uniform pattern in a soft clay soil with equal spacing in both the directions. These are friction piles with negligible end bearing.

Consider the following details:
Diameter of each pile = 1 m
Length of each pile = 15 m
Cohesion of the soil = 20 kN/m²
Unit weight of the soil = 16 kN/m³
Adhesion factor = 0.75

Considering the efficiency of the pile group as unity, the optimum value of the ratio of the pile spacing to pile diameter is _______
(rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations (Pile Groups)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • 25 piles in a \(5 \times 5\) grid; \(D = 1\) m, \(L = 15\) m
    • Soil cohesion: \(c = 20\) kN/m²; Adhesion factor: \(\alpha = 0.75\)
    • Group efficiency: \(\eta = 1\)
    • Friction piles with negligible end bearing.
  • Aim: Find the optimum ratio of spacing to diameter (\(S/D\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Group Efficiency: \(\eta = 1 \implies Q_{ug} = n \cdot Q_u\)
  • Individual Pile Capacity (no end bearing): \(Q_u = \alpha c (\pi D L)\)
  • Block Failure Capacity (side friction only, block width \(B = 4S + D\) for \(5 \times 5\) group):
    \(Q_{ug} = c \times 4B \times L\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Individual Capacity:
    \[Q_u = 0.75 \times 20 \times \pi \times 1 \times 15 = 225\pi \text{ kN}\]
    \[\Sigma Q_u = 25 \times 225\pi = 5625\pi \approx 17{,}671.46 \text{ kN}\]
  2. Block Capacity Formulation:
    Block width: \(B = 4S + 1\)
    \[Q_{ug} = 20 \times 4B \times 15 = 1200B \text{ kN}\]
  3. Equate and Solve for \(B\):
    \[1200B = 17{,}671.46 \implies B = 14.726 \text{ m}\]
  4. Solve for \(S/D\):
    \[4S + 1 = 14.726 \implies S = 3.432 \text{ m}\]
    \[S/D = 3.432 / 1 = 3.43\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.4  |  Accepted key range: 3.2 to 3.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A shallow strip footing of width 2 m is embedded at a depth of 1.5 m below the ground surface in a homogeneous pure clay with an angle of internal friction zero. Consider unit weight of soil as 20 kN/m³ and undrained cohesion of soil as 20 kN/m².

Due to rise of ground water table from far below the founding depth to the ground surface in monsoon season, the magnitude of percentage change in the net ultimate bearing capacity as per Terzaghi’s theory is _______
(rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Strip footing: \(B = 2\) m, \(D_f = 1.5\) m
    • Pure clay: \(\phi = 0\), \(c_u = 20\) kN/m²
    • Unit weight: \(\gamma = 20\) kN/m³
    • Initial state: Water table far below foundation.
    • Final state: Water table rises to ground surface.
  • Aim: Magnitude of percentage change in the net ultimate bearing capacity as per Terzaghi's theory.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Terzaghi's Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
    \[q_u = c_u N_c + \gamma_1 D_f N_q + 0.5\,\gamma_2\, B\, N_\gamma\]
  • For Pure Clay (\(\phi = 0\)): \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1\), \(N_\gamma = 0\).
    \[q_u = c_u N_c + \gamma_1 D_f\]
  • Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
    \[q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma_1 D_f = c_u N_c\]
    This is completely independent of soil unit weight and water table position.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Net Capacity:
    \[q_{nu(\text{initial})} = c_u \times N_c = 20 \times 5.7 = 114 \text{ kPa}\]
  2. Final Net Capacity (water table at surface):
    \[q_{nu(\text{final})} = c_u \times N_c = 20 \times 5.7 = 114 \text{ kPa}\]
    (The \(N_\gamma\) term is zero and the \(N_q\) surcharge cancels exactly in the net calculation.)
  3. Percentage Change:
    \[\% \text{ Change} = \dfrac{114 - 114}{114} \times 100 = 0\%\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.00%  |  Accepted key range: 0.00 to 0.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Based on the Casagrande's plasticity chart, plasticity index (in %) of inorganic clays having a liquid limit of 40 %, ranges between
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Classification

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Soil type: Inorganic clay
    • Liquid Limit (\(LL\)) \(= 40\%\)
  • Aim: Find the permissible range for the Plasticity Index (\(PI\)) based on Casagrande's plasticity chart.

3. Core Concepts:

Casagrande's Plasticity Chart (IS 1498): Used to classify fine-grained soils.

  • A-line (lower boundary for clays): \(PI_A = 0.73(LL - 20)\)
  • U-line (empirical upper boundary for all natural soils): \(PI_U = 0.9(LL - 8)\)

For a soil to be classified as an inorganic clay, its properties must plot above the A-line and below the U-line.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute \(LL = 40\%\) into the A-line equation to find the lower bound.
  2. Substitute \(LL = 40\%\) into the U-line equation to find the upper bound.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Lower Bound (A-line):\[PI_{lower} = 0.73(40 - 20) = 0.73 \times 20 = 14.6\% \]
  2. Upper Bound (U-line):\[PI_{upper} = 0.9(40 - 8) = 0.9 \times 32 = 28.8\% \]

Conclusion: The Plasticity Index must lie between \(14.6\%\) and \(28.8\%\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14.6 and 28.8 | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Information related to foundation design is provided in table below.

Column 1Column 2
(I) Converse-Labarre formula(P) Pile capacity from dynamic formula
(II) Hiley formula(Q) Pile group efficiency
(III) Newmark’s influence chart(R) Bearing capacity factor of saturated clay
(IV) Skempton’s equation(S) Increase in vertical stress below footing

Option giving the CORRECT match between Column 1 and Column 2 is:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Four design theories/tools (Column 1) to be matched with their corresponding applications (Column 2).
  • Aim: Select the correct matching sequence.

3. Core Concepts:

  • (I) Converse-Labarre formula: An empirical relationship used in deep foundations to determine the pile group efficiency based on the spacing and arrangement of piles.
  • (II) Hiley formula: A dynamic pile driving equation used to estimate the load-bearing capacity of a single driven pile based on the hammer's energy and pile penetration blow counts.
  • (III) Newmark's influence chart: A graphical tool based on Boussinesq's theory used to evaluate the increase in vertical stress at any depth beneath a loaded area of any arbitrary shape.
  • (IV) Skempton's equation: A formulation used to determine the bearing capacity factor (\(N_c\)) for shallow foundations on saturated cohesive soils (pure clays under undrained \(\phi_u = 0\) conditions).

4. Solution Method:

  • (I) Converse-Labarre → (Q) Pile group efficiency
  • (II) Hiley → (P) Pile capacity from dynamic formula
  • (III) Newmark → (S) Increase in vertical stress below footing
  • (IV) Skempton → (R) Bearing capacity factor of saturated clay

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Matching logically yields: (I) – (Q); (II) – (P); (III) – (S); (IV) – (R).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: (I) – (Q); (II) – (P); (III) – (S); (IV) – (R) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A fully saturated sandy soil deposit has water content 20 % and specific gravity 2.65.
The critical hydraulic gradient for seepage through the soil to create the quicksand condition is ________________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Fully saturated sandy soil: Degree of Saturation \(S = 1\) (100%)
    • Water content \(w = 20\% = 0.20\)
    • Specific gravity \(G_s = 2.65\)
  • Aim: Calculate the critical hydraulic gradient (\(i_c\)) rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Volumetric phase relation: \(S \cdot e = w \cdot G_s\)
  • Critical Hydraulic Gradient (\(i_c\)): The gradient at which effective stress becomes zero (quicksand condition): \[i_c = \dfrac{G_s - 1}{1 + e} \]

4. Solution Method:

Derive the void ratio (\(e\)) from the saturation phase equation, then substitute into the critical hydraulic gradient formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Solve for void ratio (\(e\)):\[1 \cdot e = 0.20 \times 2.65 \implies e = 0.53 \]
  2. Calculate \(i_c\):\[i_c = \dfrac{2.65 - 1}{1 + 0.53} = \dfrac{1.65}{1.53} = 1.07843\ldots \approx 1.08 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.08 | Accepted key range: 1.00 to 1.15

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A shallow footing is subjected to a vertical load. Within the elastic limit of the underlying soil, the TRUE statement(s) is/are:
options: Vertical displacement below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
Vertical contact pressure below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
Vertical displacement below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
Vertical contact pressure below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Vertical displacement below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
structuredOptions.html: Vertical displacement below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Vertical contact pressure below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
structuredOptions.html: Vertical contact pressure below a rigid shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Vertical displacement below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
structuredOptions.html: Vertical displacement below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Vertical contact pressure below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.
structuredOptions.html: Vertical contact pressure below a flexible shallow footing is uniform in clay as well as sand.

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Shallow footing subjected to vertical load on soil within elastic limits.
  • Aim: Identify the TRUE statements regarding displacement and contact pressure for rigid and flexible footings.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rigid Footing: Does not bend. The vertical displacement (settlement) is strictly uniform across the entire base for both clay and sand. Contact pressure is non-uniform (max at edges in clay, max at center in sand).
  • Flexible Footing: Bends to accommodate soil resistance but exerts a uniform vertical contact pressure across the entire base. Displacement is non-uniform (max at center in clay, max at edges in sand).

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate each statement against fundamental definitions:

  • (A) Vertical displacement below rigid footing is uniform → TRUE (definition of rigid)
  • (B) Vertical contact pressure below rigid footing is uniform → FALSE
  • (C) Vertical displacement below flexible footing is uniform → FALSE
  • (D) Vertical contact pressure below flexible footing is uniform → TRUE (definition of flexible)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • For an infinitely rigid footing: \(\Delta_{\text{edge}} = \Delta_{\text{center}}\) → Statement A is satisfied.
  • For a perfectly flexible footing (e.g., an oil tank on soil): stress transmitted \(= q = Q/A\) uniformly → Statement D is satisfied.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Statements (A) and (D) | Correct options: A; D

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
For a clayey soil stratum, the time required for degree of consolidation from 25 % to 50 % is 30 days.
The total time (in days) required for 90 % degree of consolidation of the same soil stratum is ______ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Time for consolidation from 25% to 50%: \(\Delta t = 30\text{ days}\)
    • Soil properties \(c_v\) and \(H\) are constant.
  • Aim: Determine the total time to reach 90% consolidation (\(t_{90}\)) in days.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Time Factor: \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v t}{H^2} \implies t \propto T_v\)
  • For \(U \le 60\%\): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4} U^2\)  (\(U\) in decimals)
  • For \(U > 60\%\): \(T_v = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - U\%)\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(T_v\) for \(U = 25\%\) and \(U = 50\%\).
  2. Deduce the constant \(c_v/H^2\) using \(\Delta t = 30\) days.
  3. Calculate \(T_v\) for \(U = 90\%\).
  4. Compute the total time \(t_{90}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Time Factors for 25% and 50%:\[T_{v,25} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.25)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{64} \approx 0.04909 \]\[T_{v,50} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.50)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{16} \approx 0.19635 \]\[\Delta T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{\pi}{64} = \dfrac{3\pi}{64} \approx 0.14726 \]
  2. Deduce Constant \(c_v/H^2\):\[\dfrac{c_v}{H^2} = \dfrac{\Delta T_v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{3\pi/64}{30} = \dfrac{\pi}{640}\text{ days}^{-1} \]
  3. Time Factor for 90%:\[T_{v,90} = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - 90) = 1.781 - 0.933(1) = 0.848 \]
  4. Total Time:\[t_{90} = \dfrac{T_{v,90}}{c_v/H^2} = \dfrac{0.848}{\pi/640} = \dfrac{0.848 \times 640}{\pi} = \dfrac{542.72}{3.14159} \approx 172.75\text{ days} \approx 173\text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 173 days | Accepted key range: 170 to 174

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The ultimate bearing capacity of a 1 m wide strip footing is 532.80 kPa, when it is embedded at 1 m depth in dry cohesionless soil. The soil has a unit weight of 18 kN/m³. The ultimate bearing capacity is 864 kPa when the depth of embedment becomes 2 m.
Neglecting the effect of the depth factor, the bearing capacity factor Nq is ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Strip footing width: \(B = 1\text{ m}\); Dry cohesionless soil: \(c = 0\)
    • Unit weight: \(\gamma = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Case 1: \(D_{f1} = 1\text{ m}\), \(q_{u1} = 532.80\text{ kPa}\)
    • Case 2: \(D_{f2} = 2\text{ m}\), \(q_{u2} = 864\text{ kPa}\)
    • Depth factors neglected.
  • Aim: Calculate the bearing capacity factor \(N_q\).

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity for strip footing on cohesionless soil (\(c = 0\)):\[q_u = \gamma D_f N_q + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate two equations for the two depth cases.
  2. Subtract to eliminate \(N_\gamma\) and isolate \(N_q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Case 1 (\(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)):\[532.80 = 18(1)N_q + 0.5(18)(1)N_\gamma = 18N_q + 9N_\gamma \quad \cdots (1) \]
  2. Case 2 (\(D_f = 2\text{ m}\)):\[864 = 18(2)N_q + 0.5(18)(1)N_\gamma = 36N_q + 9N_\gamma \quad \cdots (2) \]
  3. Subtract Eq. (1) from Eq. (2):\[864 - 532.80 = 18N_q \]\[331.20 = 18N_q \implies N_q = \dfrac{331.20}{18} = 18.4 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(N_q = 18.4\) | Accepted key range: 18.2 to 18.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A building is proposed in an area having thick deposit of silty clay. The water table is at the ground surface. The saturated unit weight of soil is 18 kN/m³ and unit weight of water is 10 kN/m³. The maximum vertical load (P) on a column of the proposed building is 2000 kN.
Consider \( \sigma_z \le 0.1 \sigma'_v \) for computation of the minimum depth of soil exploration.
\( \sigma'_v \) is the effective vertical overburden stress. \( \sigma_z \) is the increase in the vertical stress at depth Z below load P as per the Boussinesq's stress theory.
Based on above, the minimum depth (in m) of soil exploration required for the foundation design is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Exploration & Stresses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Saturated unit weight: \(\gamma_{\text{sat}} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\) (water table at ground level)
    • Point vertical load: \(P = 2000\text{ kN}\)
    • Condition: \(\sigma_z \le 0.1\,\sigma'_v\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the minimum soil exploration depth \(z\) in meters directly beneath the column.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Effective vertical stress: \(\sigma'_v = \gamma' \cdot z = (\gamma_{\text{sat}} - \gamma_w) \cdot z\)
  • Boussinesq's vertical stress (directly below load, \(r = 0\)):\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi z^2} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine effective unit weight \(\gamma'\).
  2. Write expressions for \(\sigma'_v\) and \(\sigma_z\) in terms of \(z\).
  3. Equate \(\sigma_z = 0.1\,\sigma'_v\) and solve for \(z\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Stresses:\[\gamma' = 18 - 10 = 8\text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\sigma'_v = 8z \quad (\text{kN/m}^2) \]\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3 \times 2000}{2\pi z^2} = \dfrac{3000}{\pi z^2} \quad (\text{kN/m}^2) \]
  2. Apply Threshold Condition:\[\dfrac{3000}{\pi z^2} = 0.1 \times 8z = 0.8z \]\[z^3 = \dfrac{3000}{0.8\pi} = \dfrac{3750}{\pi} = 1193.66 \]\[ z = \sqrt[3]{1193.66} \approx 10.61\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10.61 m | Accepted key range: 10.00 to 11.20

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A soil sample has following properties:
Natural water content = 30 %
Plasticity index = 40 %
Liquidity index = 50 %
The estimated plastic limit (in %) of the soil is ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Index Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Natural water content: \(w_n = 30\%\)
    • Plasticity index: \(I_p = 40\%\)
    • Liquidity index: \(I_L = 50\% = 0.50\)
  • Aim: Estimate the plastic limit (\(w_p\)) of the soil.

3. Core Concepts:

Liquidity Index:\[I_L = \dfrac{w_n - w_p}{I_p} \]where \(w_p\) is the plastic limit and \(I_p\) is the plasticity index.

4. Solution Method:

Substitute known values into the liquidity index formula and solve for the single unknown \(w_p\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the equation:\[0.50 = \dfrac{30 - w_p}{40} \]
  2. Solve algebraically:\[0.50 \times 40 = 30 - w_p \]\[20 = 30 - w_p \]\[w_p = 30 - 20 = 10\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(w_p = 10.0\%\) | Accepted key range: 10.0 to 10.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q17
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The results of a consolidated drained triaxial test on a normally consolidated clay are shown in the figure. The angle of internal friction is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soils

Taxonomy and Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: 3. Application
  • Given Data:
    Minor principal stress (cell pressure), \( \sigma_3 = 50 \text{ kPa} \)
    Major principal stress at failure, \( \sigma_1 = 100 \text{ kPa} \)
    Soil Type: Normally consolidated (NC) clay
  • Aim: Determine the angle of internal friction (\(\phi\)) of the soil sample.

Core Concepts

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: Defines the shear strength of soil in terms of effective stresses.

Normally Consolidated (NC) Clay: For an NC clay subjected to a consolidated drained (CD) test, the effective cohesion intercept is zero (\(c' = 0 \text{ kPa}\)). The strength envelope passes through the origin.

Principal Stress Relationship: The general relationship between major and minor principal stresses at failure is given by:
\[\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 \tan^2\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) + 2c \tan\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \]
For a cohesionless soil or NC clay (\(c=0\)), this simplifies directly to the geometric property of the Mohr circle touching the failure envelope:
\[\sin \phi = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3} \]

Solution Method

  • Identify the principal stresses from the provided Mohr circle diagram.
  • Apply the simplified principal stress relationship for \(c=0\) soils to solve for \(\sin \phi\).
  • Take the inverse sine to find the angle \(\phi\).

Common Pitfall: Assuming a non-zero cohesion for a normally consolidated clay. Always remember CD tests on true NC clays yield \(c' = 0\).

Step-by-Step Execution

  1. Extract values from diagram: The Mohr circle intersects the normal stress (\(\sigma\)) axis at \(50 \text{ kPa}\) and \(100 \text{ kPa}\). Thus:
    \(\sigma_3 = 50 \text{ kPa}\)
    \(\sigma_1 = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
  2. Establish cohesion: Since the soil is a normally consolidated clay, effective cohesion \(c = 0 \text{ kPa}\).
  3. Apply standard relationship:
    \[\sin \phi = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3} \]
  4. Substitute the stress values:
    \[\sin \phi = \dfrac{100 \text{ kPa} - 50 \text{ kPa}}{100 \text{ kPa} + 50 \text{ kPa}} \]
    \[\sin \phi = \dfrac{50}{150} \]
    \[\sin \phi = \dfrac{1}{3} \]
  5. Solve for \(\phi\):
    \[\phi = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \]

Validation & Error Handling:
Sanity Check: The calculated angle evaluates to approximately \(19.47^\circ\). This is a highly realistic effective friction angle for a normally consolidated clay deposit. \(\sin \phi \le 1\) is satisfied.

Final Answer

Final Answer: \(\sin^{-1}(1/3)\) | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The standard plasticity chart for the classification of a fine-grained soil is shown in the figure. As per the Indian standard soil classification system, X represents
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Classification

Taxonomy and Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: 2. Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    Point \(X\) plotted on the standard IS plasticity chart.
    Point \(X\) is located above the A-line.
    Point \(X\) corresponds to a Liquid Limit (\(w_L\)) strictly greater than \(50\%\).
  • Aim: Identify the Indian Standard Soil Classification System symbol/name for point X.

Core Concepts

IS 1498 (1970): Indian Standard Classification and Identification of Soils for General Engineering Purposes.

A-Line Equation: \(I_p = 0.73(w_L - 20)\). It separates clays from silts and organic soils.

  • Points Above A-Line: Inorganic Clays (Prefix: C)
  • Points Below A-Line: Inorganic Silts (Prefix: M) or Organic Soils (Prefix: O)

Liquid Limit Boundaries: Dictates the compressibility/plasticity suffix of the soil.

  • \(w_L < 35\%\): Low plasticity (Suffix: L)
  • \(35\% \le w_L \le 50\%\): Medium/Intermediate plasticity (Suffix: I)
  • \(w_L > 50\%\): High plasticity / High Compressibility (Suffix: H)

Solution Method

  1. Read the \(X\)-coordinate (Liquid Limit) zone for point X on the given chart.
  2. Determine the suffix (L, I, or H) based on standard boundaries.
  3. Read the position relative to the A-line (above or below).
  4. Determine the prefix (C or M/O).
  5. Combine to state the full classification.

Common Pitfall: Confusing the A-line equation or the \(35\%\) and \(50\%\) boundary lines.

Step-by-Step Execution

  1. Analyze Liquid Limit (\(w_L\)): On the x-axis, the chart marks boundaries at \(20\%\), \(35\%\), and \(50\%\). Point \(X\) is located to the right of the \(50\%\) mark.
    Therefore, \(w_L > 50\%\).
    This indicates High Plasticity (suffix H).
  2. Analyze Plasticity Index (\(I_p\)): Point \(X\) is plotted visually above the A-Line.
    Therefore, the soil exhibits clay-like behavior.
    This indicates an Inorganic Clay (prefix C).
  3. Combine Symbols: Combining C and H gives CH, which stands for Inorganic Clay with High Plasticity.

Validation & Error Handling:
Sanity Check: The options correlate perfectly with standard IS 1498 taxonomy. Option C directly maps to the 'CH' classification derived from our visual and theoretical analysis.

Final Answer

Final Answer: inorganic clay with high plasticity | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q38
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In an oedometer apparatus a specimen of fully saturated clay has been consolidated under a vertical pressure of 100 kPa and is at equilibrium state. Immediately on increasing the vertical pressure to 150 kPa, the effective stress σ' and excess pore water pressure Δu will be
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation of Soils

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    Initial vertical pressure (equilibrium): \(\sigma_1 = 100\) kPa
    Vertical pressure immediately increased to: \(\sigma_2 = 150\) kPa
    Soil: Fully saturated clay.
  • Aim: Determine effective stress \(\sigma'\) and excess pore water pressure \(\Delta u\) immediately after the load increase.

Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Principle of Effective Stress:

\[\sigma = \sigma' + u \]

Spring Analogy at \(t = 0\): Water is practically incompressible compared to the soil skeleton. In a fully saturated soil, immediately after an additional load \(\Delta\sigma\) is applied, water cannot drain instantaneously due to low permeability. Therefore, the entire load increment is initially carried by pore water: \(\Delta u = \Delta\sigma\). Effective stress does not change at \(t = 0\).

Solution:

  1. Initial Equilibrium State:
    Total stress \(\sigma_1 = 100\) kPa
    At equilibrium, excess pore pressure = 0
    ∴ Initial effective stress \(\sigma_1' = 100\) kPa
  2. Stress Increment:
    New total stress \(\sigma_2 = 150\) kPa
    Increment \(\Delta\sigma = 150 - 100 = 50\) kPa
  3. State Immediately After Loading (\(t = 0\)):
    Entire increment taken by pore water: \(\Delta u = \Delta\sigma = 50\) kPa
    Effective stress remains unchanged: \(\sigma' = \sigma_1' = 100\) kPa

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\sigma' = 100\) kPa, \(\Delta u = 50\) kPa | Option: B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A cut slope is made in a silty clay soil for a new road project, as shown in the figure. The locations of ground water table (GWT) and potential failure surface are shown in the figure. After the cut is made, the excess pore water pressure is fully dissipated, and the shear stress at the point A is 60 kN/m². The factor of safety at the point A for long-term stability is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
Note:
Shear strength properties of silty clay: c' = 15 kN/m², φ' = 15°, and cu = 75 kN/m²
Unit weight of soil above the GWT (γ) = 19 kN/m³
Unit weight of soil below the GWT (γsat) = 20 kN/m³
Unit weight of water (γw) = 9.81 kN/m³
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability / Factor of Safety

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Depth of GWT from surface = 5 m
    Depth of Point A below GWT = 6.5 m
    \(\gamma\) (above GWT) = 19 kN/m³
    \(\gamma_{sat}\) (below GWT) = 20 kN/m³
    \(\gamma_w\) = 9.81 kN/m³
    \(c' = 15\) kN/m², \(\phi' = 15°\)
    Applied shear stress \(\tau = 60\) kN/m²
    Condition: Long-term (excess pore pressure dissipated)
  • Aim: Determine the Factor of Safety (FOS) at Point A, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Effective Stress: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: \(s = c' + \sigma' \tan\phi'\)

Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{s}{\tau}\)

Solution:

  1. Total Vertical Stress at A:
    \[\sigma = (19 \times 5) + (20 \times 6.5) = 95 + 130 = 225 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Pore Water Pressure at A:
    \[u = \gamma_w \times h_2 = 9.81 \times 6.5 = 63.765 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Effective Vertical Stress:
    \[\sigma' = 225 - 63.765 = 161.235 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  4. Available Shear Strength:
    \[s = 15 + 161.235 \times \tan(15°) = 15 + 161.235 \times 0.26795 = 15 + 43.203 = 58.203 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  5. Factor of Safety:
    \[FOS = \dfrac{58.203}{60} = 0.97005 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.97 | Official Key Range: 0.96 to 0.98

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 6 m × 6 m square footing constructed in clay is subjected to a vertical load of 2500 kN at its centre. The base of the footing is 2 m below the ground surface, as shown in the figure. The footing is made of 2 m thick concrete. The ground water table is at a great depth. Considering Terzaghi’s bearing capacity theory, the factor of safety of footing against the bearing capacity failure is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
Note:
Unit weight of concrete = 24 kN/m³
Properties of clay: c = 50 kN/m², φ = 0°, and γ = 19 kN/m³
For φ = 0°: Nc = 5.7, Nq = 1, Nγ = 0
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations / Bearing Capacity

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Square footing: \(6 \times 6\) m, Depth \(D_f = 2\) m
    Applied vertical load = 2500 kN, Concrete pad thickness = 2 m
    \(\gamma_{conc} = 24\) kN/m³, \(\gamma_{clay} = 19\) kN/m³
    \(c = 50\) kN/m², \(\phi = 0°\)
    Terzaghi factors: \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1\), \(N_\gamma = 0\)
  • Aim: Factor of safety against bearing capacity failure, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity (Square Footing):

\[q_u = 1.3cN_c + qN_q + 0.4\gamma B N_\gamma \]

Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity: \(q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f\)

Net Applied Pressure: \(q_{net} = q_{gross} - \gamma D_f\)

Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{q_{nu}}{q_{net}}\)

Solution:

  1. Overburden pressure: \(q = \gamma D_f = 19 \times 2 = 38\) kPa
  2. Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(\phi = 0°\), so \(N_\gamma = 0\)):
    \[q_u = 1.3 \times 50 \times 5.7 + 38 \times 1 = 370.5 + 38 = 408.5 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity:
    \[q_{nu} = 408.5 - 38 = 370.5 \text{ kPa} \]
  4. Gross Applied Pressure:
    Base area \(A = 36\) m²
    Weight of concrete footing \(= 36 \times 2 \times 24 = 1728\) kN
    Total load \(= 2500 + 1728 = 4228\) kN
    \[q_{gross} = \dfrac{4228}{36} = 117.44 \text{ kPa} \]
  5. Net Applied Pressure:
    \[q_{net} = 117.44 - 38 = 79.44 \text{ kPa} \]
  6. Factor of Safety:
    \[FOS = \dfrac{370.5}{79.44} = 4.663 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.66 | Official Key Range: 4.62 to 4.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A clayey soil has a moisture content of 18%, a specific gravity of soil solids of 2.74, and a degree of saturation of 65%. The soil soaks up water during a rain event, and the degree of saturation increases to 85.2%. The change of the volume during the soaking is negligible. The new moisture content (in %) of the soil will be _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Phase Relations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Initial moisture content \(w_1 = 18\%\)
    Specific gravity \(G = 2.74\)
    Initial degree of saturation \(S_1 = 65\%\)
    Final degree of saturation \(S_2 = 85.2\%\)
    Condition: Negligible volume change (void ratio \(e\) remains constant)
  • Aim: Calculate the new moisture content \(w_2\) in %, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Fundamental Phase Equation:

\[S \cdot e = w \cdot G \]

This links saturation \(S\), void ratio \(e\), moisture content \(w\), and specific gravity \(G\). Since volume change is negligible, \(e\) remains constant and serves as the bridge between initial and final states.

Solution:

  1. Determine initial void ratio \(e\):
    \[e = \dfrac{w_1 \cdot G}{S_1} = \dfrac{0.18 \times 2.74}{0.65} = \dfrac{0.4932}{0.65} = 0.75877 \]
  2. Calculate new moisture content \(w_2\):
    \[w_2 = \dfrac{S_2 \cdot e}{G} = \dfrac{0.852 \times 0.75877}{2.74} = \dfrac{0.64647}{2.74} = 0.23594 \]
    \[w_2 = 0.23594 \times 100 = 23.59\% \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 23.59% | Official Key Range: 23.30 to 23.70

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A single pile with 450 mm diameter has been driven into a homogeneous clay layer, which has an undrained cohesion (cᵤ) of 20 kPa and unit weight of 18 kN/m³. The ground water table is found to be at the surface of the clay layer. The adhesion factor (α) of the soil is 0.95 and bearing capacity factor (N꜀) is 9. The pile is supporting a column load of 144 kN with a factor of safety of 3.0 against ultimate axial pile capacity in compression.
The required embedment depth of the pile (in m) is _______________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations / Pile Capacity

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Pile diameter \(D = 0.45\) m, Undrained cohesion \(c_u = 20\) kN/m²
    Unit weight of clay \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³ (distractor — see note below)
    GWT at surface, Adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.95\), \(N_c = 9\)
    Safe load \(Q_{safe} = 144\) kN, FOS = 3.0
  • Aim: Calculate the required embedment depth \(L\) in meters, rounded to nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

Ultimate Pile Capacity in Clay (\(\alpha\)-method):

\[Q_u = Q_b + Q_s \]

where \(Q_b = c_u \cdot N_c \cdot A_b\) (end bearing) and \(Q_s = \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot A_s\) (skin friction).

Note: Since this is an undrained (\(\phi = 0\)) cohesive analysis, the \(\gamma\) and GWT data are distractors — the overburden term vanishes in the standard \(\alpha\)-method.

Solution:

  1. Ultimate load required:
    \[Q_u = Q_{safe} \times FOS = 144 \times 3.0 = 432 \text{ kN} \]
  2. Base area and end bearing capacity:
    \[A_b = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} = \dfrac{\pi (0.45)^2}{4} = 0.159 \text{ m}^2 \]
    \[Q_b = 20 \times 9 \times 0.159 = 28.62 \text{ kN} \]
  3. Skin friction in terms of \(L\):
    \[A_s = \pi D L = \pi \times 0.45 \times L = 1.4137L \text{ m}^2 \]
    \[Q_s = 0.95 \times 20 \times 1.4137L = 26.86L \text{ kN} \]
  4. Solve for \(L\):
    \[432 = 28.62 + 26.86L \]
    \[26.86L = 403.38 \Rightarrow L = \dfrac{403.38}{26.86} = 15.01 \text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 m

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Two soils of permeabilities k₁ and k₂ are placed in a horizontal flow apparatus, as shown in the figure. For Soil 1, L₁ = 50 cm, and k₁ = 0.055 cm/s; for Soil 2, L₂ = 30 cm, and k₂ = 0.035 cm/s. The cross sectional area of the horizontal pipe is 100 cm², and the head difference (Δh) is 150 cm. The discharge (in cm³/s) through the soils is _______________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Permeability / Stratified Soils in Series

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Soil 1: \(L_1 = 50\) cm, \(k_1 = 0.055\) cm/s
    Soil 2: \(L_2 = 30\) cm, \(k_2 = 0.035\) cm/s
    Cross-sectional area \(A = 100\) cm², Head difference \(\Delta h = 150\) cm
  • Aim: Calculate discharge in cm³/s, rounded to 2 decimal places.

Core Concepts:

Equivalent Permeability (soils in series — flow perpendicular to bedding):

\[k_{eq} = \dfrac{L_{total}}{\dfrac{L_1}{k_1} + \dfrac{L_2}{k_2}} \]

Darcy's Law: \(Q = k_{eq} \cdot i \cdot A\), where \(i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L_{total}}\)

Solution:

  1. Total Length: \(L_{total} = 50 + 30 = 80\) cm
  2. Equivalent Permeability:
    \[k_{eq} = \dfrac{80}{\dfrac{50}{0.055} + \dfrac{30}{0.035}} = \dfrac{80}{909.09 + 857.14} = \dfrac{80}{1766.23} = 0.04529 \text{ cm/s} \]
  3. Hydraulic Gradient:
    \[i = \dfrac{150}{80} = 1.875 \]
  4. Discharge:
    \[Q = 0.04529 \times 1.875 \times 100 = 8.49 \text{ cm}^3\text{/s} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.49 cm³/s | Acceptable Range: 8.44 to 8.56

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The most suitable test for measuring the permeability of clayey soils in the laboratory is _______.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Permeability (Laboratory Testing)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Clayey soil (low permeability, \(k\) typically \(< 10^{-7}~m/s\)).
  • Aim: Select the most suitable laboratory permeability test.

Core Concepts:

Darcy's Law: \(v = k\,i\), where \(v\) = discharge velocity, \(k\) = coefficient of permeability, \(i\) = hydraulic gradient.

  • Constant-head test (IS 2720 Part 17): Suitable for coarse-grained soils (\(k > 10^{-5}~m/s\)) — maintains steady head with measurable discharge.
  • Falling-head test (IS 2720 Part 17): Suitable for fine-grained soils (\(k < 10^{-5}~m/s\)) — measures time for head drop in standpipe, ideal for clays where discharge is too small for constant-head accuracy.
  • Pumping-out test: Field test only.
  • Hydrometer test: Used for particle size analysis (IS 2720 Part 4), not permeability.

Standard assumption: Laminar flow (Re < 1).

Solution:

  1. Clayey soils have very low \(k\) → constant-head test gives negligible measurable outflow.
  2. Falling-head test allows measurement of time for head drop in standpipe using the formula:
    \[k = \dfrac{2.303\, a\, L}{A\, t} \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{h_1}{h_2}\right)\]where \(a\) = standpipe area, \(L\) = sample length, \(A\) = sample cross-sectional area, \(t\) = elapsed time.
  3. Hence, most suitable test = Falling head test.

Final Answer:

Falling head test | Option(s): D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q24
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?
options: As the depth of the ground water table from the ground surface increases, the effective stress in the soil decreases.
Bulking of the moist sand is due to the capillary action in the sand.
The effective stress in a liquified soil is almost zero.
The earth pressure at any point in the soil, under all conditions, is always smaller than the vertical effective stress at that point.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: As the depth of the ground water table from the ground surface increases, the effective stress in the soil decreases.
structuredOptions.html: As the depth of the ground water table from the ground surface increases, the effective stress in the soil decreases.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Bulking of the moist sand is due to the capillary action in the sand.
structuredOptions.html: Bulking of the moist sand is due to the capillary action in the sand.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: The effective stress in a liquified soil is almost zero.
structuredOptions.html: The effective stress in a liquified soil is almost zero.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: The earth pressure at any point in the soil, under all conditions, is always smaller than the vertical effective stress at that point.
structuredOptions.html: The earth pressure at any point in the soil, under all conditions, is always smaller than the vertical effective stress at that point.

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Effective Stress & Earth Pressure (IS 1904)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Aim: Identify incorrect statements on soil stress behaviour.

Core Concepts:

  • Effective stress: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\) (Terzaghi). A deeper groundwater table (GWT) → lower pore pressure \(u\) at a given depth → higher \(\sigma'\).
  • Bulking: Capillary tension in moist sand (3–5% moisture) causes volume increase.
  • Liquefaction: Excess pore pressure \(u =\) total stress → \(\sigma' \approx 0\).
  • Earth pressure: \(\sigma_h = K\,\sigma_v'\); \(K_p > 1 > K_0 > K_a\) → horizontal stress is not always less than vertical effective stress (passive case: \(\sigma_h > \sigma_v'\)).

Common pitfall: Assuming earth pressure is always in the active condition.

Solution:

  1. Option (A): GWT depth ↑ → \(u\) ↓ → \(\sigma'\) ↑. Statement claims \(\sigma'\) decreases → incorrect.
  2. Option (B): Bulking caused by capillary tension in moist sand → correct.
  3. Option (C): Liquefied soil → \(\sigma' \approx 0\) → correct.
  4. Option (D): In passive case \(\sigma_h > \sigma_v'\) → claim that horizontal stress is always smaller → incorrect.

Final Answer:

Options A and D (incorrect statements) | Option(s): A; D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
From a flow-net diagram drawn under a concrete dam, following information are obtained: (i) The head difference between upstream and downstream side of the dam is 9 m. (ii) The total number of equipotential drops between upstream and downstream side of the dam is 10. (iii) The length of the field nearest to the toe of the dam in the downstream side is 1 m.
If the soil below the dam is having a saturated unit weight of 21 kN/m³ and unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³, then the factor of safety against the quick condition will be _______ (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage & Quick Condition (Flow Net)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Total head loss \(\Delta H = 9~m\), number of equipotential drops \(N_d = 10\), exit field length \(\Delta l = 1~m\), \(\gamma_{sat} = 21~kN/m^3\), \(\gamma_w = 9.81~kN/m^3\).
  • Aim: Factor of safety against quick condition, rounded to two decimal places.

Core Concepts:

  • Exit hydraulic gradient: \(i_e = \dfrac{\Delta H / N_d}{\Delta l}\)
  • Critical hydraulic gradient: \(i_{cr} = \dfrac{\gamma'}{\gamma_w} = \dfrac{\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w}{\gamma_w}\)
  • Factor of Safety: \(FS = \dfrac{i_{cr}}{i_e}\)

Solution:

  1. Head drop per equipotential: \(\Delta h = 9 / 10 = 0.9~m\)
  2. Exit hydraulic gradient: \(i_e = 0.9 / 1 = 0.9\)
  3. Submerged unit weight: \(\gamma' = 21 - 9.81 = 11.19~kN/m^3\)
  4. Critical gradient: \(i_{cr} = 11.19 / 9.81 \approx 1.1407\)
  5. Factor of Safety: \(FS = 1.1407 / 0.9 \approx \mathbf{1.27}\)

Final Answer:

1.27 | Option(s): 1.24 to 1.30

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 6 m thick clay stratum has drainage at both its top and bottom surface due to the presence of sand strata. The time to complete 50% consolidation is 2 years. The coefficient of volume change (m_v) is 1.51×10⁻³ m²/kN and unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³.
The coefficient of permeability (in m/year) is _______ (round off to three decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation (Terzaghi Theory)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Clay layer thickness \(H = 6~m\) (double drainage), time for 50% consolidation \(t_{50} = 2~years\), coefficient of volume compressibility \(m_v = 1.51 \times 10^{-3}~m^2/kN\), \(\gamma_w = 9.81~kN/m^3\).
  • Aim: Coefficient of permeability \(k\) in m/year, rounded to three decimal places.

Core Concepts:

  • Double drainage → drainage path \(H_{dr} = H/2 = 3~m\).
  • Time factor at \(U = 50\%\): \(T_v = 0.197\).
  • Coefficient of consolidation: \(C_v = \dfrac{T_v \cdot H_{dr}^2}{t}\)
  • Permeability: \(k = C_v \times m_v \times \gamma_w\)

Solution:

  1. Drainage path: \(H_{dr} = 6/2 = 3~m\)
  2. Coefficient of consolidation:
    \[C_v = \dfrac{0.197 \times (3)^2}{2} = \dfrac{0.197 \times 9}{2} = \dfrac{1.773}{2} = 0.8865~m^2/year\]
  3. \(m_v \times \gamma_w = 1.51 \times 10^{-3} \times 9.81 = 0.014813~m^{-1}\)
  4. Permeability:
    \[k = C_v \times m_v \times \gamma_w = 0.8865 \times 0.014813 \approx 0.01313~m/year\]
  5. Rounded to three decimal places: 0.013 m/year.

Final Answer:

0.013 m/year | Option(s): 0.010 to 0.015

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
For a partially saturated soil deposit at a construction site, water content (w) is 15%, degree of saturation (S) is 67%, void ratio (e) is 0.6 and specific gravity of solids in the soil (Gs) is 2.67. Consider unit weight of water as 9.81 kN/m³.
To fully saturate 5 m³ of this soil, the required weight of water (in kN) will be _______ (round off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Phase Relationships

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Total Volume \(V = 5~m^3\), Water Content \(w = 15\%\), Degree of Saturation \(S = 67\%\), Void Ratio \(e = 0.6\), Specific Gravity \(G_s = 2.67\), \(\gamma_w = 9.81~kN/m^3\).
  • Aim: Required weight of water (kN) to fully saturate the soil deposit, rounded to the nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

  • Total volume: \(V = V_s + V_v\)
  • Volume of solids: \(V_s = \dfrac{V}{1+e}\)
  • Degree of saturation: \(S = \dfrac{V_w}{V_v}\)
  • Volume of air voids: \(V_a = V_v \times (1 - S)\)
  • To fully saturate: fill all air voids with water → \(W_{add} = V_a \times \gamma_w\)

Solution:

  1. Volume of solids: \(V_s = \dfrac{5}{1 + 0.6} = \dfrac{5}{1.6} = 3.125~m^3\)
  2. Total void volume: \(V_v = 5 - 3.125 = 1.875~m^3\)
  3. Volume of air voids: \(V_a = 1.875 \times (1 - 0.67) = 1.875 \times 0.33 = 0.61875~m^3\)
  4. Weight of water to be added:
    \[W_{add} = 0.61875 \times 9.81 = 6.07~kN \approx \mathbf{6}~kN\]

Final Answer:

6 kN | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q47

The shear strength parameters obtained from the consolidated-drained (CD) triaxial tests should be used to analyse rapid construction in clay.
Vane shear test is commonly used for determining in situ undrained strength of saturated clay soils.
In an unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial tests, the angle of internal friction (φ) is equal to zero.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: The unconfined compression test is a special case of the unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial tests.
structuredOptions.html: The unconfined compression test is a special case of the unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial tests.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: The shear strength parameters obtained from the consolidated-drained (CD) triaxial tests should be used to analyse rapid construction in clay.
structuredOptions.html: The shear strength parameters obtained from the consolidated-drained (CD) triaxial tests should be used to analyse rapid construction in clay.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Vane shear test is commonly used for determining in situ undrained strength of saturated clay soils.
structuredOptions.html: Vane shear test is commonly used for determining in situ undrained strength of saturated clay soils.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: In an unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial tests, the angle of internal friction (φ) is equal to zero.
structuredOptions.html: In an unconsolidated-undrained (UU) triaxial tests, the angle of internal friction (φ) is equal to zero.

questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Shear Strength of Soil

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Recall
  • Given Data: Statements regarding UU tests, CD tests, Vane shear tests, and the angle of internal friction.
  • Aim: Identify all correct statements.

Core Concepts:

  • Unconfined Compression Test (UCC): A special case of the UU triaxial test where confining pressure \(\sigma_3 = 0\).
  • CD Tests: Represent long-term drained stability. Rapid construction in saturated clay is modeled by UU tests (undrained conditions).
  • Vane Shear Test: Standard field test for in-situ undrained shear strength (\(c_u\)) of soft, saturated clays.
  • \(\phi = 0\) concept: In a truly undrained (UU) test on saturated clay, the total stress failure envelope is horizontal → \(\phi_u = 0\).

Solution:

  1. Statement (A): UCC has no lateral pressure, making it effectively a UU test with \(\sigma_3 = 0\) → Correct.
  2. Statement (B): Rapid construction prevents drainage — UU (not CD) parameters should be used → Incorrect.
  3. Statement (C): Vane shear is specifically designed for soft saturated clays where undisturbed sampling is difficult → Correct.
  4. Statement (D): In undrained (UU) conditions, increased total stress is carried by pore water → shear strength is constant regardless of cell pressure → \(\phi = 0\) → Correct.

Final Answer:

(A), (C), and (D) are correct | Option(s): A, C, D

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The bank of a canal has the profile shown in the figure. The material is a homogeneous clay with a bulk unit weight of 20 kN/m³, undrained cohesion of 30 kPa and it is fully saturated (φu = 0). For the trial slip circle shown, the area ABCDEA is 150 m² and the centroid is at P. A tension crack (DE) of 2.5 m deep was also observed. Assume unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³ and consider 1 m run of the bank for the analysis.
Considering the canal is empty and tension crack is completely filled with water, the factor of safety against slope failure of the bank is _______ (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Bulk unit weight of clay \(\gamma = 20~kN/m^3\), Undrained cohesion \(c_u = 30~kPa\), Fully saturated clay \(\phi_u = 0\), Area of slip circle wedge (ABCDEA) \(A = 150~m^2\), Depth of tension crack \(z_c = 2.5~m\), Unit weight of water \(\gamma_w = 9.81~kN/m^3\), Radius of slip circle \(R = 14~m\), Arc angle \(\theta = 80^{\circ}\), Lever arm of wedge weight from center of rotation \(x = 2.5~m\), Vertical lever arm of water pressure in crack from center of rotation \(y = 7.5~m\).
  • Aim: Calculate the factor of safety against slope failure considering an empty canal and a completely water-filled tension crack.

Core Concepts:

Swedish Circle Method (\(\phi_u = 0\) analysis): Evaluates stability by comparing the resisting moments along the slip surface against the driving moments.

  • Driving Moments (\(M_D\)): Caused by the weight of the soil wedge and the hydrostatic force acting horizontally within the tension crack.
  • Resisting Moments (\(M_R\)): Provided entirely by the undrained cohesion (\(c_u\)) acting along the length of the slip arc.

Key Formulas:

  • Weight of wedge: \(W = \text{Area} \times \gamma \times 1~m\)
  • Hydrostatic force in crack: \(P_w = \dfrac{1}{2} \gamma_w z_c^2\)
  • Arc Length: \(L = R \times \theta_{radians}\)
  • Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_D}\)

Pitfall to avoid: Do not forget to convert the arc angle from degrees to radians before calculating arc length.

Solution:

  1. Calculate Driving Forces and Moments:
    Weight of the soil mass: \(W = A \times \gamma = 150~m^2 \times 20~kN/m^3 = 3000~kN/m\)
    Moment due to soil weight: \(M_W = W \times x = 3000 \times 2.5 = 7500~kN\cdot m/m\)
    Hydrostatic force in tension crack: \(P_w = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.81 \times (2.5)^2 = 30.656~kN/m\)
    Moment due to water pressure: \(M_{Pw} = P_w \times y = 30.656 \times 7.5 = 229.92~kN\cdot m/m\)
    Total Driving Moment: \(M_D = 7500 + 229.92 = 7729.92~kN\cdot m/m\)
  2. Calculate Resisting Moment:
    Convert angle to radians: \(\theta = 80^{\circ} \times \left(\dfrac{\pi}{180}\right) = 1.3963~rad\)
    Length of slip arc: \(L = R \times \theta = 14 \times 1.3963 = 19.548~m\)
    Total Resisting Moment: \(M_R = c_u \times L \times R = 30 \times 19.548 \times 14 = 8210.16~kN\cdot m/m\)
  3. Calculate Factor of Safety:
    \[FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_D} = \dfrac{8210.16}{7729.92} = 1.062\]

Final Answer:

1.06 | Option(s): Official Key Range is 1.00 to 1.10

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A designer used plate load test to obtain the value of the bearing capacity factor Nγ. A circular plate of 1 m diameter was placed on the surface of a dry sand layer extending very deep beneath the ground. The unit weight of the sand is 16.66 kN/m³. The plate is loaded to failure at a pressure of 1500 kPa.
Considering Terzaghi's bearing capacity theory, the bearing capacity factor Nγ is _______ (round off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Plate diameter \(D = 1~m\), Condition: Surface of a dry sand layer (Depth of foundation \(D_f = 0\)), Unit weight of sand \(\gamma = 16.66~kN/m^3\), Failure pressure (Ultimate bearing capacity) \(q_u = 1500~kPa\).
  • Aim: Find Terzaghi's bearing capacity factor \(N_\gamma\) to the nearest integer.

Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity Theory: For a circular footing placed on the surface (\(D_f = 0\)) of dry sand (cohesion \(c = 0\)), the bearing capacity equation simplifies significantly:

\[q_u = 1.3\, c\, N_c + \gamma D_f N_q + 0.3\, \gamma\, D\, N_\gamma\]

Since \(c = 0\) (sand) and \(D_f = 0\) (surface loading), the first two terms vanish, giving the simplified equation:

\[q_u = 0.3\, \gamma\, D\, N_\gamma\]

Solution:

  1. Set up the simplified equation:
    \[1500~kPa = 0.3 \times \gamma \times D \times N_\gamma\]
  2. Substitute and solve:
    \[1500 = 0.3 \times 16.66 \times 1 \times N_\gamma\]\[1500 = 4.998 \times N_\gamma\]\[N_\gamma = \dfrac{1500}{4.998} = 300.12\]
  3. Round to nearest integer: \(N_\gamma \approx 300\)

Final Answer:

300 | Option(s): Official Key Range is 300 to 300

questions.title: GATE CE 2025 Set 2 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 4 × 4 group pile, with each pile 20 m long and 500 mm in diameter, is installed in a square pattern in a clayey soil, as shown in the figure. The average unconfined compressive strength of the soil is 100 kN/m², and the adhesion factor is 0.8. Neglect the bearing at the tip of the piles. For a group efficiency factor of 1.0, the centre to centre spacing (s) of the piles (in m) would be _______ (round off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: \(4 \times 4\) pile group (\(n = 16\) piles), Pile length \(L = 20~m\), Pile diameter \(d = 500~mm = 0.5~m\), Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS) \(= 100~kN/m^2\), Adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.8\), Group efficiency factor \(\eta_g = 1.0\), Condition: Neglect tip bearing (pure friction piles).
  • Aim: Determine the center-to-center spacing (\(s\)) of the piles.

Core Concepts:

Shear Strength of Clay: Undrained cohesion (\(c_u\)) is half of the Unconfined Compressive Strength (UCS).

Group Efficiency (\(\eta_g\)): The ratio of the ultimate capacity of the pile group to the sum of the ultimate capacities of the individual piles. An efficiency of 1.0 means the block failure capacity equals the sum of individual capacities.

Key Formulas (IS 2911):

  • Individual Pile Capacity: \(Q_{us} = \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot (\pi d L)\)
  • Block Failure Capacity: \(Q_{ug} = c_u \cdot (4BL)\), where \(B\) is the width of the pile group.
  • Group Width for an \(N \times N\) group: \(B = (N-1)s + d\)

Solution:

  1. Determine undrained cohesion:
    \[c_u = \dfrac{UCS}{2} = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50~kN/m^2\]
  2. Calculate individual pile capacity (\(Q_{us}\)):
    \[Q_{us} = 0.8 \times 50 \times (\pi \times 0.5 \times 20) = 40 \times 10\pi = 1256.64~kN\]Total capacity of 16 piles \(= 16 \times 1256.64 = 20106.19~kN\)
  3. Express group width (\(B\)) and block capacity (\(Q_{ug}\)):
    For a \(4 \times 4\) group: \(B = (4-1)s + d = 3s + 0.5\)
    \[Q_{ug} = c_u \times 4BL = 50 \times 4 \times (3s + 0.5) \times 20 = 4000(3s + 0.5)~kN\]
  4. Equate capacities (\(\eta_g = 1.0\)) and solve for \(s\):
    \[4000(3s + 0.5) = 20106.19\]\[3s + 0.5 = \dfrac{20106.19}{4000} = 5.0265~m\]\[3s = 4.5265~m\]\[s = 1.5088~m\]

Final Answer:

1.51 m | Option(s): Official Key Range is 1.50 to 1.52

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 2 m wide strip footing is founded at a depth of 1.5 m below the ground level in a homogeneous pure clay bed. The clay bed has unit cohesion of 40 kPa. Due to seasonal fluctuations of water table from peak summer to peak monsoon period, the net ultimate bearing capacity of the footing, as per Terzaghi’s theory, will
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Strip footing, \(B = 2\) m, \(D_f = 1.5\) m
    • Homogeneous pure clay: \(\phi = 0°\), \(c_u = 40\) kPa
    • Water table fluctuates seasonally (summer low → monsoon high)
  • Aim: Effect on net ultimate bearing capacity \(q_{net,ult}\) as per Terzaghi's theory.

Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Equation (strip footing):\[q_u = cN_c + \gamma D_f N_q + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma\]

For \(\phi = 0°\) (pure clay): \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1.0\), \(N_\gamma = 0\).

Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity:\[q_{net,ult} = q_u - \gamma D_f = cN_c + \gamma D_f(N_q - 1) + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma\]

Water table changes effective unit weight \(\gamma\), but for \(\phi = 0°\) the \(\gamma\) terms cancel exactly in the net expression. Reference: IS 6403 : 1981.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Terzaghi gross capacity:\[q_u = 5.7c + \gamma D_f \times 1 + 0\]

  2. Net capacity:\[q_{net,ult} = (5.7c + \gamma D_f) - \gamma D_f = 5.7c\]

  3. Substitute \(c = 40\) kPa:\[q_{net,ult} = 5.7 \times 40 = 228 \text{ kPa}\]

  4. The \(\gamma\) term (whether dry or submerged due to water table fluctuation) cancels completely. Therefore \(q_{net,ult}\) remains unchanged.

Common Pitfall: Using gross capacity or the general \(c\)-\(\phi\) equation without simplifying for \(\phi = 0°\).

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(q_{net,ult}\) will remain the same (228 kPa) | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Consider the statements P and Q.

P: Soil particles formed by mechanical weathering, and close to their origin are generally subrounded.

Q: Activity of the clay physically signifies its swell potential.


Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: Both P and Q are TRUE
P is TRUE and Q is FALSE
Both P and Q are FALSE
P is FALSE and Q is TRUE

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Both P and Q are TRUE
structuredOptions.html: Both P and Q are TRUE

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: P is TRUE and Q is FALSE
structuredOptions.html: P is TRUE and Q is FALSE

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Both P and Q are FALSE
structuredOptions.html: Both P and Q are FALSE

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: P is FALSE and Q is TRUE
structuredOptions.html: P is FALSE and Q is TRUE

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Origin & Properties of Soils

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Two statements P and Q on soil particle shape and clay activity.
  • Aim: Identify which statements are TRUE or FALSE.

Core Concepts:

  • Particle Shape from Weathering: Mechanical (physical) weathering near the parent rock produces angular to sub-angular particles (no abrasion). Subrounded/rounded shapes require fluvial or glacial transport and abrasion.
  • Activity of Clay: \(A = \dfrac{\text{Plasticity Index } (I_p)}{\% \text{ fines} < 2\,\mu\text{m}}\). High activity clays (e.g. montmorillonite, \(A > 1.25\)) exhibit high swell-shrink potential; low activity clays (e.g. kaolinite, \(A < 0.75\)) exhibit low swell.
  • Reference: IS 2720 (Part 5) : 1985.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Statement P: "Soil particles formed by mechanical weathering, and close to their origin, are generally subrounded."
    → FALSE. Near origin means no transport or abrasion → particles are angular. Subrounded shape requires significant transport.

  2. Statement Q: "Activity of the clay physically signifies its swell potential."
    → TRUE. Activity (Skempton's definition) directly correlates with swell-shrink potential.

Common Pitfall: Confusing mechanical vs. chemical weathering, or assuming transport is not needed for rounding.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: P is FALSE and Q is TRUE | Option(s): D

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q34
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: An embankment is constructed with soil by maintaining the degree of saturation as 75% during compaction. The specific gravity of soil is 2.68 and the moisture content is 17% during compaction. Consider the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³. The dry unit weight (in kN/m³) of the compacted soil is ________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Compaction / Unit Weights and Phase Relations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Degree of saturation \(S = 75\% = 0.75\)
    • Moisture content \(w = 17\% = 0.17\)
    • Specific gravity \(G = 2.68\)
    • Unit weight of water \(\gamma_w = 10\) kN/m³
  • Aim: Find dry unit weight \(\gamma_d\) of compacted soil in kN/m³.

Core Concepts:

Void ratio from phase relations:\[e = \dfrac{wG}{S}\]

Dry unit weight:\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1 + e}\]

Reference: IS 2720 (Part 7/8) for compaction tests.

Common Pitfall: Using \(S = 1\) (full saturation); confusing \(\gamma_d\) with bulk unit weight \(\gamma\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute void ratio:\[e = \dfrac{wG}{S} = \dfrac{0.17 \times 2.68}{0.75} = \dfrac{0.4556}{0.75} = 0.6075\]

  2. Compute dry unit weight:\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1+e} = \dfrac{2.68 \times 10}{1 + 0.6075} = \dfrac{26.8}{1.6075} \approx 16.67 \text{ kN/m}^3\]

Sanity check: \(e \approx 0.61\) is realistic for compacted soil; \(\gamma_d \approx 16.7\) kN/m³ is typical for silty/clayey soils.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 16.67 kN/m³

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A vertical smooth rigid retaining wall is supporting horizontal ground with dry cohesionless backfill having a friction angle of 30°. The inclinations of failure planes with respect to the major principal plane for Rankine’s active and passive earth pressure conditions, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theories

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Wall type: Vertical, smooth, rigid.
    • Backfill: Horizontal, dry, cohesionless.
    • Friction angle: \(\phi = 30^\circ\)
  • Aim: Find inclinations of failure planes with respect to the major principal plane for active and passive conditions.

Core Concepts:

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: The failure plane in a soil mass makes an angle of \(\theta = 45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\) with the direction of the major principal plane.

Active vs. Passive States: In the active state, the vertical stress (\(\sigma_v\)) is the major principal stress, so the major principal plane is horizontal. In the passive state, the horizontal stress (\(\sigma_h\)) is the major principal stress, so the major principal plane is vertical. However, the angle between the failure plane and the major principal plane is governed purely by \(\phi\) and remains mathematically the same in both cases.

Solution Method:

  1. Recognize that the angle between the failure plane and the major principal plane is governed purely by \(\phi\).
  2. Calculate the angle using the standard formula for both active and passive cases.

Step-by-Step Execution:

Active State:

\[\theta_{active} = 45^\circ + \dfrac{30^\circ}{2} = 60^\circ\]

Passive State:

\[\theta_{passive} = 45^\circ + \dfrac{30^\circ}{2} = 60^\circ\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(60^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) | Option(s): B
