questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties & Site Characterization

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Four theoretical statements regarding soil mechanics and site characterization.
  • Aim: Identify the strictly CORRECT statement(s).

Core Concepts & Solution Method:

Each statement is evaluated systematically based on standard geotechnical principles:

  • (A) Swell potential vs. Shrinkage limit: Highly expansive soils (like montmorillonite) have high liquid limits and high swell potentials, but characteristically low shrinkage limits. Therefore, as the shrinkage limit of a soil increases, its swell potential generally decreases. → Correct
  • (B) Critical Void Ratio: According to Critical State Soil Mechanics, regardless of whether a sand is initially dense (dilates) or loose (contracts), it will eventually shear towards a constant void ratio known as the critical void ratio at large strains. → Correct
  • (C) SPT-N Corrections: The standard IS 2131 sequence dictates applying the Overburden Correction (\(N_1\)) first, followed by the Dilatancy Correction (\(N_2\)) for water table effects in fine sands. The statement claims dilatancy is applied first. → Incorrect
  • (D) Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT): The depth of current penetration depends heavily on the array type used (e.g., Wenner, Schlumberger). For a Wenner array with spacing \(a\), the depth of investigation is approximately equal to \(a\), not half the spacing. → Incorrect

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Statements A and B are correct | Option(s): A, B

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The total primary consolidation settlement (\( S_c \)) of a building constructed on a 10 m thick saturated clay layer is estimated to be 50 mm. After 300 days of the construction of the building, primary consolidation settlement was reported as 10 mm. The additional time (in days) required to achieve 50% of \( S_c \) will be _____________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total primary consolidation, \(S_c = 50\) mm
    • Time elapsed, \(t_1 = 300\) days
    • Settlement at \(t_1\), \(S_1 = 10\) mm
  • Aim: Find the additional time required to reach 50% of the total consolidation settlement.

Core Concepts:

  • Degree of Consolidation (\(U\)): \(U = \dfrac{S_t}{S_c} \times 100\)
  • Time Factor (\(T_v\)): For \(U \le 60\%\): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4} U^2\)
  • Time-Settlement Relationship: Since \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v \cdot t}{d^2}\) and \(c_v\), \(d\) are constant, \(T_v \propto t\). Therefore \(t \propto U^2\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Degree of Consolidation (\(U_1\)):\[U_1 = \dfrac{S_1}{S_c} = \dfrac{10}{50} = 0.2 \text{ (20\%)}\]

  2. Target Degree of Consolidation: \(U_2 = 50\% = 0.5\)

  3. Calculate Total Time (\(t_2\)):
    Since both \(U_1, U_2 \le 0.6\), use the parabolic relation:\[\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \left(\dfrac{U_1}{U_2}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{0.2}{0.5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{25}\]\[t_2 = 300 \times \dfrac{25}{4} = 1875 \text{ days}\]

  4. Calculate Additional Time:\[\text{Additional Time} = t_2 - t_1 = 1875 - 300 = 1575 \text{ days}\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1575 days | Accepted key range: 1550 to 1600

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
An infinite slope is made up of cohesionless soil with seepage parallel to and up to the sloping surface. The angle of slope is 30° with respect to horizontal ground surface. The unit weights of the saturated soil and water are 20 kN/m³ and 10 kN/m³, respectively.

The minimum angle of shearing resistance of the soil (in degrees) for the critically stable condition of the slope is ____________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Slope angle, \(\beta = 30^\circ\)
    • Cohesionless soil (\(c' = 0\))
    • Seepage is parallel to and up to the sloping surface (full seepage)
    • \(\gamma_{sat} = 20\) kN/m³, \(\gamma_w = 10\) kN/m³
  • Aim: Minimum angle of shearing resistance (\(\phi'\)) for critically stable condition (FoS = 1).

Core Concepts:

Infinite Slope Stability: For cohesionless soils with seepage parallel to the surface, the Factor of Safety is reduced due to pore water pressure:\[FoS = \left(\dfrac{\gamma'}{\gamma_{sat}}\right) \dfrac{\tan \phi'}{\tan \beta}\]where \(\gamma'\) is the submerged unit weight.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(\gamma'\):\[\gamma' = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w = 20 - 10 = 10 \text{ kN/m}^3\]

  2. Apply FoS Formula with FoS = 1:\[1 = \left(\dfrac{10}{20}\right) \dfrac{\tan \phi'}{\tan 30^\circ} = 0.5 \times \dfrac{\tan \phi'}{1/\sqrt{3}}\]

  3. Solve for \(\phi'\):\[\tan \phi' = 2 \cdot \tan 30^\circ = 2 \times 0.57735 = 1.1547\]\[\phi' = \arctan(1.1547) = 49.106^\circ \approx 49^\circ\]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 49° | Accepted key range: 48 to 50

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A soil sample was consolidated at a cell pressure of 20 kPa and a back pressure of 10 kPa for 24 hours during a consolidated undrained (CU) triaxial test. The cell pressure was increased to 30 kPa on the next day and it resulted in the development of pore water pressure of 1 kPa. The soil sample failed when the axial stress was gradually increased to 50 kPa. The pore water pressure at failure was recorded as 21 kPa. The value of Skempton’s pore pressure parameter \( B \) for the soil sample is ___________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength (Triaxial Test)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Initial consolidation: Cell pressure \(\sigma_3 = 20\) kPa, Back pressure \(u_0 = 10\) kPa
    • B-check phase: Cell pressure increased to 30 kPa, pore water pressure developed \(\Delta u = 1\) kPa
    • Shear phase: Failed at axial stress = 50 kPa, final pore pressure \(u_f = 21\) kPa
  • Aim: Value of Skempton's pore pressure parameter B.

Core Concepts:

Skempton's Pore Pressure Equation:\[\Delta u = B \left[\Delta \sigma_3 + A (\Delta \sigma_1 - \Delta \sigma_3) \right]\]

Parameter B Phase: Parameter \(B\) is determined purely during the isotropic stress application phase (the B-check). Here \(\Delta \sigma_1 = \Delta \sigma_3\), so the equation simplifies to:\[B = \dfrac{\Delta u}{\Delta \sigma_3}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Stress Increment (B-check phase):\[\Delta \sigma_3 = 30 - 20 = 10 \text{ kPa}\]

  2. Identify Pore Pressure Increment:\[\Delta u = 1 \text{ kPa}\]

  3. Calculate B:\[B = \dfrac{\Delta u}{\Delta \sigma_3} = \dfrac{1}{10} = 0.10\]

Sanity Check: The official answer key accepts two ranges: 0.09–0.11 or 0.55–0.65. This reveals a common terminology ambiguity — some authors refer to the combined parameter \(\bar{A} = A \cdot B = \dfrac{\Delta u_{shear}}{\Delta \sigma_d}\) simply as "Skempton's parameter". Using shear phase data: \(\Delta u_{shear} = 21 - 10 = 11\) kPa and \(\Delta \sigma_d = 50 - 30 = 20\) kPa gives \(\bar{A} = \dfrac{11}{20} = 0.55\). Strictly speaking however, \(B = 0.10\) based on the explicit B-check phase description.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.10 | Accepted key range: 0.09 to 0.11 OR 0.55 to 0.65

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations (Contact Pressure Distribution)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Contact pressure distribution figure showing higher intensity at edges and lower at centre.
  • Aim: Identify the footing type and soil condition.

Core Concepts:

  • Rigid footing enforces uniform settlement → pressure distribution varies with soil type.
  • Cohesive soil (clay): Edge soil resists lateral displacement due to cohesion → higher contact pressure at edges.
  • Cohesionless soil (sand): Edge soil yields laterally → higher pressure at centre.
  • Flexible footing: Produces uniform pressure (= total load / area).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Non-uniform pressure distribution → rigid footing (flexible footing would give uniform pressure).
  2. Higher pressure at edges → soil provides edge resistance → cohesive (clay) behaviour.
  3. Lower pressure at centre → consistent with rigid settlement on clay.
  4. Cohesionless soil would show a central peak, ruling out sand.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Rigid footing resting on a cohesive soil | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Which one of the following saturated fine-grained soils can attain a negative Skempton’s pore pressure coefficient (\( A \))?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soils (Pore Pressure Parameters)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Saturated fine-grained soils.
  • Aim: Identify the soil that can attain a negative Skempton's pore pressure coefficient \(A\).

Core Concepts:

Skempton's equation (saturated soil, \(B = 1\)):
\[\Delta u = \Delta\sigma_3 + A(\Delta\sigma_1 - \Delta\sigma_3) \]

  • Normally consolidated clays: Contractive tendency on shearing → positive pore pressure → \(A > 0\) (typically 0.5–1.0).
  • Over-consolidated clays: Dilative tendency on shearing → negative pore pressure generated → \(A < 0\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Quick clays and NC clays: contractive → high positive \(A\).
  2. Lightly consolidated clays: positive \(A\).
  3. Over-consolidated clays: dilate on shearing → \(\Delta u\) is negative for the same \(\Delta\sigma\) → \(A\) is negative.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: Over-consolidated clays | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q34
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A reinforced concrete pile of 10 m length and 0.7 m diameter is embedded in a saturated pure clay with unit cohesion of 50 kPa. If the adhesion factor is 0.5, the net ultimate uplift pullout capacity (in kN) of the pile is _________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Pile Foundations (Uplift Capacity in Clay)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Pile length \(L = 10\text{ m}\), diameter \(D = 0.7\text{ m}\); saturated clay \(c_u = 50\text{ kPa}\); adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.5\).
  • Aim: Net ultimate uplift pullout capacity (kN, nearest integer).

Core Concepts:

For uplift in cohesive soil, net ultimate capacity = skin adhesion only (end resistance neglected):
\[Q_u = \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot (\pi D L) \]
Relevant provision: IS 2911 (Part 1/Sec 1):2010, Clause 7.3.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Adhesion strength:
    \[\alpha \cdot c_u = 0.5 \times 50 = 25\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Shaft surface area:
    \[\pi D L = \pi \times 0.7 \times 10 = 21.991\text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Uplift capacity:
    \[Q_u = 25 \times 21.991 = 549.78\text{ kN} \approx 550\text{ kN} \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 550 kN | Accepted range: [545 to 555]

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Consider the statements P and Q related to the analysis/design of retaining walls.

P: When a rough retaining wall moves toward the backfill, the wall friction force/resistance mobilizes in upward direction along the wall.

Q: Most of the earth pressure theories calculate the earth pressure due to surcharge by neglecting the actual distribution of stresses due to surcharge.

Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: Both P and Q are TRUE
P is TRUE and Q is FALSE
Both P and Q are FALSE

structuredOptions.label: A

structuredOptions.html: P is TRUE and Q is FALSE

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theories

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    Statement P: In a passive state (wall moves toward backfill), wall friction mobilizes upward.
    Statement Q: Most theories neglect actual stress distribution for surcharge earth pressure.
  • Aim: Identify whether statements P and Q are TRUE or FALSE.

Core Concepts:

Passive Earth Pressure & Wall Friction: When a retaining wall is pushed into the backfill (passive case), the soil wedge is forced upward and outward along the failure plane. Because the soil wedge moves upward relative to the wall, the friction exerted by the wall on the soil is downward to oppose the movement. Therefore, the wall friction resistance mobilized along the wall acts downward.

Surcharge Loading: Standard theories (Rankine/Coulomb) simplify a uniform surcharge \(q\) as a constant lateral earth pressure increase (\(\Delta p = K \cdot q\)) throughout the entire depth, completely ignoring the non-linear Boussinesq or Westergaard elastic stress distribution bulbs.

Solution Method:

  • Evaluate P: The relative motion of the soil wedge is upward. Therefore, the frictional resistance acting on the soil is downward. Statement P claims it is upward, so it is FALSE.
  • Evaluate Q: Standard earth pressure theories indeed simplify surcharge effects by treating them as uniform rectangular distributions, neglecting the exact elastic stress variations. So, statement Q is TRUE.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Statement P: Wall moves toward backfill \(\rightarrow\) Passive state. Soil moves upward relative to the wall. Frictional resistance (acting to oppose soil movement) is downward. Statement P says "upward", so P is FALSE.
  2. Analyze Statement Q: Theories calculate pressure due to surcharge assuming uniform lateral pressure increase, neglecting actual stress distributions. Q is TRUE.

Final Answer:

Final Answer: P is FALSE and Q is TRUE | Correct option: (D)

questions.explanation:

  • Given Data: Statements P, Q, and R regarding soil properties and seepage.

Core Concepts:

Statement P: Compacted fine-grained soils with a flocculated structure (dry of optimum) are relatively more random and thus often considered to have isotropic permeability compared to dispersed structures (wet of optimum), which are highly anisotropic. P is TRUE in standard geotechnical literature.

Statement Q: The phreatic line is the uppermost flow line in an earth dam where the pore water pressure is strictly zero (atmospheric), not maximum. Maximum pore pressure occurs deeper below the water table. Q is FALSE.

Statement R: Piping below a dam foundation due to backward erosion is simply called "piping" or "seepage erosion". "Blowout" (or heave) specifically refers to the instability at the base of an excavation due to upward seepage forces exceeding buoyant unit weight. R is FALSE.

  1. Result: P is TRUE, Q is FALSE, R is FALSE.
  2. Evaluate the MCQ-style options:

    • (B) P is FALSE and Q is TRUE → Incorrect (Both reversed)

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A homogeneous earth dam has a maximum water head difference of 15 m between the upstream and downstream sides. A flownet was drawn with the number of potential drops as 10 and the average length of the element as 3 m. Specific gravity of the soil is 2.65. For a factor of safety of 2.0 against piping failure, void ratio of the soil is _________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage & Flownets

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    Maximum water head difference (\(\Delta H\)) = 15 m
    Number of potential drops (\(N_d\)) = 10
    Average length of element (\(\Delta L\)) = 3 m
    Specific gravity (\(G_s\)) = 2.65
    Factor of safety against piping (\(FOS\)) = 2.0
  • Aim: Calculate the void ratio (\(e\)) of the soil.

Core Concepts:

  • Head Loss per Drop: \(\Delta h = \dfrac{\Delta H}{N_d}\)
  • Exit Gradient: \(i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{\Delta L}\)
  • Critical Hydraulic Gradient: \(i_c = \dfrac{G_s - 1}{1 + e}\)
  • Factor of Safety: \(FOS = \dfrac{i_c}{i}\)

Solution Method:

First determine the actual exit gradient. Using the given FOS, back-calculate the required critical hydraulic gradient. Then use the specific gravity to solve for the unknown void ratio.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate head loss per drop:
    \[\Delta h = \dfrac{15}{10} = 1.5\text{ m} \]
  2. Calculate maximum exit gradient (\(i\)):
    \[i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{\Delta L} = \dfrac{1.5}{3} = 0.5 \]
  3. Calculate required critical gradient (\(i_c\)):
    \[FOS = \dfrac{i_c}{i} \implies 2.0 = \dfrac{i_c}{0.5} \implies i_c = 1.0 \]
  4. Solve for Void Ratio (\(e\)):
    \[i_c = \dfrac{G_s - 1}{1 + e} \implies 1.0 = \dfrac{2.65 - 1}{1 + e} \]\[1 + e = 1.65 \implies e = 0.65 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(e = 0.65\) | Accepted key range: [0.63 to 0.67]

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The in-situ percentage of voids of a sand deposit is 50%. The maximum and minimum densities of sand determined from the laboratory tests are 1.8 g/cm³ and 1.3 g/cm³, respectively. Assume the specific gravity of sand as 2.7.

The relative density index of the in-situ sand is _________ (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Index Properties

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data:
    In-situ percentage of voids (\(n\)) = 50% = 0.5
    Maximum lab density (\(\rho_{max}\)) = 1.8 g/cm³
    Minimum lab density (\(\rho_{min}\)) = 1.3 g/cm³
    Specific gravity (\(G_s\)) = 2.7
  • Aim: Find the relative density index (\(I_d\)) of the in-situ sand.

Core Concepts:

  • Void Ratio and Porosity: \(e = \dfrac{n}{1 - n}\)
  • Dry Density Relation: \(e = \dfrac{G_s \rho_w}{\rho_d} - 1\)
  • Relative Density: \(I_d = \dfrac{e_{max} - e}{e_{max} - e_{min}}\)

Solution Method:

Convert the given porosity to an in-situ void ratio. Then use the specific gravity relationship to convert maximum and minimum lab densities into minimum and maximum void ratios respectively. Plug into the relative density formula.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate in-situ void ratio (\(e\)):
    \[e = \dfrac{0.5}{1 - 0.5} = 1.0 \]
  2. Calculate minimum void ratio (\(e_{min}\)) — occurs at maximum density:
    \[e_{min} = \dfrac{G_s \rho_w}{\rho_{max}} - 1 = \dfrac{2.7 \times 1.0}{1.8} - 1 = 1.5 - 1 = 0.5 \]
  3. Calculate maximum void ratio (\(e_{max}\)) — occurs at minimum density:
    \[e_{max} = \dfrac{G_s \rho_w}{\rho_{min}} - 1 = \dfrac{2.7 \times 1.0}{1.3} - 1 = 2.0769 - 1 = 1.0769 \]
  4. Calculate Relative Density (\(I_d\)):
    \[I_d = \dfrac{e_{max} - e}{e_{max} - e_{min}} = \dfrac{1.0769 - 1.0}{1.0769 - 0.5} = \dfrac{0.0769}{0.5769} = 0.1333 \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.13 (or 13%) | Accepted key range: [0.12 to 0.14] or [12 to 14]

questions.title: GATE CE 2024 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A drained triaxial test was conducted on a saturated sand specimen using a stress-path triaxial testing system. The specimen failed when the axial stress reached a value of 100 kN/m² from an initial confining pressure of 300 kN/m².

The angle of shearing plane (in degrees) with respect to horizontal is _________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soil

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    Drained test on saturated sand. Cohesion \(c' = 0\).
    Initial confining pressure (\(\sigma_c\)) = 300 kN/m².
    Axial stress at failure = 100 kN/m².
  • Aim: Find the angle of the shearing plane with respect to the horizontal.

Core Concepts:

Triaxial Extension Path: The phrasing "axial stress reached a value of 100 from an initial confining pressure of 300" indicates an unloading scenario. The horizontal confining stress remains 300 kN/m², while vertical stress drops to 100 kN/m².

  • Major principal stress: \(\sigma_1 = 300\text{ kN/m}^2\) (acting on the vertical plane)
  • Minor principal stress: \(\sigma_3 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2\) (acting on the horizontal plane)
  • Angle of Internal Friction: \(\sin\phi = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3}\) (for sand, \(c = 0\))
  • Failure Plane Angle: \(\theta_f = 45^\circ + \phi/2\) with the major principal plane

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Principal Stresses: Since \(\sigma_h > \sigma_v\), \(\sigma_1 = 300\text{ kN/m}^2\) and \(\sigma_3 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2\).
    The major principal plane (where \(\sigma_1\) acts) is the vertical plane.
  2. Calculate Angle of Internal Friction (\(\phi\)):
    \[\sin\phi = \dfrac{300 - 100}{300 + 100} = \dfrac{200}{400} = 0.5 \implies \phi = 30^\circ \]
  3. Determine Shearing Plane Angle:
    Failure plane makes an angle \(\theta = 45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\) with the major principal plane (vertical):
    \[\theta = 45^\circ + \dfrac{30^\circ}{2} = 60^\circ \text{ (with respect to vertical)} \]
    Therefore, angle with respect to the horizontal:
    \[90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ \]

Final Answer:

Final Answer: 30° | Accepted key range: [30 to 30]

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q16
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The specific gravity of a soil is 2.60. The soil is at 50% degree of saturation with a water content of 15%. The void ratio of the soil is ________ .
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Phase Diagram & Index Properties

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Specific Gravity: \(G = 2.60\)
    • Degree of Saturation: \(S = 50\% = 0.50\)
    • Water Content: \(w = 15\% = 0.15\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Void Ratio \((e)\).

Core Concepts:

Fundamental relationship between void ratio \((e)\), degree of saturation \((S)\), specific gravity \((G)\), and water content \((w)\):\[Se = wG \]

  • \(e = \dfrac{V_v}{V_s}\) (Void Ratio)
  • \(S = \dfrac{V_w}{V_v}\) (Degree of Saturation)
  • \(w = \dfrac{W_w}{W_s}\) (Water Content)
  • \(G = \dfrac{\gamma_s}{\gamma_w}\) (Specific Gravity)

Solution Method:

Rearrange the fundamental formula to solve for \(e\), then substitute given values.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. State the formula:\[Se = wG \]
  2. Rearrange for \(e\):\[e = \dfrac{wG}{S} \]
  3. Substitute values:\[e = \dfrac{0.15 \times 2.60}{0.50} \]
  4. Calculate:\[e = \dfrac{0.39}{0.50} = 0.78 \]

Sanity Check: For a medium-dense soil with 50% saturation and 15% water content, a void ratio of 0.78 is physically consistent.

Final Answer:

0.78 | Correct Option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q17
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A group of 9 friction piles are arranged in a square grid maintaining equal spacing in all directions. Each pile is of diameter 300 mm and length 7 m. Assume that the soil is cohesionless with effective friction angle \( \phi' = 32^\circ \). What is the center-to-center spacing of the piles (in m) for the pile group efficiency of 60%?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations (Piles)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Number of piles: \(n = 9\), arranged in a \(3 \times 3\) square grid
    • Pile Diameter: \(D = 300\text{ mm} = 0.3\text{ m}\)
    • Pile Length: \(L = 7\text{ m}\)
    • Soil: Cohesionless, \(\phi' = 32^\circ\)
    • Group Efficiency: \(\eta_g = 60\% = 0.60\)
  • Aim: Calculate center-to-center spacing \((s)\).

Core Concepts:

Converse-Labarre Formula: A standard empirical formula for estimating group efficiency for friction piles in cohesionless soils.\[ \eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{\alpha}{90} \left[\dfrac{(m-1)n + (n-1)m}{mn} \right] \]where \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{D}{s}\right)\) in degrees, \(m\) and \(n\) are the number of rows and columns.

Note: This question was officially marked MTA (Marks To All) by GATE due to ambiguity in the data or formula intended.

Solution Method:

  1. Identify grid parameters \(m\) and \(n\).
  2. Apply the Converse-Labarre formula.
  3. Solve for spacing \(s\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Define Grid Parameters:
    For a \(3 \times 3\) square grid: \(m = 3,\; n = 3\)
  2. Apply Converse-Labarre Formula:\[ 0.60 = 1 - \dfrac{\tan^{-1}(0.3/s)}{90} \left[\dfrac{(3-1)\cdot3 + (3-1)\cdot3}{3 \times 3} \right] \]
  3. Calculate the geometric bracket term:\[\text{Term} = \dfrac{(2 \times 3) + (2 \times 3)}{9} = \dfrac{6+6}{9} = \dfrac{4}{3} \]
  4. Solve for \(\alpha\):\[1 - 0.60 = \dfrac{\alpha}{90} \times \dfrac{4}{3} \]\[0.40 = \dfrac{4\alpha}{270} \]\[\alpha = \dfrac{0.40 \times 270}{4} = 27^\circ \]
  5. Solve for spacing \(s\):\[\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{0.3}{s}\right) = 27^\circ \]\[\dfrac{0.3}{s} = \tan(27^\circ) \approx 0.5095 \]\[s = \dfrac{0.3}{0.5095} \approx 0.588\text{ m} \]

The calculated value \(0.588\text{ m}\) is closest to Option (A) \(0.582\text{ m}\). Due to discrepancy between the calculated value and provided options, GATE awarded marks to all.

Final Answer:

0.588 m (Closest to Option A) | Official Key: MTA (Marks to All)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A possible slope failure is shown in the figure. Three soil samples are taken from different locations (I, II and III) of the potential failure plane. Which is the most appropriate shear strength test for each of the sample to identify the failure mechanism? Identify the correct combination from the following options:
P: Triaxial compression test
Q: Triaxial extension test
R: Direct shear or shear box test
S: Vane shear test
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength & Slope Stability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: A slope failure profile with three locations:
    • Location III: Top (Crest)
    • Location II: Mid-slope
    • Location I: Toe
  • Aim: Match each location to the appropriate shear strength test:
    • P: Triaxial Compression Test
    • Q: Triaxial Extension Test
    • R: Direct Shear (Shear Box) Test
    • S: Vane Shear Test

Core Concepts:

LocationPositionStress StateMajor Principal Stress \((\sigma_1)\)Appropriate Test
IIITop/CrestActive (Rankine)Vertical \((\sigma_v)\)Triaxial Compression (P)
IIMid-slopeShear along failure planeRotated (plane-specific)Direct Shear (R)
IToePassive (Rankine)Horizontal \((\sigma_h)\)Triaxial Extension (Q)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Location III (Top/Crest):
    The soil mass moves downward and away from the slope → Active State.
    Vertical stress is the major principal stress (\(\sigma_1 = \sigma_v\)); lateral stress is minor (\(\sigma_3 = \sigma_h\)).
    Best simulated by Triaxial Compression Test (P), where axial stress is the major principal stress.
    → III–P
  2. Location II (Mid-slope):
    The potential failure plane is parallel or sub-parallel to the slope face. Principal stresses rotate along this plane.
    Direct Shear Test (R) allows shearing on a specific pre-determined plane, which can be aligned with the slope failure surface.
    → II–R
  3. Location I (Toe):
    The sliding soil mass pushes against the toe → Passive State.
    Horizontal stress from the sliding wedge exceeds vertical stress (\(\sigma_1 = \sigma_h\), \(\sigma_3 = \sigma_v\)). Failure involves lateral compression pushing soil upward.
    Best simulated by Triaxial Extension Test (Q), where cell pressure (lateral) exceeds axial stress.
    → I–Q
  4. Match with options:
    Derived combination: I–Q, II–R, III–P → matches Option (A).

Final Answer:

I–Q, II–R, III–P | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A drained direct shear test was carried out on a sandy soil. Under a normal stress of 50 kPa, the test specimen failed at a shear stress of 35 kPa. The angle of internal friction of the sample is ______________ degree (round off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength – Drained Direct Shear Test

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Test: Drained Direct Shear on sandy soil (\(c' = 0\))
    • Normal stress: \(\sigma_n = 50\text{ kPa}\)
    • Shear stress at failure: \(\tau_f = 35\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Determine the angle of internal friction \((\phi')\).

Core Concepts:

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion for cohesionless soil (\(c' = 0\)):\[\tau_f = \sigma_n \tan(\phi') \]In a drained test on sand, total stresses equal effective stresses (no excess pore pressure).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply failure criterion:\[35 = 50 \times \tan(\phi') \]
  2. Solve for \(\tan(\phi')\):\[\tan(\phi') = \dfrac{35}{50} = 0.7 \]
  3. Calculate angle:\[\phi' = \arctan(0.7) \approx 34.99^\circ \approx 35^\circ \]

Final Answer:

\(\phi' = 35^\circ\) | Accepted range: 35 to 35

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: With reference to the compaction test conducted on soils, which of the following is INCORRECT?
options: Peak point of the compaction curve gives the maximum dry unit weight and optimum moisture content
With increase in the compaction effort, the maximum dry unit weight increases
With increase in the compaction effort, the optimum moisture content decreases
Compaction curve crosses the zero-air-voids curve

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Peak point of the compaction curve gives the maximum dry unit weight and optimum moisture content
structuredOptions.html: Peak point of the compaction curve gives the maximum dry unit weight and optimum moisture content

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: With increase in the compaction effort, the maximum dry unit weight increases
structuredOptions.html: With increase in the compaction effort, the maximum dry unit weight increases

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: With increase in the compaction effort, the optimum moisture content decreases
structuredOptions.html: With increase in the compaction effort, the optimum moisture content decreases

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Compaction curve crosses the zero-air-voids curve
structuredOptions.html: Compaction curve crosses the zero-air-voids curve

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Compaction

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data: Statements regarding soil compaction tests.
  • Aim: Identify the INCORRECT statement among the four options.

Core Concepts:

  • Compaction Curve: A plot of dry unit weight \((\gamma_d)\) versus moisture content \((w)\). The peak gives Maximum Dry Unit Weight and Optimum Moisture Content (OMC).
  • Effect of Compaction Effort: Increasing compactive effort (e.g., Standard → Modified Proctor) shifts the compaction curve upward and to the left — higher maximum \(\gamma_d\), lower OMC.
  • Zero-Air-Voids (ZAV) Curve: Represents the theoretical maximum \(\gamma_d\) at 100% saturation (no air voids).\[\gamma_{ZAV} = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1 + wG} \]

Evaluation of Each Statement:

  • (A) "Peak point gives maximum dry unit weight and OMC" — TRUE. This is the fundamental definition of the peak of the compaction curve.
  • (B) "With increase in compaction effort, maximum dry unit weight increases" — TRUE. Higher energy compacts the soil more densely.
  • (C) "With increase in compaction effort, OMC decreases" — TRUE. Higher energy forces particles closer together, requiring less water for maximum density.
  • (D) "Compaction curve crosses the zero-air-voids curve" — FALSE. Reaching the ZAV line requires 100% saturation. Mechanical compaction always leaves some entrapped air (saturation typically 85–95%). It is physically impossible for the compaction curve to touch or cross the ZAV line.

Final Answer:

Compaction curve crosses the zero-air-voids curve (is the incorrect statement) | Correct Option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Consider that a force \( P \) is acting on the surface of a half-space (Boussinesq's problem). The expression for the vertical stress (\( \sigma_z \)) at any point \( (r, z) \), within the half-space is given as,
\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi} \dfrac{z^3}{(r^2 + z^2)^{\dfrac{5}{2}}} \]
where, \( r \) is the radial distance, and \( z \) is the depth with downward direction taken as positive. At any given \( r \), there is a variation of \( \sigma_z \) along \( z \), and at a specific \( z \), the value of \( \sigma_z \) will be maximum. What is the locus of the maximum \( \sigma_z \)?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stress Distribution in Soil

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data: Boussinesq's vertical stress expression:\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi} \cdot \dfrac{z^3}{(r^2 + z^2)^{5/2}} \]
    • \(r\) = radial distance (constant)
    • \(z\) = depth (variable)
  • Aim: Find the locus (relationship between \(r\) and \(z\)) where \(\sigma_z\) is maximized for a given constant \(r\).

Core Concepts:

Calculus — Maximization: To find the maximum of a differentiable function with respect to \(z\), set the first derivative \(\dfrac{\partial \sigma_z}{\partial z} = 0\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up the differentiation:
    Let \(K = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi}\) (constant). Maximize:\[f(z) = z^3 \cdot (r^2 + z^2)^{-5/2} \]
  2. Differentiate with respect to \(z\) (product rule):\[\dfrac{df}{dz} = 3z^2(r^2+z^2)^{-5/2} + z^3 \cdot \left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right)(r^2+z^2)^{-7/2} \cdot 2z = 0 \]
  3. Simplify:\[3z^2(r^2+z^2)^{-5/2} - 5z^4(r^2+z^2)^{-7/2} = 0 \]Divide both sides by \(z^2(r^2+z^2)^{-7/2}\) (assuming \(z \neq 0\)):\[3(r^2+z^2) - 5z^2 = 0 \]\[3r^2 + 3z^2 - 5z^2 = 0 \]\[3r^2 = 2z^2 \]\[\boxed{z^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}r^2} \]

Final Answer:

\(z^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}r^2\) | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A square footing of size 2.5 m × 2.5 m is placed 1.0 m below the ground surface on a cohesionless homogeneous soil stratum. Considering that the groundwater table is located at the base of the footing, the unit weights of soil above and below the groundwater table are 18 kN/m³ and 20 kN/m³, respectively, and the bearing capacity factor \( N_q \) is 58, the net ultimate bearing capacity of the soil is estimated as 1706 kPa (unit weight of water = 10 kN/m³).
Earlier, a plate load test was carried out with a circular plate of 30 cm diameter in the same foundation pit during a dry season, when the water table was located beyond the plate influence zone. Using Terzaghi's bearing capacity formulation, what is the ultimate bearing capacity (in kPa) of the plate?
questions.explanation:
Foundation Engineering | Bearing Capacity

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Square footing: \(B_1 = 2.5\text{ m}\), \(D_{f1} = 1.0\text{ m}\)
    • Water table at base of footing: \(\gamma_1 = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\) (above WT), \(\gamma_{sat} = 20\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3 \Rightarrow \gamma' = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • \(N_q = 58\), cohesionless soil \((c = 0)\)
    • Net ultimate bearing capacity: \(q_{nu} = 1706\text{ kPa}\)
    • Plate load test: Circular plate, \(B_p = 0.3\text{ m}\), placed at pit base (surcharge \(= 0\))
    • WT beyond influence zone for plate test \(\Rightarrow\) use bulk \(\gamma = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the ultimate bearing capacity \(q_u\) of the plate.

Core Concepts:

  • Terzaghi's formula — Square Footing \((c=0)\):
    Net ultimate capacity:\[q_{nu} = \gamma_1 D_f (N_q - 1) + 0.4\,\gamma'\, B\, N_\gamma \]
  • Terzaghi's formula — Circular Plate \((c=0,\; \bar{q}=0)\):\[q_u = 0.3\,\gamma_2\, B_p\, N_\gamma \]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Extract \(N_\gamma\) from the footing data:\[1706 = (18 \times 1.0 \times (58-1)) + (0.4 \times 10 \times 2.5 \times N_\gamma) \]\[1706 = 18 \times 57 + 10\, N_\gamma \]\[1706 = 1026 + 10\, N_\gamma \]\[N_\gamma = \dfrac{680}{10} = 68 \]
  2. Calculate \(q_u\) for the plate load test:
    Circular plate at pit base: \(c=0\), \(\bar{q}=0\), \(\gamma_2 = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(B_p = 0.3\text{ m}\):\[q_u = 0.3 \times 18 \times 0.3 \times 68 \]\[q_u = 1.62 \times 68 = 110.16\text{ kPa} \]
ParameterValue
\(N_q\)58
\(N_\gamma\) (back-calculated)68
\(B_p\)0.3 m
\(\gamma_2\)18 kN/m³
\(q_u\) (plate)110.16 kPa

Final Answer:

110.16 kPa | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A soil having the average properties, bulk unit weight = 19 kN/m³; angle of internal friction = 25° and cohesion = 15 kPa, is being formed on a rock slope existing at an inclination of 35° with the horizontal. The critical height (in m) of the soil formation up to which it would be stable without any failure is ________________ (round off to one decimal place).
[Assume the soil is being formed parallel to the rock bedding plane and there is no ground water effect.]
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability – Infinite Slope / Planar Failure

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Bulk unit weight: \(\gamma = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Angle of internal friction: \(\phi = 25^\circ\)
    • Cohesion: \(c = 15\text{ kPa}\)
    • Slope inclination: \(\beta = 35^\circ\)
    • Condition: Critical height at \(F_s = 1.0\)
  • Aim: Calculate the critical vertical height \(H\) (in m).

Core Concepts:

  • Stresses on the failure plane at depth \(H\):
    • Normal Stress: \(\sigma_n = \gamma H \cos^2\beta\)
    • Driving Shear Stress: \(\tau = \gamma H \cos\beta\sin\beta\)
  • Shear Strength (Mohr-Coulomb): \(\tau_f = c + \sigma_n\tan\phi\)
  • Stability condition at critical height: Driving stress \(=\) Resisting strength \((\tau = \tau_f)\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Equilibrium equation:\[\gamma H\cos\beta\sin\beta = c + (\gamma H\cos^2\beta)\tan\phi \]
  2. Trigonometric values:
    \(\cos 35^\circ \approx 0.8192\), \(\sin 35^\circ \approx 0.5736\), \(\tan 25^\circ \approx 0.4663\)
  3. Simplify driving term (LHS):\[\tau = 19H \times 0.8192 \times 0.5736 \approx 8.928H \]
  4. Simplify resisting term (RHS):\[\sigma_n\tan\phi = 19H \times (0.8192)^2 \times 0.4663 \approx 5.946H \]\[\tau_f = 15 + 5.946H \]
  5. Solve for \(H\):\[8.928H = 15 + 5.946H \]\[(8.928 - 5.946)H = 15 \]\[2.982H = 15 \Rightarrow H = \dfrac{15}{2.982} \approx 5.03\text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

\(H \approx 5.0\text{ m}\) | Accepted range: 4.8 to 5.2

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A smooth vertical retaining wall supporting layered soils is shown in figure. According to Rankine’s earth pressure theory, the lateral active earth pressure acting at the base of the wall is ________________ kPa (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure – Rankine's Active Pressure (Layered Soil)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Surcharge: \(q = 20\text{ kPa}\)
    • Layer 1 (top 3 m): \(\gamma_1 = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi_1 = 32^\circ\), \(c_1 = 0\)
    • Layer 2 (bottom 4 m): \(\gamma_2 = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi_2 = 25^\circ\), \(c_2 = 20\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Lateral active earth pressure at the base of the wall (depth \(z = 7\text{ m}\)).

Core Concepts:

Rankine's Active Pressure: \(p_a = K_a\,\sigma_v - 2c\sqrt{K_a}\)

Active Pressure Coefficient: \(K_a = \tan^2(45^\circ - \phi/2)\)

At the base, use Layer 2 properties \((\phi_2, c_2)\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(K_{a2}\) for Layer 2:\[K_{a2} = \tan^2(45^\circ - 12.5^\circ) = \tan^2(32.5^\circ) \approx (0.6371)^2 \approx 0.4059 \]
  2. Vertical stress at base \((z = 7\text{ m})\):\[\sigma_v = q + \gamma_1 h_1 + \gamma_2 h_2 = 20 + (18 \times 3) + (19 \times 4) \]\[= 20 + 54 + 76 = 150\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Active earth pressure at base:\[p_a = K_{a2}\,\sigma_v - 2c_2\sqrt{K_{a2}} \]\[= (0.4059 \times 150) - (2 \times 20 \times 0.6371) \]\[= 60.885 - 25.484 = 35.40\text{ kPa} \]

Final Answer:

\(p_a \approx 35.4\text{ kPa}\) | Accepted range: 34.0 to 37.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 1 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A vertical trench is excavated in a clayey soil deposit having a surcharge load of 30 kPa. A fluid of unit weight 12 kN/m³ is poured in the trench to prevent collapse as the excavation proceeds. Assume that the fluid is not seeping through the soil deposit. If the undrained cohesion of the clay deposit is 20 kPa and saturated unit weight is 18 kN/m³, what is the maximum depth of unsupported excavation (in m, rounded off to two decimal places)? ________________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Excavation – Stability of Slurry Trench

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Surcharge: \(q = 30\text{ kPa}\)
    • Fluid unit weight in trench: \(\gamma_f = 12\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Clay: \(c_u = 20\text{ kPa}\), \(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi_u = 0\)
  • Aim: Maximum depth \(H\) of unsupported excavation.

Core Concepts:

  • Active Earth Pressure (soil side) for \(\phi = 0\), \(K_a = 1\):\[\sigma_a = \gamma_{sat}z + q - 2c_u \]Total active thrust:\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_{sat}H^2 + (q - 2c_u)H \]
  • Fluid resistance (trench side):\[P_f = \dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_f H^2 \]
  • Limit equilibrium: \(P_a = P_f\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Force equilibrium:\[\dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_{sat}H^2 + qH - 2c_u H = \dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_f H^2 \]
  2. Rearrange and divide by \(H\) \((H \neq 0)\):\[\dfrac{1}{2}(\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_f)H + (q - 2c_u) = 0 \]
  3. Substitute values:\[\dfrac{1}{2}(18 - 12)H + (30 - 40) = 0 \]\[3H - 10 = 0 \]
  4. Solve for \(H\):\[H = \dfrac{10}{3} \approx 3.33\text{ m} \]

Final Answer:

\(H \approx 3.33\text{ m}\) | Accepted range: 3.30 to 3.35

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A standard penetration test (SPT) was carried out at a location by using a manually operated hammer dropping system with 50% efficiency. The recorded SPT value at a particular depth is 28. If an automatic hammer dropping system with 70% efficiency is used at the same location, the recorded SPT value will be ______.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Standard Penetration Test (SPT)

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Manual hammer efficiency: \(\eta_1 = 50\% = 0.50\)
    • Recorded SPT value: \(N_1 = 28\)
    • Automatic hammer efficiency: \(\eta_2 = 70\% = 0.70\)
  • Aim: Determine corrected SPT value \(N_2\) for new hammer efficiency at identical soil conditions.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Energy Correction Principle: SPT \(N\)-value is inversely proportional to energy delivered to the sampler for identical soil resistance.
  • Correction Formula:\[\eta_1 \times N_1 = \eta_2 \times N_2 \implies N_2 = N_1 \times \dfrac{\eta_1}{\eta_2}\]

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Energy delivered to sampler: \(E \propto \eta \times N\) for constant soil resistance.
  2. Equate energy for same soil conditions: \(\eta_1 \times N_1 = \eta_2 \times N_2\)
  3. Rearrange and substitute values:\[N_2 = 28 \times \dfrac{0.50}{0.70} = 28 \times \dfrac{5}{7} = 20.0\]

Sanity Check: Higher efficiency hammer (70% > 50%) delivers more energy per blow → fewer blows required for same penetration → \(N_2 < N_1\) (20 < 28). ✓

4. Final Answer:

\(N_2 = \mathbf{20}\) | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A vertical sheet pile wall is installed in an anisotropic soil having coefficient of horizontal permeability, \( k_H \) and coefficient of vertical permeability, \( k_V \). In order to draw the flow net for the isotropic condition, the embedment depth of the wall should be scaled by a factor of _______, without changing the horizontal scale.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage Analysis in Anisotropic Soils

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Horizontal permeability coefficient: \(k_H\)
    • Vertical permeability coefficient: \(k_V\)
    • Horizontal scale: maintained unchanged.
  • Aim: Determine the scaling factor for the vertical dimension (embedment depth) to transform the anisotropic flow domain to an isotropic equivalent for flow net construction.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Anisotropic Flow Transformation: For soils with \(k_H \neq k_V\), coordinate transformation converts the anisotropic domain to an isotropic equivalent:\[x' = x, \quad z' = z \times \sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\]
  • Governing Equation: The anisotropic Laplace equation:\[k_H \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2} + k_V \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial z^2} = 0\]transforms to the isotropic form \(\nabla^2 h = 0\) under the scaling.
  • Equivalent Isotropic Permeability: \(k' = \sqrt{k_H \cdot k_V}\)

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Introduce transformed vertical coordinate: \(z' = z \times \alpha\) where \(\alpha\) is the scaling factor.
  2. Apply chain rule: \(\dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial z^2} = \alpha^2 \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial z'^2}\)
  3. Substitute into governing equation:\[k_H \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial x^2} + k_V \alpha^2 \dfrac{\partial^2 h}{\partial z'^2} = 0\]
  4. For isotropic form, require \(k_H = k_V \alpha^2\):\[\alpha^2 = \dfrac{k_H}{k_V} \implies \alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\]

Sanity Check: For typical stratified soils (\(k_H > k_V\)), scaling factor > 1 → vertical dimensions are stretched to compensate for higher horizontal permeability. ✓

4. Final Answer:

Scaling factor = \(\sqrt{\dfrac{k_H}{k_V}}\) | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q28
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The reason(s) of the nonuniform elastic settlement profile below a flexible footing, resting on a cohesionless soil while subjected to uniform loading, is/are:
options: Variation of friction angle along the width of the footing
Variation of soil stiffness along the width of the footing
Variation of friction angle along the depth of the footing
Variation of soil stiffness along the depth of the footing

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Variation of friction angle along the width of the footing
structuredOptions.html: Variation of friction angle along the width of the footing

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Variation of soil stiffness along the width of the footing
structuredOptions.html: Variation of soil stiffness along the width of the footing

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Variation of friction angle along the depth of the footing
structuredOptions.html: Variation of friction angle along the depth of the footing

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Variation of soil stiffness along the depth of the footing
structuredOptions.html: Variation of soil stiffness along the depth of the footing

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Settlement Analysis — Flexible Footings on Cohesionless Soil

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Analysis
  • Given Data: Non-uniform elastic settlement profile under a flexible footing on cohesionless soil with uniform loading.
  • Aim: Identify reason(s) for non-uniform settlement.

2. Core Concepts:

Footing TypePressure DistributionSettlement Pattern
RigidNon-uniform (higher at edges)Uniform settlement
FlexibleUniform pressureNon-uniform settlement (dish-shaped)

For cohesionless soil, soil stiffness (\(E_s\)) is proportional to confining pressure: \(E_s \propto (\sigma'_v)^n\) where \(n \approx 0.5\). Stiffness increases with depth.

3. Solution Method:

LocationStress ConditionSoil StiffnessSettlement
CenterStress bulb extends deeperLower effective stiffness (deeper, less confined near surface)More settlement
Edge/CornerStress concentrated near surfaceHigher effective stiffnessLess settlement

4. Statement Analysis:

StatementAnalysisVerdict
(A) Variation of friction angle along width\(\phi\) is a fundamental soil property; does not vary along width for homogeneous soil.❌ FALSE
(B) Variation of soil stiffness along widthDifferent positions (center vs. edge) experience different stress distributions with depth → different effective stiffness. This directly explains non-uniform settlement across the width.✅ TRUE
(C) Variation of friction angle along depth\(\phi'\) is constant for normally consolidated sand; it is \(K_0\) and \(\sigma'_v\) that vary with depth.❌ FALSE
(D) Variation of soil stiffness along depthWhile stiffness varies with depth (the root cause), the question specifically asks about non-uniformity across the width. (D) is too general and does not directly explain the settlement variation pattern along the width.❌ FALSE (per answer key)

5. Final Answer:

Statement (B) is TRUE | Option(s): B

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: An unconfined compression strength test was conducted on a cohesive soil. The test specimen failed at an axial stress of 76 kPa. The undrained cohesion (in kPa, in integer) of the soil is _________________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soil — Unconfined Compression Test

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: Axial failure stress \(\sigma_1 = 76\text{ kPa}\) (cohesive soil, UU condition).
  • Aim: Find undrained cohesion \(c_u\) (kPa, integer).

2. Core Concepts:

  • In the Unconfined Compression Test (UCT): \(\sigma_3 = 0\), so the unconfined compressive strength \(q_u = \sigma_1\).
  • For cohesive soil under undrained conditions (\(\phi_u = 0\)), the Mohr circle diameter equals \(q_u\):\[c_u = \dfrac{q_u}{2}\]

Reference: IS 2720, Part 10.

3. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(q_u = 76\text{ kPa}\) (given axial stress at failure).
  2. \(c_u = \dfrac{q_u}{2} = \dfrac{76}{2} = 38\text{ kPa}\)

Common Pitfall: Forgetting \(\phi_u = 0\) or confusing with drained shear strength parameters.

4. Final Answer:

\(c_u = \mathbf{38}\text{ kPa}\) | Accepted range: 38 to 38

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In the given figure, Point O indicates the stress point of a soil element at initial non-hydrostatic stress condition. For the stress path (OP), which of the following loading conditions is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Stress Path

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Initial stress condition at Point O.
    • Stress path (OP) drawn in the \(p\)-\(q\) space.
    • The slope of line OP is given graphically as \(1\) (vertical leg \(= 1\), horizontal leg \(= 1\)).
  • Aim: Determine the correct loading condition (variation of vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) and horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\)) that corresponds to the given stress path.

2. Core Concepts:

Stress Invariants:

  • Mean effective stress: \(p = \dfrac{\sigma_v + \sigma_h}{2}\)
  • Deviatoric stress: \(q = \dfrac{\sigma_v - \sigma_h}{2}\)

Stress Path Slope: The slope of the \(p\)-\(q\) plot is defined as \(m = \dfrac{\Delta q}{\Delta p}\).

3. Solution Method:

By evaluating the mathematical slope of the given stress path, we can establish a relationship between \(\Delta\sigma_v\) and \(\Delta\sigma_h\). Applying the graphical direction (upward and rightward) will tell us whether the stresses are increasing or decreasing.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine the slope from the graph:
    The right-angled triangle on the stress path OP shows a rise of \(1\) and a run of \(1\).\[\text{Slope} = \dfrac{\Delta q}{\Delta p} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1\]
  2. Substitute \(p\) and \(q\) variations:\[\Delta q = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h}{2}, \quad \Delta p = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h}{2}\]
  3. Equate and solve for stress changes:\[\dfrac{\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h}{2}}{\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h}{2}} = 1\]\[\Delta\sigma_v - \Delta\sigma_h = \Delta\sigma_v + \Delta\sigma_h\]
    Subtract \(\Delta\sigma_v\) from both sides:\[-\Delta\sigma_h = \Delta\sigma_h\]\[2\Delta\sigma_h = 0 \implies \Delta\sigma_h = 0\]
    This means the horizontal stress \(\sigma_h\) is constant.
  4. Determine the direction of vertical stress:
    The path OP moves upwards, meaning \(q\) is increasing (\(\Delta q > 0\)).\[\Delta q = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_v - 0}{2} > 0 \implies \Delta\sigma_v > 0\]
    This means the vertical stress \(\sigma_v\) is increasing.

5. Final Answer:

\(\sigma_v\) is increasing and \(\sigma_h\) is constant | Option(s): A

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The figure shows a vertical retaining wall with backfill consisting of cohesive-frictional soil and a failure plane developed due to passive earth pressure. The forces acting on the failure wedge are: \( P \) as the reaction force between the wall and the soil, \( R \) as the reaction force on the failure plane, \( C \) as the cohesive force along the failure plane and \( W \) as the weight of the failure wedge. Assuming that there is no adhesion between the wall and the wedge, identify the most appropriate force polygon for the wedge.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theory

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Vertical retaining wall retaining cohesive-frictional soil.
    • Failure plane developed due to passive earth pressure.
    • No adhesion between the wall and the wedge.
    • Forces: \(P\) (reaction from wall), \(R\) (reaction from soil), \(C\) (cohesive force), \(W\) (weight).
  • Aim: Identify the most appropriate, mathematically closed force polygon for the failure wedge.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Passive State Kinematics: The wall is pushed into the soil backfill. The failure soil wedge is consequently pushed upward and outward along the inclined failure plane.
  • Force Equilibrium (\(\sum \vec{F} = 0\)): The vectors must form a closed polygon when placed tip-to-tail.
  • Direction of Resistance: Frictional and cohesive forces always act in the direction opposite to the relative impending motion.

3. Solution Method:

Map out the true physical directions of all 4 forces acting on the wedge, then trace the vector additions to see which polygon structurally matches.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Vector Directions:
    • Weight (\(W\)): Gravity acts vertically downward (↓).
    • Cohesion (\(C\)): The wedge is moving up the failure plane. Cohesion resists this, so it acts downward along the failure plane (↙).
    • Failure plane reaction (\(R\)): The stationary soil resists the wedge's sliding via friction, so \(R\) points upward and to the left (↖).
    • Wall reaction (\(P\)): The wall pushes the wedge to the right; since the wedge moves upward relative to the wall, wall friction acts downward on the wedge. Thus \(P\) pushes to the right and slightly downward (↘).
  2. Evaluate the Polygons:
    Trace the correct sequence starting with \(W\):
    • \(W\) goes ↓
    • From \(W\)'s tip, \(C\) goes ↙
    • From \(C\)'s tip, \(R\) goes ↖
    • From \(R\)'s tip, \(P\) must close the shape going ↘ or → to reach \(W\)'s tail.
    Option (A): Vector \(P\) slopes upward (↗) — implies wall friction acting upward, which only occurs in the active state. (Incorrect)
    Option (B): Vector placement does not form a sequential physical polygon. (Incorrect)
    Option (C): \(W\) goes ↓, \(C\) goes ↙, \(R\) goes ↖, and \(P\) closes the loop pointing ↘. This perfectly matches passive state mechanics. (Correct)

5. Final Answer:

The polygon with \(W\) ↓, \(C\) ↙, \(R\) ↖, \(P\) ↘ | Option(s): C

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A square footing is to be designed to carry a column load of 500 kN which is resting on a soil stratum having the following average properties: bulk unit weight = 19 kN/m³; angle of internal friction = 0° and cohesion = 25 kPa.
Considering the depth of the footing as 1 m and adopting Meyerhof’s bearing capacity theory with a factor of safety of 3, the width of the footing (in m) is _________________ (round off to one decimal place)
[Assume the applicable shape and depth factor values as unity; ground water level at greater depth.]
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Type: Square footing
    • Column Load (\(P\)) = \(500\text{ kN}\)
    • Bulk unit weight (\(\gamma\)) = \(19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Friction angle (\(\phi\)) = \(0^\circ\)
    • Cohesion (\(c\)) = \(25\text{ kPa}\)
    • Depth of footing (\(D_f\)) = \(1\text{ m}\)
    • Factor of Safety (FoS) = \(3\)
    • Meyerhof's theory; Shape and depth factors = \(1.0\); Water table at greater depth (no correction needed).
  • Aim: Calculate the width of the footing \(B\) (in m, rounded to one decimal place).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Meyerhof's Bearing Capacity Equation:\[q_u = c N_c s_c d_c i_c + q N_q s_q d_q i_q + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma s_\gamma d_\gamma i_\gamma\]
  • Bearing Capacity Factors for \(\phi = 0^\circ\): \(N_q = 1.0,\ N_c = 5.14,\ N_\gamma = 0\)
  • Net Safe Bearing Capacity (\(q_{ns}\)):\[q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f, \quad q_{ns} = \dfrac{q_{nu}}{\text{FoS}}\]
  • Sizing the Footing:\[\dfrac{P}{B^2} = q_{ns}\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Simplify Meyerhof's equation (shape/depth factors = 1.0, \(N_\gamma = 0\)).
  2. Evaluate ultimate bearing capacity (\(q_u\)).
  3. Extract net ultimate (\(q_{nu}\)) and apply FoS to find net safe bearing capacity (\(q_{ns}\)).
  4. Calculate base area required, then take square root to find \(B\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Simplify Bearing Capacity Equation:\[q_u = c N_c + q N_q\]Where \(q = \gamma D_f = 19 \times 1 = 19\text{ kPa}\).
  2. Calculate Ultimate Bearing Capacity:\[q_u = (25 \times 5.14) + (19 \times 1.0) = 128.5 + 19 = 147.5\text{ kPa}\]
  3. Calculate Net Safe Bearing Capacity (\(q_{ns}\)):\[q_{nu} = 147.5 - 19 = 128.5\text{ kPa}\]\[q_{ns} = \dfrac{128.5}{3} = 42.833\text{ kPa}\]
  4. Equate and Find Width (\(B\)):\[\dfrac{500}{B^2} = 42.833 \implies B^2 = \dfrac{500}{42.833} = 11.673\text{ m}^2\]\[B = \sqrt{11.673} = 3.416\text{ m} \approx 3.4\text{ m}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(B = \mathbf{3.4}\text{ m}\) | Accepted key range: 3.0 to 3.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A circular pile of diameter 0.6 m and length 8 m was constructed in a cohesive soil stratum having the following properties: bulk unit weight = 19 kN/m³; angle of internal friction = 0° and cohesion = 25 kPa.
The allowable load the pile can carry with a factor of safety of 3 is _________________ kN (round off to one decimal place).
[Adopt: Adhesion factor, \( \alpha = 1.0 \) and Bearing capacity factor, \( N_c = 9.0 \)]
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Diameter of circular pile: \(D = 0.6\text{ m}\)
    • Length of pile: \(L = 8\text{ m}\)
    • Bulk unit weight: \(\gamma = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Angle of internal friction: \(\phi = 0^\circ\)
    • Cohesion: \(c = 25\text{ kPa}\)
    • Factor of Safety: \(FOS = 3\)
    • Adhesion factor: \(\alpha = 1.0\)
    • Bearing capacity factor: \(N_c = 9.0\)
  • Aim: Determine the allowable load (\(Q_{allow}\)) the pile can carry in kN.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(Q_u\)):\[Q_u = Q_p + Q_s\]
  • End Bearing (\(Q_p\)):\[Q_p = c \cdot N_c \cdot A_b\]where \(A_b\) is the cross-sectional area of the pile base.
  • Skin Friction (\(Q_s\)):\[Q_s = \alpha \cdot \bar{c} \cdot A_s\]where \(A_s\) is the surface area of the pile shaft.
  • Allowable Load:\[Q_{allow} = \dfrac{Q_u}{FOS}\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate base area (\(A_b\)) and shaft surface area (\(A_s\)).
  2. Compute point bearing resistance (\(Q_p\)) and frictional resistance (\(Q_s\)).
  3. Sum to find ultimate load capacity (\(Q_u\)).
  4. Apply the Factor of Safety to compute \(Q_{allow}\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate geometrical properties of the pile:\[A_b = \dfrac{\pi}{4}D^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.6)^2 = 0.28274\text{ m}^2\]\[A_s = \pi D L = \pi(0.6)(8) = 15.0796\text{ m}^2\]
  2. Calculate Ultimate End Bearing Capacity (\(Q_p\)):\[Q_p = 25 \times 9.0 \times 0.28274 = 63.617\text{ kN}\]
  3. Calculate Ultimate Skin Friction Resistance (\(Q_s\)):\[Q_s = 1.0 \times 25 \times 15.0796 = 376.99\text{ kN}\]
  4. Calculate Total Ultimate Load (\(Q_u\)):\[Q_u = 63.617 + 376.99 = 440.607\text{ kN}\]
  5. Calculate Allowable Load (\(Q_{allow}\)):\[Q_{allow} = \dfrac{440.607}{3} = 146.869 \approx 146.9\text{ kN}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(Q_{allow} = \mathbf{146.9}\text{ kN}\) | Accepted key range: 145.0 to 149.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: For the flow setup shown in the figure (not to scale), the hydraulic conductivities of the two soil samples, Soil 1 and Soil 2, are 10 mm/s and 1 mm/s, respectively. Assume the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³ and ignore the velocity head. At steady state, what is the total head (in m, rounded off to two decimal places) at any point located at the junction of the two samples? _________________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Permeability & Seepage

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Hydraulic conductivity of Soil 1: \(k_1 = 10\text{ mm/s}\)
    • Hydraulic conductivity of Soil 2: \(k_2 = 1\text{ mm/s}\)
    • Length of Soil 1 (elev. 3 m to 2 m): \(L_1 = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Length of Soil 2 (elev. 2 m to 1 m): \(L_2 = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Pressure on top water surface (elev. 4 m): \(P = 10\text{ kPa}\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Bottom water surface elevation: \(0\text{ m}\)
    • Velocity head is ignored.
  • Aim: Find the total head (\(H_{junction}\)) at the junction of the two samples (elevation 2 m).

2. Core Concepts:

  • Total Head (\(H\)):\[H = \dfrac{P}{\gamma_w} + Z\]
  • Continuity Equation for 1D Seepage: In steady state, discharge velocity is constant across series soil layers.\[v = k_1 i_1 = k_2 i_2, \quad i_1 = \dfrac{\Delta H_1}{L_1},\ i_2 = \dfrac{\Delta H_2}{L_2}\]

3. Solution Method:

  1. Establish boundary conditions for total head at top and bottom of the soil system.
  2. Equate flow velocities in both soil layers.
  3. Solve for the unknown total head at the junction (\(H_{junction}\)).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Head at Top Boundary (\(H_{top}\)):
    Top water surface at \(Z = 4\text{ m}\), pressure head \(= \dfrac{10}{10} = 1\text{ m}\).\[H_{top} = 4 + 1 = 5\text{ m}\]Since water is continuous from 4 m to 3 m, total head at the top of Soil 1 (elev. 3 m) remains \(5\text{ m}\).
  2. Total Head at Bottom Boundary (\(H_{bot}\)):
    Bottom free surface at \(Z = 0\text{ m}\), \(P = 0\).\[H_{bot} = 0 + 0 = 0\text{ m}\]
  3. Apply Continuity Equation:
    Let \(H_{junction}\) be the total head at elevation 2 m.
    Head loss across Soil 1: \(\Delta H_1 = 5 - H_{junction}\)
    Head loss across Soil 2: \(\Delta H_2 = H_{junction} - 0 = H_{junction}\)\[k_1\dfrac{\Delta H_1}{L_1} = k_2\dfrac{\Delta H_2}{L_2}\]\[10 \times \dfrac{5 - H_{junction}}{1} = 1 \times \dfrac{H_{junction}}{1}\]\[50 - 10\,H_{junction} = H_{junction}\]\[11\,H_{junction} = 50 \implies H_{junction} = \dfrac{50}{11} = 4.5\overline{45}\text{ m}\]
  4. Rounding Off: \(H_{junction} \approx 4.55\text{ m}\)

5. Final Answer:

\(H_{junction} = \mathbf{4.55}\text{ m}\) | Accepted key range: 4.50 to 4.60

questions.title: GATE CE 2023 Set 2 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A consolidated drained (CD) triaxial test was carried out on a sand sample with the known effective shear strength parameters, \( c' = 0 \) and \( \phi' = 30^\circ \). In the test, prior to the failure, when the sample was undergoing axial compression under constant cell pressure, the drainage valve was accidentally closed. At the failure, 360 kPa deviatoric stress was recorded along with 70 kPa pore water pressure. If the test is repeated without such error, and no back pressure is applied in either of the tests, what is the deviatoric stress (in kPa, in integer) at the failure? _________________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soil

1. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Sand sample effective shear strength parameters: \(c' = 0\text{ kPa}\), \(\phi' = 30^\circ\)
    • Test 1: Intended as CD, but drainage valve accidentally closed prior to failure. Constant cell pressure maintained.
      • Deviatoric stress at failure: \(q_{f1} = (\sigma_1 - \sigma_3)_{f1} = 360\text{ kPa}\)
      • Pore water pressure at failure: \(u_f = 70\text{ kPa}\)
    • Test 2: Correctly repeated as CD test (no accidental valve closure \(\implies u = 0\)). No back pressure applied in either test.
  • Aim: Find the deviatoric stress (\(q_{f2}\)) at failure in Test 2.

2. Core Concepts:

  • Effective Stress Principle: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)
  • Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion for \(c' = 0\):\[\sigma_1' = \sigma_3'\tan^2\!\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi'}{2}\right)\]
  • Deviatoric Stress: \(q = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3 = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3'\)

3. Solution Method:

  1. Use failure conditions of Test 1 to find effective cell pressure (\(\sigma_3'\)) and total cell pressure (\(\sigma_3\)).
  2. Recognize the same total cell pressure (\(\sigma_3\)) is used in Test 2.
  3. For Test 2 (true CD test), pore pressure is zero, so total stresses equal effective stresses.
  4. Apply the failure criterion to find \(\sigma_1'\) and compute \(q_{f2}\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Analyze Test 1 to find cell pressure (\(\sigma_3\)):\[N_\phi = \tan^2\!\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{30^\circ}{2}\right) = \tan^2(60^\circ) = 3\]At failure in Test 1: \(\sigma_1' = 3\sigma_3'\)\[q_{f1} = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3' = 3\sigma_3' - \sigma_3' = 2\sigma_3' = 360\text{ kPa}\]\[\sigma_3' = 180\text{ kPa}\]Total cell pressure:\[\sigma_3 = \sigma_3' + u_f = 180 + 70 = 250\text{ kPa}\]
  2. Analyze Test 2 (True CD Test):
    Same constant total cell pressure: \(\sigma_3 = 250\text{ kPa}\).
    Excess pore pressure fully dissipates, so \(u = 0\):\[\sigma_3' = \sigma_3 = 250\text{ kPa}\]
  3. Calculate Deviatoric Stress for Test 2:\[\sigma_1' = 3 \times 250 = 750\text{ kPa}\]\[q_{f2} = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3' = 750 - 250 = 500\text{ kPa}\]

5. Final Answer:

\(q_{f2} = \mathbf{500}\text{ kPa}\) | Accepted key range: 500 to 500

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q17
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Four different soils are classified as CH, ML, SP, and SW, as per the Unified Soil Classification System. Which one of the following options correctly represents their arrangement in the decreasing order of hydraulic conductivity?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Classification and Permeability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Four soil types classified under USCS: CH (Fat Clay), ML (Silt), SP (Poorly Graded Sand), SW (Well-Graded Sand).
  • Aim: Arrange these soils in decreasing order of hydraulic conductivity \(k\).

Core Concepts:

Hydraulic Conductivity (\(k\)): A measure of the ease with which water can move through pore spaces. It primarily depends on grain size, void ratio, and pore connectivity.

General Magnitude of \(k\):

  • Gravels: \(> 10^{-1}\) cm/s
  • Sands: \(10^{-1}\) to \(10^{-3}\) cm/s
  • Silts: \(10^{-3}\) to \(10^{-5}\) cm/s
  • Clays: \(< 10^{-7}\) cm/s

USCS Classification Groups:

  • SW/SP (Sands): Coarse-grained soils. High permeability.
  • ML (Silts): Fine-grained soils (low plasticity). Intermediate permeability.
  • CH (Clays): Fine-grained soils (high plasticity). Very low permeability due to high surface area and small pore spaces.

Solution Method:

  1. Compare permeability of coarse-grained soils (Sands) vs. fine-grained soils (Silts/Clays). Sands have significantly higher \(k\).
  2. Compare Silts (ML) vs. Clays (CH). Silts have larger particle sizes, hence \(k_{ML} > k_{CH}\).
  3. Analyze options based on the hierarchy: Sands > Silts > Clays.
  4. (Secondary Check) Compare SW vs SP — the critical differentiator in the given options is the relative position of ML and CH and the separation of Sands from Fines.

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish Hierarchy:
    • Sands (SW, SP) → High \(k\)
    • Silts (ML) → Low \(k\)
    • Clays (CH) → Very Low \(k\)
  2. Evaluate Options:
    OptionOrderAnalysis
    (A)SW, SP, ML, CH✓ Sands (High) → Silt (Medium) → Clay (Low). Correct physical trend.
    (B)CH, ML, SP, SW✗ Starts with Clay (lowest). This is increasing order.
    (C)SP, SW, CH, ML✗ Implies Clay (CH) is more permeable than Silt (ML). Incorrect.
    (D)ML, SP, CH, SW✗ Starts with Silt; inconsistent with Sands having highest \(k\).
  3. Conclusion: Only Option (A) respects the fundamental order \(k_{Sands} > k_{Silt} > k_{Clay}\).

Final Answer:

Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Let \(\sigma'_v\) and \(\sigma'_h\) denote the effective vertical stress and effective horizontal stress, respectively. Which one of the following conditions must be satisfied for a soil element to reach the failure state under Rankine's passive earth pressure condition?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theories

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Soil element under Rankine's passive earth pressure condition.
  • Aim: Identify the relationship between effective vertical stress \(\sigma'_v\) and effective horizontal stress \(\sigma'_h\) at failure.

Core Concepts:

Rankine's Earth Pressure Theory: Assumes a smooth vertical wall and horizontal backfill.

Passive Earth Pressure Condition:

  • The wall moves into the soil mass.
  • The horizontal stress \(\sigma'_h\) increases as the wall compresses the soil.
  • The vertical stress \(\sigma'_v\) remains constant (due to overburden).
  • At failure, horizontal stress becomes the Major Principal Stress \((\sigma_1)\), and vertical stress becomes the Minor Principal Stress \((\sigma_3)\).

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: At failure, the stress state touches the failure envelope. For passive failure, the Mohr circle expands to the right (increasing \(\sigma_h\)).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Define Stress State:
    • Vertical Stress \(\sigma'_v\) is constant.
    • Horizontal Stress \(\sigma'_h\) increases as wall pushes into soil.
  2. Identify Major/Minor Principal Stresses:
    • In passive state: Horizontal stress > Vertical stress.
    • \(\sigma_1 = \sigma'_h\), \(\quad \sigma_3 = \sigma'_v\)
  3. Evaluate Condition: Since \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_3\), we have \(\sigma'_h > \sigma'_v\), i.e., \(\sigma'_v < \sigma'_h\).
  4. Check Options:
    OptionConditionAnalysis
    (A)\(\sigma'_v < \sigma'_h\)✓ Matches the passive condition.
    (B)\(\sigma'_v > \sigma'_h\)✗ This is the Active condition.
    (C)\(\sigma'_v = \sigma'_h\)✗ This is the At-rest (\(K_0\)) condition.
    (D)Sum is zero✗ Physically impossible for effective stresses.

Final Answer:

Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Let \(\psi\) represent soil suction head and \(K\) represent hydraulic conductivity of the soil. If the soil moisture content \(\theta\) increases, which one of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Water and Permeability

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Soil moisture content \(\theta\) increases.
  • Aim: Determine the variation in soil suction head \(\psi\) and hydraulic conductivity \(K\).

Core Concepts:

Soil Water Characteristic Curve (SWCC): Describes the relationship between water content and suction.

  • Suction Head \((\psi)\): The tension or negative pressure in pore water. As the soil gets wetter (higher \(\theta\)), surface tension forces decrease. Therefore, \(\psi\) decreases.
  • Hydraulic Conductivity \((K)\): In unsaturated soils, \(K\) depends on the degree of saturation. As water content increases, more pores fill with water, increasing connectivity of water films. Therefore, \(K\) increases.

Relationship Summary:

  • \(\theta \uparrow \implies \psi \downarrow\)
  • \(\theta \uparrow \implies K \uparrow\)

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effect on Suction \((\psi)\): Dry soil has high suction (strong capillary attraction). As moisture content increases, soil approaches saturation and suction drops to zero. Thus, \(\psi\) decreases.
  2. Effect on Conductivity \((K)\): Dry soil has discontinuous water films (low \(K\)). As moisture increases, flow paths become continuous, approaching saturated hydraulic conductivity. Thus, \(K\) increases.
  3. Check Options:
    Option\(\psi\)\(K\)Analysis
    (A)DecreasesIncreases✓ Correct
    (B)IncreasesDecreases✗ Opposite trend
    (C)DecreasesDecreases✗ Incorrect for \(K\)
    (D)IncreasesIncreases✗ Incorrect for \(\psi\)

Final Answer:

Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: An uncompacted heap of soil has a volume of 10000 m³ and void ratio of 1. If the soil is compacted to a volume of 7500 m³, then the corresponding void ratio of the compacted soil is __________. (round off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Phase Relationships & Compaction

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ParameterValueUnit
    Initial volume, \(V_1\)10,000m³
    Initial void ratio, \(e_1\)1.0—
    Final volume, \(V_2\)7,500m³
    Final void ratio, \(e_2\)?—
  • Aim: Find \(e_2\) (void ratio after compaction).

Core Concepts:

Key Principle: During compaction, the volume of solids (\(V_s\)) remains constant; only voids reduce.

Phase Relationship:

\[e = \dfrac{V_v}{V_s} = \dfrac{V - V_s}{V_s} \implies V_s = \dfrac{V}{1+e}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate volume of solids (constant):\[V_s = \dfrac{V_1}{1+e_1} = \dfrac{10000}{1+1} = \dfrac{10000}{2} = 5000 \text{ m}^3\]
  2. Apply to compacted state:\[V_s = \dfrac{V_2}{1+e_2} \implies 5000 = \dfrac{7500}{1+e_2}\]
  3. Solve for \(e_2\):\[1 + e_2 = \dfrac{7500}{5000} = 1.5 \implies e_2 = 0.5\]

Sanity Check:

  • \(e_2 = 0.5 < e_1 = 1.0\) ✓ (compaction reduces void ratio)
  • \(e_2 = 0.5\) is reasonable for compacted soil (typically 0.4–0.8 for sands, 0.3–0.6 for clays).

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{e_2 = 0.5}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A concentrated vertical load of 3000 kN is applied on a horizontal ground surface. Points P and Q are at depths 1 m and 2 m below the ground, respectively, along the line of application of the load. Considering the ground to be a linearly elastic, isotropic, semi-infinite medium, the ratio of the increase in vertical stress at P to the increase in vertical stress at Q is _________. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics / Elasticity | Boussinesq Stress Distribution

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ParameterValueUnit
    Concentrated load, \(Q\)3000kN
    Depth at Point P, \(z_P\)1m
    Depth at Point Q, \(z_Q\)2m
    Both points on load axis\(r = 0\)—
  • Aim: Find the ratio \(\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_{z,P}}{\Delta\sigma_{z,Q}}\).

Core Concepts:

Boussinesq Equation (1885) for vertical stress under a point load on a semi-infinite elastic medium:

\[\Delta\sigma_z = \dfrac{3Q}{2\pi z^2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\left[1+\left(\dfrac{r}{z}\right)^2\right]^{5/2}}\]

On the load axis (\(r = 0\)):

\[\Delta\sigma_z = \dfrac{3Q}{2\pi z^2}\]

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Vertical stress at Point P (\(z = 1\) m, \(r = 0\)):\[\Delta\sigma_{z,P} = \dfrac{3 \times 3000}{2\pi \times (1)^2} = \dfrac{9000}{2\pi} = \dfrac{4500}{\pi} \text{ kN/m}^2\]
  2. Vertical stress at Point Q (\(z = 2\) m, \(r = 0\)):\[\Delta\sigma_{z,Q} = \dfrac{3 \times 3000}{2\pi \times (2)^2} = \dfrac{9000}{8\pi} = \dfrac{1125}{\pi} \text{ kN/m}^2\]
  3. Calculate ratio:\[\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_{z,P}}{\Delta\sigma_{z,Q}} = \dfrac{4500/\pi}{1125/\pi} = \dfrac{4500}{1125} = 4\]

Alternative Verification:

\[\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_{z,P}}{\Delta\sigma_{z,Q}} = \dfrac{z_Q^2}{z_P^2} = \dfrac{2^2}{1^2} = 4\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{\dfrac{\Delta\sigma_{z,P}}{\Delta\sigma_{z,Q}} = 4}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
At a site, Static Cone Penetration Test was carried out. The measured point (tip) resistance \(q_c\) was 1000 kPa at a certain depth. The friction ratio (\(f_r\)) was estimated as 1 % at the same depth.

The value of sleeve (side) friction (in kPa) at that depth was _________________. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Cone Penetration Test (CPT)

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    ParameterValueUnit
    Cone (tip) resistance, \(q_c\)1000kPa
    Friction ratio, \(f_r\)1%
  • Aim: Find sleeve (side) friction \(f_s\) in kPa.

Core Concepts:

IS 4968 (Part 3): 1976 — Method for subsurface sounding using static cone penetrometer.

Friction Ratio Definition:

\[f_r = \dfrac{f_s}{q_c} \times 100\%\]

Where \(f_s\) = sleeve (side) friction (kPa), \(q_c\) = cone resistance (kPa), \(f_r\) = friction ratio (%).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert friction ratio to decimal:\[f_r = 1\% = 0.01\]
  2. Solve for sleeve friction:\[f_s = f_r \times q_c = 0.01 \times 1000 = 10 \text{ kPa}\]

Sanity Check: Typical \(f_r\) values: 0.5%–1.5% for sands, 3%–10% for clays. \(f_s = 10\) kPa is reasonable for sandy soils with \(q_c = 1000\) kPa. ✓

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{f_s = 10 \text{ kPa}}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The correct match between the physical states of the soils given in Group I and the governing conditions given in Group II is

Group IGroup II
1.normally consolidated soilP.sensitivity > 16
2.quick clayQ.dilation angle = 0
3.sand in critical stateR.liquid limit > 50
4.clay of high plasticityS.over consolidation ratio = 1
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties and Classification

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    Group I: Normally consolidated soil, Quick clay, Sand in critical state, Clay of high plasticity.
    Group II: Sensitivity > 16, Dilation angle = 0, Liquid limit > 50%, Over consolidation ratio = 1.
  • Aim: Map each soil state in Group I to its correct governing condition in Group II.

Core Concepts & Matching:

Group I — Soil StateGroup II — ConditionJustification
