1. Normally Consolidated SoilS — OCR = 1A normally consolidated soil is currently experiencing the highest effective overburden pressure in its history, so Over Consolidation Ratio = 1 by definition.
2. Quick ClayP — Sensitivity > 16Sensitivity \(S_t\) = undisturbed UCS / remolded UCS. Clays with \(S_t > 16\) are termed "quick clays", turning into viscous fluid upon remolding.
3. Sand in Critical StateQ — Dilation angle = 0At critical state, continuous shear deformation occurs with no further volume change (constant void ratio). Zero volume change rate means dilation angle \(\psi = 0\).
4. Clay of High PlasticityR — Liquid Limit > 50%Per IS 1498, fine-grained soils with liquid limit strictly greater than 50% are classified as high plasticity (e.g., CH).

Final Answer:

1–S, 2–P, 3–Q, 4–R | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
As per Rankine's theory of earth pressure, the inclination of failure planes is \(\left(45 + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)^\circ\) with respect to the direction of the minor principal stress.

The above statement is correct for which one of the following options?
options: Only the active state and not the passive state
Only the passive state and not the active state
Both active as well as passive states

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Only the active state and not the passive state
structuredOptions.html: Only the active state and not the passive state

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Only the passive state and not the active state
structuredOptions.html: Only the passive state and not the active state

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Both active as well as passive states
structuredOptions.html: Both active as well as passive states

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theories

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Analysis
  • Given Data: Inclination of the failure plane is \(\left(45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) with respect to the direction of the minor principal stress.
  • Aim: Identify whether this statement holds for the active state, passive state, both, or neither.

Core Concepts:

  • Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: A material fails when shear stress reaches \(\tau_f = c + \sigma_n \tan\phi\).
  • Mohr's Circle Geometry: The theoretical failure plane makes an angle \(\theta_f\) with the major principal plane:\[\theta_f = 45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\]
  • Principal Planes vs. Principal Stresses: The direction of the minor principal stress \(\sigma_3\) is perpendicular to the minor principal plane, which is parallel to the major principal plane. Therefore, the angle between the failure plane and the direction of the minor principal stress equals \(\left(45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\).
  • Active vs. Passive States:
    • Active State: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_v\) (vertical), \(\sigma_3 = \sigma_h\) (horizontal).
    • Passive State: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_h\) (horizontal), \(\sigma_3 = \sigma_v\) (vertical).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Active Earth Pressure State:
    Major principal plane is horizontal. Failure plane angle with horizontal \(= 45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\).
    Direction of \(\sigma_3\) is horizontal → angle between failure plane and direction of minor principal stress \(= 45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\). ✓ Statement holds.
  2. Passive Earth Pressure State:
    Major principal plane is vertical. Failure plane angle with vertical \(= 45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\).
    Direction of \(\sigma_3\) is vertical → angle between failure plane and direction of minor principal stress \(= 45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\). ✓ Statement holds.

Conclusion: The purely geometric property of Mohr's circle dictates that the failure plane is always inclined at \(\left(45° + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)\) to the major principal plane, and hence to the direction of the minor principal stress, regardless of whether the stress state is active or passive.

Final Answer:

Both active as well as passive states | Correct Option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A square concrete pile of 10 m length is driven into a deep layer of uniform homogeneous clay. Average unconfined compressive strength of the clay, determined through laboratory tests on undisturbed samples extracted from the clay layer, is 100 kPa. If the ultimate compressive load capacity of the driven pile is 632 kN, the required width of the pile is _________ mm. (in integer)

(Bearing capacity factor \(N_c = 9\); adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.7\))
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Pile length \(L = 10\) m; unconfined compressive strength \(q_u = 100\) kPa; \(Q_u = 632\) kN; \(N_c = 9\); adhesion factor \(\alpha = 0.7\).
  • Aim: Find the required width of the square pile \(B\) (in mm).

Core Concepts:

  • Undrained Shear Strength: \(c_u = \dfrac{q_u}{2}\)
  • Ultimate Pile Capacity (IS 2911):\[Q_u = Q_{eb} + Q_{sf} = c_u \cdot N_c \cdot A_b + \alpha \cdot c_u \cdot A_s\]For a square pile of width \(B\): \(A_b = B^2\), \(A_s = 4BL\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Undrained Shear Strength:\[c_u = \dfrac{100}{2} = 50 \text{ kPa}\]
  2. Setup the equation:\[Q_{eb} = 50 \times 9 \times B^2 = 450B^2 \text{ kN}\]\[Q_{sf} = 0.7 \times 50 \times (4 \times B \times 10) = 1400B \text{ kN}\]\[450B^2 + 1400B = 632\]
  3. Solve the quadratic equation:
    Dividing by 2: \(225B^2 + 700B - 316 = 0\)
    Applying the quadratic formula:\[B = \dfrac{-700 \pm \sqrt{700^2 - 4 \times 225 \times (-316)}}{2 \times 225}\]\[B = \dfrac{-700 \pm \sqrt{490000 + 284400}}{450} = \dfrac{-700 \pm \sqrt{774400}}{450} = \dfrac{-700 \pm 880}{450}\]Taking the positive root:\[B = \dfrac{180}{450} = 0.4 \text{ m}\]
  4. Unit Conversion:\[B = 0.4 \times 1000 = 400 \text{ mm}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{B = 400 \text{ mm}}\]

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A raft foundation of 30 m × 25 m is proposed to be constructed at a depth of 8 m in a sand layer. A 25 m thick saturated clay layer exists 2 m below the base of the raft foundation. Below the clay layer, a dense sand layer exists at the site.

A 25 mm thick undisturbed sample was collected from the mid-depth of the clay layer and tested in a laboratory oedometer under double drainage condition. It was found that the soil sample had undergone 50 % consolidation settlement in 10 minutes.

The time (in days) required for 25 % consolidation settlement of the raft foundation will be _______________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation of Soils

Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data: Field clay layer: \(H_f = 25\) m, double drainage (sand above, dense sand below); Lab sample: \(H_l = 25\) mm, double drainage; Lab: \(U_1 = 50\%\) at \(t_1 = 10\) minutes; Field target: \(U_2 = 25\%\).
  • Aim: Find the time \(t_2\) (in days) for 25% consolidation in the field.

Core Concepts:

  • Terzaghi's 1D Consolidation: \(T_v = \dfrac{C_v \cdot t}{d^2}\)
  • Time Factor (for \(U \leq 60\%\)): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4}U^2\)
  • Drainage Path: For double drainage, \(d = H/2\).

Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Drainage Paths:\[d_l = \dfrac{25 \text{ mm}}{2} = 12.5 \text{ mm}, \qquad d_f = \dfrac{25 \text{ m}}{2} = 12.5 \text{ m} = 12500 \text{ mm}\]
  2. Time Factors:\[T_{v1}\,(U=0.5) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.5)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{16}\]\[T_{v2}\,(U=0.25) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.25)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{64}\]
  3. Equating \(C_v\) for lab and field:\[C_v = \dfrac{T_{v1} \cdot d_l^2}{t_1} = \dfrac{T_{v2} \cdot d_f^2}{t_2} \implies t_2 = t_1 \cdot \dfrac{T_{v2}}{T_{v1}} \cdot \left(\dfrac{d_f}{d_l}\right)^2\]
  4. Calculations:\[\dfrac{T_{v2}}{T_{v1}} = \dfrac{\pi/64}{\pi/16} = \dfrac{1}{4}\]\[\left(\dfrac{d_f}{d_l}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{12500}{12.5}\right)^2 = (1000)^2 = 10^6\]\[t_2 = 10 \text{ min} \times 0.25 \times 10^6 = 2{,}500{,}000 \text{ minutes}\]
  5. Convert to days:\[t_2 = \dfrac{2{,}500{,}000}{60 \times 24} = \dfrac{2{,}500{,}000}{1440} \approx 1736 \text{ days}\]

Final Answer:

\[\boxed{t_2 \approx 1736 \text{ days}}\] Accepted range: 1730 to 1740

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q17
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Read the following statements:

(P) While designing a shallow footing in sandy soil, monsoon season is considered for critical design in terms of bearing capacity.

(Q) For slope stability of an earthen dam, sudden drawdown is never a critical condition.

(R) In a sandy sea beach, quicksand condition can arise only if the critical hydraulic gradient exceeds the existing hydraulic gradient.

(S) The active earth thrust on a rigid retaining wall supporting homogeneous cohesionless backfill will reduce with the lowering of water table in the backfill.

Which one of the following combinations is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Bearing Capacity, Slope Stability, Seepage, Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Four statements (P, Q, R, S) related to geotechnical design.
  • Aim: Identify the correct True/False values for each statement.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Shallow footing in sandy soil: Bearing capacity reduces when water table rises due to reduced effective stress → monsoon is critical.
  • Slope stability and sudden drawdown: Rapid drawdown reduces external water pressure while high pore pressures remain inside, reducing effective stress → classical critical condition for upstream slope.
  • Quicksand condition: Occurs when upward seepage gradient \(i \ge i_c\) (critical gradient). Requires existing gradient to exceed or equal critical gradient.
  • Active earth thrust with water table lowering: Lowering water table increases effective stress, thus increasing active earth pressure (soil thrust increases).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

StatementAnalysisVerdict
(P) Monsoon is critical for shallow footing in sandy soil.Rising water table during monsoon reduces effective stress and bearing capacity. Monsoon is indeed critical.TRUE
(Q) Sudden drawdown is never a critical condition for slope stability of an earthen dam.Sudden drawdown is a classic critical condition for the upstream slope — high pore pressures remain after drawdown.FALSE
(R) Quicksand arises only if critical hydraulic gradient exceeds existing hydraulic gradient (\(i_c > i\)).Quicksand requires \(i \ge i_c\), i.e., existing gradient must equal or exceed critical. The statement reverses this condition.FALSE
(S) Active earth thrust reduces with lowering of water table in cohesionless backfill.Lowering water table increases effective vertical stress, increasing active earth pressure. Thrust increases, not reduces.FALSE

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: (P)-True, (Q)-False, (R)-False, (S)-False | Correct Option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The inside diameter of a sampler tube is 50 mm. The inside diameter of the cutting edge is kept such that the Inside Clearance Ratio (ICR) is 1.0 % to minimize the friction on the sample as the sampler tube enters into the soil.
The inside diameter (in mm) of the cutting edge is _________________.
(round off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering | Soil Exploration & Sampling

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Inside diameter of sampler tube, \(D_2 = 50 \text{ mm}\)
    • Inside Clearance Ratio, \(ICR = 1.0\%\)
  • Aim: Find inside diameter of cutting edge (\(D_1\)) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Inside Clearance Ratio (ICR) as per IS 1892: \[ICR = \dfrac{D_2 - D_1}{D_1} \times 100\% \] where \(D_1\) = inside diameter of cutting edge, \(D_2\) = inside diameter of sampler tube.

For undisturbed samples, ICR should be 1% to 3% — lower ICR minimizes sample disturbance and friction.

4. Solution Method:

Rearrange the ICR formula to solve for \(D_1\): \[D_1 = \dfrac{D_2}{1 + \dfrac{ICR}{100}} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. State the formula:
    \[D_1 = \dfrac{D_2}{1 + \dfrac{ICR}{100}} \]
  2. Substitute values:
    \[D_1 = \dfrac{50}{1 + \dfrac{1.0}{100}} = \dfrac{50}{1.01} \]
  3. Calculate:
    \[D_1 = 49.5049\ldots \approx 49.50 \text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 49.50 mm | Accepted range: 49.49 to 49.52

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A concentrically loaded isolated square footing of size 2 m × 2 m carries a concentrated vertical load of 1000 kN. Considering Boussinesq's theory of stress distribution, the maximum depth (in m) of the pressure bulb corresponding to 10 % of the vertical load intensity will be _____________. (round off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering | Stress Distribution in Soil Mass

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Footing size = \(2 \text{ m} \times 2 \text{ m}\)
    • Concentrated load, \(Q = 1000 \text{ kN}\)
    • Pressure bulb intensity = 10% of applied load intensity
  • Aim: Find maximum depth (\(z\)) of the pressure bulb in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

Boussinesq's equation for vertical stress at centerline (\(r = 0\)) under concentrated load: \[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3Q}{2\pi z^2} \]

Pressure Bulb Definition: The 10% pressure bulb corresponds to \(\sigma_z = 0.10 \times \dfrac{Q}{A}\), where \(A\) = footing area.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Footing area and load intensity:
    \[A = 2 \times 2 = 4 \text{ m}^2, \quad q = \dfrac{1000}{4} = 250 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. 10% pressure intensity:
    \[\sigma_z = 0.10 \times 250 = 25 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Rearrange Boussinesq equation for \(z\):
    \[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3Q}{2\pi z^2} \implies z = \sqrt{\dfrac{3Q}{2\pi \sigma_z}} \]
  4. Substitute values:
    \[z = \sqrt{\dfrac{3 \times 1000}{2\pi \times 25}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3000}{157.08}} = \sqrt{19.099} = 4.37 \text{ m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.37 m | Accepted range: 4.35 to 4.39

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In a triaxial unconsolidated undrained (UU) test on a saturated clay sample, the cell pressure was 100 kPa. If the deviatoric stress at failure was 150 kPa, then the undrained shear strength of the soil is ________ kPa. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering | Shear Strength of Soils

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Cell pressure, \(\sigma_3 = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Deviatoric stress at failure, \(\sigma_d = 150 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Test type: Unconsolidated Undrained (UU)
  • Aim: Find undrained shear strength (\(c_u\)) in kPa.

3. Core Concepts:

UU Triaxial Test: For saturated clay, the undrained friction angle \(\phi_u = 0\). The Mohr-Coulomb criterion simplifies to \(\tau_f = c_u\).

Key Relationships:

ParameterFormula
Major principal stress\(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 + \sigma_d\)
Undrained shear strength\(c_u = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{2} = \dfrac{\sigma_d}{2}\)
Radius of Mohr's circle\(= c_u\)

Reference: IS 2720 (Part 11)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Major principal stress:
    \[\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 + \sigma_d = 100 + 150 = 250 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Undrained shear strength:
    \[c_u = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{2} = \dfrac{\sigma_d}{2} = \dfrac{150}{2} = 75 \text{ kPa} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 75 kPa | Accepted range: 75 to 75

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Match the following in Column X with Column Y:
Column XColumn Y
(P) In a triaxial compression test, with increase of axial strain in loose sand under drained shear condition, the volumetric strain(I) decreases.
(Q) In a triaxial compression test, with increase of axial strain in loose soil under undrained shear condition, the excess pore water pressure(II) increases.
(R) In a triaxial compression test, the pore pressure parameter “B” for a saturated soil(III) remains same.
(S) For shallow strip footing in pure saturated clay, Terzaghi’s bearing capacity factor (Nq) due to surcharge(IV) is always 0.0.
(V) is always 1.0.
(VI) is always 0.5.

Which one of the following combinations is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength & Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Four statements relating to triaxial tests, pore pressure, and bearing capacity factors.
  • Aim: Match the geotechnical phenomenon in Column X with its correct behavior/value in Column Y.

3. Core Concepts & Solution Method:

  • Item (P) — Loose sand, drained condition: Under shearing, soil particles in loose sand tend to collapse into voids, resulting in volume contraction. Since the test is drained, pore water escapes freely. Physically, the volume decreases. → Matches (I).
  • Item (Q) — Loose sand, undrained condition: The loose sand structure tries to collapse similarly, but since the test is undrained, pore water cannot escape. The trapped water takes up the compressive stress, causing excess pore water pressure to increase. → Matches (II).
  • Item (R) — Skempton's Pore Pressure Parameter 'B': \(B = \Delta u / \Delta \sigma_3\). For fully saturated soils, water is virtually incompressible compared to the soil skeleton, so any applied isotropic stress is immediately carried by the pore water. Hence, \(B \approx 1.0\). → Matches (V).
  • Item (S) — Bearing Capacity Factor \(N_q\): For pure saturated clay under undrained conditions, \(\phi_u = 0^\circ\). According to Terzaghi's bearing capacity theory at \(\phi = 0^\circ\): \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1.0\), \(N_\gamma = 0\). → Matches (V).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

ItemMatches
(P) Loose sand, drained(I)
(Q) Loose sand, undrained(II)
(R) Skempton's B parameter(V)
(S) Bearing capacity factor \(N_q\) at \(\phi = 0^\circ\)(V)

Checking the options: Option (A) gives (P)-(I), (Q)-(II), (R)-(V), (S)-(V) — matches perfectly.

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: (P)-(I), (Q)-(II), (R)-(V), (S)-(V) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A soil sample is underlying a water column of height h₁, as shown in the figure. The vertical effective stresses at points A, B, and C are σ'ₐ, σ'ᵦ, and σ'꜀ respectively. Let γsat and γ' be the saturated and submerged unit weights of the soil sample, respectively, and γw be the unit weight of water. Which one of the following expressions correctly represents the sum (σ'ₐ + σ'ᵦ + σ'꜀)?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Effective Stress Principle

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Water column height above soil = \(h_1\)
    • Point A is at the soil-water interface.
    • Point B is at depth \(h_2\) below A.
    • Point C is at depth \(h_3\) below B.
    • Unit weights: \(\gamma_{sat}\) (saturated soil), \(\gamma'\) (submerged soil), \(\gamma_w\) (water).
  • Aim: Find the correct expression for \((\sigma'_A + \sigma'_B + \sigma'_C)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Principle of Effective Stress: \[\sigma' = \sigma - u \]

Total Stress (\(\sigma\)): Weight of all overlying material (soil and water) per unit area.

Pore Water Pressure (\(u\)): Hydrostatic pressure measured from the free water surface.

Submerged Unit Weight: \(\gamma' = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w\)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate total stress (\(\sigma\)) and pore water pressure (\(u\)) independently for points A, B, and C, then compute effective stress (\(\sigma'\)) for each.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective Stress at Point A:
    \(\sigma_A = h_1 \gamma_w\), \quad \(u_A = h_1 \gamma_w\)
    \[\sigma'_A = h_1 \gamma_w - h_1 \gamma_w = 0 \]
  2. Effective Stress at Point B:
    \(\sigma_B = h_1 \gamma_w + h_2 \gamma_{sat}\), \quad \(u_B = (h_1 + h_2)\gamma_w\)
    \[\sigma'_B = (h_1 \gamma_w + h_2 \gamma_{sat}) - (h_1 \gamma_w + h_2 \gamma_w) = h_2(\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w) = h_2 \gamma' \]
  3. Effective Stress at Point C:
    \(\sigma_C = h_1 \gamma_w + (h_2 + h_3)\gamma_{sat}\), \quad \(u_C = (h_1 + h_2 + h_3)\gamma_w\)
    \[\sigma'_C = (h_2 + h_3)(\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w) = (h_2 + h_3)\gamma' \]
  4. Summation:
    \[\sigma'_A + \sigma'_B + \sigma'_C = 0 + h_2\gamma' + (h_2 + h_3)\gamma' = (2h_2 + h_3)\gamma' \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \((2h_2 + h_3)\gamma'\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A group of total 16 piles are arranged in a square grid format. The center-to-center spacing (s) between adjacent piles is 3 m. The diameter (d) and length of embedment of each pile are 1 m and 20 m, respectively. The design capacity of each pile is 1000 kN in the vertical downward direction. The pile group efficiency (ηg) is given by
\[ \eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{\theta}{90} \left[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn} \right] \]
where m and n are number of rows and columns in the plan grid of pile arrangement, and \( \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{s}\right) \).

The design value of the pile group capacity (in kN) in the vertical downward direction is _________________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total number of piles = 16, in a \(4 \times 4\) square grid (\(m = 4\) rows, \(n = 4\) columns)
    • Spacing between piles, \(s = 3 \text{ m}\)
    • Diameter of each pile, \(d = 1 \text{ m}\)
    • Capacity of single pile, \(Q_u = 1000 \text{ kN}\)
    • Group efficiency formula: Converse-Labarre equation
  • Aim: Calculate the pile group capacity (\(Q_{ug}\)) in kN.

3. Core Concepts:

Pile Group Efficiency (\(\eta_g\)): Due to overlapping stress zones of closely spaced friction piles, group capacity is often less than the sum of individual capacities.

Converse-Labarre Formula: \[ \eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{\theta}{90} \left[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn}\right] \] where \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{s}\right)\) in degrees.

Pile Group Capacity: \(Q_{ug} = \eta_g \times N \times Q_u\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate angle \(\theta\).
  2. Substitute into the efficiency formula.
  3. Compute the group capacity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(\theta\):
    \[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 18.4349^\circ \]
  2. Bracket Term:
    \[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn} = \dfrac{(3)(4) + (3)(4)}{16} = \dfrac{12 + 12}{16} = 1.5 \]
  3. Group Efficiency:
    \[\eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{18.4349}{90} \times 1.5 = 1 - 0.20483 \times 1.5 = 1 - 0.30725 = 0.69275 \]
  4. Group Capacity:
    \[Q_{ug} = 0.69275 \times 16 \times 1000 = 11{,}084 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 11084 kN | Accepted key range: 11000 to 11200

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A saturated compressible clay layer of thickness h is sandwiched between two sand layers, as shown in the figure. Initially, the total vertical stress and pore water pressure at point P, which is located at the mid-depth of the clay layer, were 150 kPa and 25 kPa, respectively. Construction of a building caused an additional total vertical stress of 100 kPa at P. When the vertical effective stress at P is 175 kPa, the percentage of consolidation in the clay layer at P is _________. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Point P at mid-depth of a clay layer (double drainage)
    • Initial total vertical stress, \(\sigma_0 = 150 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Initial pore water pressure, \(u_0 = 25 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Additional total stress from building, \(\Delta\sigma = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Current vertical effective stress, \(\sigma'_t = 175 \text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Find the percentage of consolidation (\(U_z\)) at point P.

3. Core Concepts:

Principle of Effective Stress: \(\sigma = \sigma' + u\)

Consolidation Phenomenon: Upon loading saturated clay, the initial increase in total stress (\(\Delta\sigma\)) is entirely borne by pore water (\(\Delta u_i = \Delta\sigma\)). As water escapes, excess pore pressure dissipates and transfers to the soil skeleton.

Degree of Consolidation: \[U_z = \dfrac{\sigma'_t - \sigma'_0}{\sigma'_f - \sigma'_0} \times 100\% \]

4. Solution Method:

Method 1 (Effective Stress): Compute \(\sigma'_0\) and \(\sigma'_f\), then interpolate using \(\sigma'_t\).
Method 2 (Pore Pressure): Determine initial and current excess pore pressure to calculate \(U_z\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_0\)):
    \[\sigma'_0 = 150 - 25 = 125 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Ultimate Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_f\)):
    \[\sigma'_f = \sigma'_0 + \Delta\sigma = 125 + 100 = 225 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Degree of Consolidation:
    \[U_z = \dfrac{175 - 125}{225 - 125} \times 100\% = \dfrac{50}{100} \times 100\% = 50\% \]

Validation via Pore Pressure Method:
Current total stress: \(\sigma_t = 150 + 100 = 250 \text{ kPa}\)
Current pore pressure: \(u_t = 250 - 175 = 75 \text{ kPa}\)
Current excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_t = 75 - 25 = 50 \text{ kPa}\)
Initial excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_i = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
\[U_z = \left(1 - \dfrac{50}{100}\right) \times 100\% = 50\% \checkmark \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50% | Accepted key range: 50 to 50

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q7
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In an Oedometer apparatus, a specimen of fully saturated clay has been consolidated under a vertical pressure of 50 kN/m² and is presently at equilibrium. The effective stress and pore water pressure immediately on increasing the vertical stress to 150 kN/m², respectively are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Fully saturated clay specimen
    • Initial vertical stress (at equilibrium): \(\sigma_0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • New total vertical stress: \(\sigma_1 = 150\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Find effective stress (\(\sigma'\)) and pore water pressure (\(u\)) immediately after increasing the vertical stress.

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Stress Principle (Terzaghi): \(\sigma = \sigma' + u\)

Undrained Loading: Immediately upon load application on a fully saturated clay, water cannot drain instantly. Since Skempton's pore pressure parameter \(B \approx 1\) for fully saturated clay, the entire increment in total stress is initially carried by pore water.\[\Delta u = B \cdot \Delta\sigma = 1 \times \Delta\sigma \]

Key Result: Effective stress does not change instantly under undrained loading.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define initial equilibrium state.
  2. Calculate excess pore pressure generated by the load increment.
  3. Compute absolute conditions immediately post-loading.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Initial Equilibrium State
    • Total stress: \(\sigma_0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_0 = 0\) (equilibrium)
    • Total pore pressure: \(u_0 = 0\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Effective stress: \(\sigma'_0 = 50 - 0 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  2. Step 2: Instantaneous Stress Changes\[\Delta\sigma = 150 - 50 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[\Delta u = B \cdot \Delta\sigma = 1 \times 100 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Step 3: Immediate Post-Loading Values\[u = u_0 + \Delta u = 0 + 100 = 100\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[\sigma'_1 = \sigma_1 - u = 150 - 100 = 50\text{ kN/m}^2 \](Effective stress remains unchanged immediately after undrained loading.)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\sigma' = 50\text{ kN/m}^2\) and \(u = 100\text{ kN/m}^2\)  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A partially-saturated soil sample has natural moisture content of 25% and bulk unit weight of 18.5 kN/m³. The specific gravity of soil solids is 2.65 and unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³. The unit weight of the soil sample on full saturation is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Natural moisture content, \(w = 25\% = 0.25\)
    • Bulk unit weight, \(\gamma_t = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Specific gravity of solids, \(G_s = 2.65\)
    • Unit weight of water, \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Determine the saturated unit weight (\(\gamma_{sat}\)) upon full saturation.

3. Core Concepts:

\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{\gamma_t}{1+w}, \qquad \gamma_d = \dfrac{G_s \gamma_w}{1+e}, \qquad \gamma_{sat} = \dfrac{(G_s + e)\gamma_w}{1+e} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate dry unit weight \(\gamma_d\).
  2. Use \(\gamma_d\) to find void ratio \(e\).
  3. Use \(e\) and \(G_s\) to compute \(\gamma_{sat}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Dry Unit Weight\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{18.5}{1 + 0.25} = \dfrac{18.5}{1.25} = 14.80\text{ kN/m}^3 \]
  2. Step 2: Void Ratio\[14.80 = \dfrac{2.65 \times 9.81}{1+e} \implies 1+e = \dfrac{25.9965}{14.80} = 1.7565 \implies e = 0.7565 \]
  3. Step 3: Saturated Unit Weight\[\gamma_{sat} = \dfrac{(2.65 + 0.7565) \times 9.81}{1.7565} = \dfrac{3.4065 \times 9.81}{1.7565} = \dfrac{33.4178}{1.7565} \approx 19.03\text{ kN/m}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 19.03 kN/m³  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The cohesion (c), angle of internal friction (φ) and unit weight (γ) of a soil are 15 kPa, 20° and 17.5 kN/m³, respectively. The maximum depth of unsupported excavation in the soil (in m, round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure & Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Cohesion, \(c = 15\text{ kPa}\)
    • Angle of internal friction, \(\phi = 20^\circ\)
    • Unit weight of soil, \(\gamma = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the maximum depth of unsupported excavation (\(H_c\)) in metres.

3. Core Concepts:

Active Earth Pressure (\(c\)-\(\phi\) soil, Rankine's):\[p_a = \gamma z K_a - 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]

Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure:\[K_a = \tan^2\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \implies \sqrt{K_a} = \tan\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \]

Critical Depth Formula: The maximum unsupported height equals twice the depth of the tension crack.\[H_c = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma}\tan\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute \(\sqrt{K_a}\) using \(\phi = 20^\circ\).
  2. Substitute \(c\), \(\gamma\), and \(\sqrt{K_a}\) into the formula.
  3. Round to two decimal places.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Calculate \(\sqrt{K_a}\)\[\sqrt{K_a} = \tan\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{20^\circ}{2}\right) = \tan(35^\circ) \approx 0.7002 \]
  2. Step 2: Calculate \(H_c\)\[H_c = \dfrac{4 \times 15}{17.5 \times 0.7002} = \dfrac{60}{12.2535} = 4.8965\text{ m} \approx 4.90\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.90 m  |  Accepted key range: 4.80 to 5.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Based on drained triaxial shear tests on sands and clays, the representative variations of volumetric strain (ΔV/V) with the shear strain (γ) is shown in the figure.



Choose the CORRECT option regarding the representative behaviour exhibited by Curve P and Curve Q.
options: Curve P represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay
Curve P represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay
Curve P represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay
Curve P represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Curve P represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay
structuredOptions.html: Curve P represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: Curve P represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay
structuredOptions.html: Curve P represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Curve P represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay
structuredOptions.html: Curve P represents loose sand and overconsolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and normally consolidated clay

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Curve P represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay
structuredOptions.html: Curve P represents loose sand and normally consolidated clay, while Curve Q represents dense sand and overconsolidated clay

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Drained triaxial shear test graph depicting Volumetric strain (\(\Delta V/V\)) vs. Shear strain (\(\gamma\)).
    • Curve P: shows initial slight compression followed by substantial expansion (dilation).
    • Curve Q: shows continuous compression.
  • Aim: Identify the representative soil types that exhibit the behaviors of Curve P and Curve Q.

3. Core Concepts:

Dense Sand & Overconsolidated (OC) Clay: These soils exist in a closely packed state. Upon shearing, particles are forced to ride up and roll over each other, leading to an overall increase in volume. This phenomenon is called dilation (expansion).

Loose Sand & Normally Consolidated (NC) Clay: These soils have a highly porous, loosely packed structure. Under shear stress, the loose soil skeleton tends to collapse and rearrange into a denser packing, leading to a continuous decrease in volume (compression).

4. Solution Method:

Observe the direction of the plotted volumetric strain for both curves.

  • The upward direction on the y-axis represents Expansion (negative volumetric strain).
  • The downward direction represents Compression (positive volumetric strain).

Match the observed behavior with the fundamental soil mechanics principles.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Analyze Curve P. The curve moves downwards slightly (initial elastic compression) and then steeply upwards into the expansion zone. Therefore, Curve P corresponds to dilative soils: Dense sand and overconsolidated clay.
  2. Step 2: Analyze Curve Q. The curve moves continuously downwards into the compression zone. Therefore, Curve Q corresponds to compressive soils: Loose sand and normally consolidated clay.
  3. Step 3: Compare with options. Option (A) states Curve P: dense sand and OC clay; Curve Q: loose sand and NC clay — this matches our deduction.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The soil profile at a construction site is shown in the figure (not to scale). Ground water table (GWT) is at 5 m below the ground level at present. An old well data shows that the ground water table was as low as 10 m below the ground level in the past. Take unit weight of water, \( \gamma_w = 9.81 \) kN/m³.



The overconsolidation ratio (OCR) (round off to two decimal places) at the mid-point of the clay layer is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation (Overconsolidation Ratio)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Current Ground Water Table (GWT) depth = \(5\text{ m}\)
    • Past maximum GWT depth = \(10\text{ m}\)
    • \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Soil Profile:
      LayerDepth (m)SoilUnit Weight
      10 – 5Sand\(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      25 – 15Sand\(\gamma_{sat} = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      315 – 23 (8 m thick)Clay\(\gamma_{sat} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Overconsolidation Ratio (OCR) at the mid-point of the clay layer (depth \(= 15 + 8/2 = 19\text{ m}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Effective Stress Principle: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\), where \(\sigma'\) is effective stress, \(\sigma\) is total stress, and \(u\) is pore water pressure.

Overconsolidation Ratio (OCR):\[OCR = \dfrac{\sigma'_c}{\sigma'_0} \]where \(\sigma'_c\) is the maximum past effective stress and \(\sigma'_0\) is the present effective stress.

Standard Assumption: When the water table drops, the soil that is no longer submerged drains and its unit weight reverts to \(\gamma_{bulk}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Locate the point of interest: mid-point of the clay layer at \(z = 19\text{ m}\).
  2. Calculate present effective stress (\(\sigma'_0\)) using current GWT at \(5\text{ m}\).
  3. Calculate past maximum effective stress (\(\sigma'_c\)) using past GWT at \(10\text{ m}\), applying \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\) for the \(5\text{ m}\) to \(10\text{ m}\) zone.
  4. Compute the OCR.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Point of Interest
    Mid-point of clay layer: \(z = 15 + \dfrac{8}{2} = 19\text{ m}\)
  2. Step 2: Present Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_0\)) — GWT at 5 m\[\sigma_0 = (5 \times 17.5) + (10 \times 18.5) + (4 \times 17) = 87.5 + 185.0 + 68.0 = 340.5\text{ kPa} \]\[u_0 = (19 - 5) \times 9.81 = 14 \times 9.81 = 137.34\text{ kPa} \]\[\sigma'_0 = 340.5 - 137.34 = 203.16\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Step 3: Past Maximum Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_c\)) — Past GWT at 10 m
    Sand from \(5\text{ m}\) to \(10\text{ m}\) is drained; apply \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17.5\text{ kN/m}^3\) to entire \(0\)–\(10\text{ m}\) zone.\[\sigma_c = (10 \times 17.5) + (5 \times 18.5) + (4 \times 17) = 175.0 + 92.5 + 68.0 = 335.5\text{ kPa} \]\[u_c = (19 - 10) \times 9.81 = 9 \times 9.81 = 88.29\text{ kPa} \]\[\sigma'_c = 335.5 - 88.29 = 247.21\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Step 4: Calculate OCR\[OCR = \dfrac{\sigma'_c}{\sigma'_0} = \dfrac{247.21}{203.16} = 1.2168 \approx 1.22 \]

Note: If the \(5\)–\(10\text{ m}\) layer is assumed to remain saturated due to capillary action (\(\gamma = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)), then \(\sigma'_c = 252.21\text{ kPa}\) and \(OCR = 1.24\). The official GATE answer range (1.18–1.26) accommodates both interpretations; reverting to bulk unit weight is the most standard approach.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.22  |  Accepted key range: 1.18 to 1.26

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A retaining wall of height 10 m with clay backfill is shown in the figure (not to scale). Weight of the retaining wall is 5000 kN per m acting at 3.3 m from the toe of the retaining wall. The interface friction angle between base of the retaining wall and the base soil is 20°. The depth of clay in front of the retaining wall is 2.0 m. The properties of the clay backfill and the clay placed in front of the retaining wall are the same. Assume that the tension crack is filled with water. Use Rankine’s earth pressure theory. Take unit weight of water, γw = 9.81 kN/m³.



The factor of safety (round off to two decimal places) against sliding failure of the retaining wall after ignoring the passive earth pressure will be ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure & Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Wall height, \(H = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Weight of wall, \(W = 5000\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Base interface friction angle, \(\delta = 20^\circ\)
    • Clay backfill: \(\gamma = 17.2\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi = 0^\circ\), \(c = 30\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Tension crack filled with water (\(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\))
    • Passive earth pressure is ignored.
  • Aim: Find the Factor of Safety (FOS) against sliding failure.

3. Core Concepts:

Rankine's Active Earth Pressure (Cohesive Soil): For \(\phi = 0^\circ\), \(K_a = 1\).
Active pressure at depth \(z\): \(p_a = \gamma z - 2c\)

Depth of Tension Crack (\(z_c\)): Depth where active pressure = 0.\[z_c = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma} \]

Hydrostatic Force in Tension Crack (\(P_w\)): Water in the tension crack exerts an outward lateral hydrostatic force.

Factor of Safety against Sliding:\[FOS = \dfrac{\text{Resisting Forces } (F_R)}{\text{Driving Forces } (F_D)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the depth of the tension crack \(z_c\).
  2. Calculate the active earth thrust \(P_a\) (acting from \(z_c\) to \(H\)).
  3. Calculate the water thrust \(P_w\) from the tension crack.
  4. Total driving force \(F_D = P_a + P_w\).
  5. Resisting force \(F_R = W\tan(\delta)\). (Note: Base width \(B\) and adhesion factor are not provided, so base adhesion is not added.)
  6. Compute \(FOS = F_R / F_D\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Depth of Tension Crack (\(z_c\))\[z_c = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma} = \dfrac{2 \times 30}{17.2} = 3.4884\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Active Earth Thrust (\(P_a\))
    Pressure at the base (\(z = 10\text{ m}\)):\[p_{a,base} = \gamma H - 2c = (17.2 \times 10) - (2 \times 30) = 172 - 60 = 112\text{ kN/m}^2 \]The pressure distribution is triangular from 0 at \(z_c\) to \(112\text{ kN/m}^2\) at \(H\):\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 112 \times (10 - 3.4884) = 56 \times 6.5116 = 364.65\text{ kN/m} \]
  3. Step 3: Water Thrust in Tension Crack (\(P_w\))\[P_w = \dfrac{1}{2}\gamma_w z_c^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9.81 \times (3.4884)^2 = 59.69\text{ kN/m} \]
  4. Step 4: Total Driving Force (\(F_D\))\[F_D = P_a + P_w = 364.65 + 59.69 = 424.34\text{ kN/m} \]
  5. Step 5: Resisting Force (\(F_R\))\[F_R = W\tan\delta = 5000 \times \tan(20^\circ) = 5000 \times 0.36397 = 1819.85\text{ kN/m} \]
  6. Step 6: Factor of Safety\[FOS = \dfrac{F_R}{F_D} = \dfrac{1819.85}{424.34} = 4.29 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.29  |  Accepted key range: 4.20 to 4.35

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A combined trapezoidal footing of length L supports two identical square columns (P₁ and P₂) of size 0.5 m × 0.5 m, as shown in the figure. The columns P₁ and P₂ carry loads of 2000 kN and 1500 kN, respectively.



If the stress beneath the footing is uniform, the length of the combined footing L (in m, round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Shallow Foundations (Combined Footing)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Trapezoidal footing length = \(L\)
    • Column loads: \(P_1 = 2000\text{ kN}\), \(P_2 = 1500\text{ kN}\) (both \(0.5\text{ m} \times 0.5\text{ m}\))
    • Center-to-center distance between columns = \(5\text{ m}\)
    • Left edge width, \(a = 5\text{ m}\); Right edge width, \(b = 1.5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Determine the length \(L\) such that the soil bearing stress beneath the footing is strictly uniform.

3. Core Concepts:

Condition for Uniform Pressure: The resultant of all applied vertical column loads must coincide with the geometric centroid of the footing area.

Centroid of a Trapezoid (distance \(\bar{x}_{area}\) from the base of width \(a\)):\[\bar{x}_{area} = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{2b + a}{a + b}\right) \]where \(L\) is the length (height) of the trapezoid.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Place the reference origin at the extreme left edge of the footing.
  2. Locate column \(P_1\): center at \(x_1 = 0.5/2 = 0.25\text{ m}\) from the left edge.
  3. Locate column \(P_2\): center at \(x_2 = 0.25 + 5 = 5.25\text{ m}\) from the left edge.
  4. Find the Center of Gravity of loads (\(\bar{x}_{load}\)).
  5. Equate \(\bar{x}_{load}\) to \(\bar{x}_{area}\) and solve for \(L\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Position of Resultant Load (\(\bar{x}_{load}\))
    Taking moments about the extreme left edge:\[\bar{x}_{load} = \dfrac{P_1 x_1 + P_2 x_2}{P_1 + P_2} = \dfrac{2000(0.25) + 1500(5.25)}{2000 + 1500} = \dfrac{500 + 7875}{3500} = \dfrac{8375}{3500} = 2.3928\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Area Centroid of Trapezoid (\(\bar{x}_{area}\))
    With \(a = 5\text{ m}\) (left edge) and \(b = 1.5\text{ m}\) (right edge):\[\bar{x}_{area} = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{2(1.5) + 5}{5 + 1.5}\right) = \dfrac{L}{3}\left(\dfrac{8}{6.5}\right) = \dfrac{8L}{19.5} \]
  3. Step 3: Equate and Solve for \(L\)\[\bar{x}_{load} = \bar{x}_{area} \]\[2.3928 = \dfrac{8L}{19.5} \]\[L = 2.3928 \times \dfrac{19.5}{8} = 5.8325\text{ m} \approx 5.83\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5.83 m  |  Accepted key range: 5.70 to 5.90

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
An unsupported slope of height 15 m is shown in the figure (not to scale), in which the slope face makes an angle 50° with the horizontal. The slope material comprises purely cohesive soil having undrained cohesion 75 kPa. A trial slip circle KLM, with a radius 25 m, passes through the crest and toe of the slope and it subtends an angle 60° at its center O. The weight of the active soil mass (W, bounded by KLMN) is 2500 kN/m, which is acting at a horizontal distance of 10 m from the toe of the slope. Consider the water table to be present at a very large depth from the ground surface.



Considering the trial slip circle KLM, the factor of safety against the failure of slope under undrained condition (round off to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stability of Slopes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Slope height \(H = 15\text{ m}\)
    • Undrained cohesion \(c_u = 75\text{ kPa}\), purely cohesive (\(\phi_u = 0^\circ\))
    • Radius of slip circle \(R = 25\text{ m}\)
    • Angle subtended by slip circle at center O, \(\theta = 60^\circ\)
    • Weight of active soil mass \(W = 2500\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Horizontal distance of \(W\) from the toe \(= 10\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Factor of Safety (FOS) against slope failure under undrained conditions.

3. Core Concepts:

Swedish Circle Method (Undrained Analysis): For purely cohesive soil (\(\phi = 0\)), the resisting moment is derived purely from cohesion acting along the arc length of the slip circle.\[M_R = c_u \cdot L \cdot R \]where \(L = R \cdot \theta_{rad}\) is the arc length.

Actuating (Driving) Moment:\[M_A = W \cdot \bar{x} \]where \(\bar{x}\) is the horizontal distance from the center of rotation O to the line of action of \(W\).

Factor of Safety:\[FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_A} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Interpretation: The driving moment \(M_A\) requires the horizontal distance of \(W\) from center O. Based on the diagram, O lies vertically above the toe K, so the lever arm equals the given horizontal distance from the toe: \(\bar{x} = 10\text{ m}\).
    (Note: If O is strictly above the toe, the vertical drop \(R - R\cos(60^\circ) = 12.5\text{ m}\) technically differs from the stated height of 15 m. In such GATE ambiguities, the explicitly labelled moment arm parameter (10 m) takes precedence.)
  2. Calculate arc length \(L\).
  3. Calculate Resisting Moment \(M_R\) and Actuating Moment \(M_A\).
  4. Divide \(M_R\) by \(M_A\) to obtain FOS.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Arc Length Calculation\[\theta_{rad} = 60^\circ \times \dfrac{\pi}{180^\circ} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians} \]\[L = R \cdot \theta_{rad} = 25 \times \dfrac{\pi}{3} = 26.1799\text{ m} \]
  2. Step 2: Resisting Moment (\(M_R\))\[M_R = c_u \cdot L \cdot R = 75 \times 26.1799 \times 25 = 49{,}087.39\text{ kN·m/m} \]
  3. Step 3: Actuating Moment (\(M_A\))\[M_A = W \cdot \bar{x} = 2500 \times 10 = 25{,}000\text{ kN·m/m} \]
  4. Step 4: Factor of Safety\[FOS = \dfrac{M_R}{M_A} = \dfrac{49{,}087.39}{25{,}000} = 1.963 \approx 1.96 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.96  |  Accepted key range: 1.94 to 1.98

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q10
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The most appropriate triaxial test to assess the long-term stability of an excavated clay slope is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics – Shear Strength / Triaxial Testing

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Scenario: Long-term stability of an excavated clay slope.
  • Aim: Select the most appropriate triaxial test for this condition.

3. Core Concepts:

Long-Term vs Short-Term Stability in Clay: Excavation induces negative excess pore water pressure (suction). In the long term, water seeps in, suction dissipates, pore pressures return to equilibrium, and effective stress is minimized — this is the critical condition.

Triaxial Tests:

  • Consolidated Drained (CD): Full drainage during consolidation and shearing. Yields effective stress parameters \(c'\) and \(\phi'\). Simulates long-term drained conditions.
  • Unconsolidated Undrained (UU): No drainage allowed. Yields total stress parameters. Simulates short-term (end-of-construction) conditions.
  • Consolidated Undrained (CU): Simulates rapid loading after initial consolidation (e.g., rapid drawdown).

4. Solution Method:

Long-term stability → excess pore pressures fully dissipated → drained condition → requires a Consolidated Drained (CD) test to determine \(c'\) and \(\phi'\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Consolidated Drained (CD) test | Correct option: (A)

  • Aim: Expand the symbol into its correct descriptive classification.

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The internal (\( d_i \)) and external (\( d_o \)) diameters of a Shelby sampler are 48 mm and 52 mm, respectively. The area ratio (\( A_r \)) of the sampler (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Exploration – Area Ratio of Sampler

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Internal diameter: \(D_i = 48\text{ mm}\)
    • External diameter: \(D_o = 52\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the area ratio (\(A_r\)) of the Shelby sampler in %, rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Area Ratio (\(A_r\)): Represents the volume of soil displaced by the sampler tube relative to the sample volume — a measure of soil disturbance.\[A_r = \dfrac{D_o^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2} \times 100\% \]

4. Solution Method:

Direct substitution of \(D_o\) and \(D_i\) into the formula, using the difference of squares shortcut.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Numerator (difference of squares):\[D_o^2 - D_i^2 = (52-48)(52+48) = 4\times100 = 400 \]
  2. Denominator:\[D_i^2 = 48^2 = 2304 \]
  3. Area Ratio:\[A_r = \dfrac{400}{2304}\times100 = \dfrac{40{,}000}{2304} \approx 17.3611\% \approx 17.36\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 17.36% | Accepted key range: 17.25 to 17.45

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A clay layer of thickness H has a preconsolidation pressure \( p_c \) and an initial void ratio \( e_0 \). The initial effective overburden stress at the mid-height of the layer is \( p_0 \). At the same location, the increment in effective stress due to applied external load is \( \Delta p \). The compression and swelling indices of the clay are \( C_c \) and \( C_s \), respectively. If \( p_0 < p_c < (p_0 + \Delta p) \), then the correct expression to estimate the consolidation settlement (\( s_c \)) of the clay layer is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Thickness of clay layer: \(H\)
    • Preconsolidation pressure: \(p_c\)
    • Initial void ratio: \(e_0\)
    • Initial effective overburden stress: \(p_0\)
    • Increment in effective stress: \(\Delta p\)
    • Stress condition: \(p_0 < p_c < (p_0 + \Delta p)\)
    • Compression index: \(C_c\)
    • Swelling (or Recompression) index: \(C_s\)
  • Aim: Identify the correct expression to estimate the consolidation settlement (\(s_c\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Overconsolidated Soil Behavior: The soil is currently at an effective stress \(p_0\) which is less than its historical maximum \(p_c\). Thus, it is in an overconsolidated state.

Two-Stage Settlement: Since the final stress \((p_0 + \Delta p)\) exceeds the preconsolidation pressure \(p_c\), the settlement will occur in two distinct phases:

  1. Recompression Phase (from \(p_0\) to \(p_c\)): The soil compresses along the recompression/swelling curve. This phase uses the swelling index (\(C_s\)).
  2. Virgin Compression Phase (from \(p_c\) to \(p_0 + \Delta p\)): Once the stress exceeds \(p_c\), the soil behaves as normally consolidated and compresses along the virgin consolidation line. This phase uses the compression index (\(C_c\)).

Formula:\[ s_c = \dfrac{H}{1+e_0} \left[C_s \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{p_c}{p_0}\right) + C_c \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{p_0 + \Delta p}{p_c}\right) \right] \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Combine the terms for both phases of consolidation.
  2. Factor out the common multiplier \(\dfrac{H}{1+e_0}\).
  3. Match the derived equation with the given options.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Recompression settlement (\(s_{c1}\)):\[s_{c1} = \dfrac{H}{1+e_0}\, C_s \log\left(\dfrac{p_c}{p_0}\right) \]
  2. Virgin compression settlement (\(s_{c2}\)):\[s_{c2} = \dfrac{H}{1+e_0}\, C_c \log\left(\dfrac{p_0 + \Delta p}{p_c}\right) \]
  3. Total settlement (\(s_c\)):\[ s_c = \dfrac{H}{1+e_0} \left[C_s \log\left(\dfrac{p_c}{p_0}\right) + C_c \log\left(\dfrac{p_0 + \Delta p}{p_c}\right) \right] \]
  4. The derived expression exactly matches Option (B).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{H}{1+e_0}\left[C_s \log\left(\dfrac{p_c}{p_0}\right) + C_c \log\left(\dfrac{p_0+\Delta p}{p_c}\right)\right]\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: From laboratory investigations, the liquid limit, plastic limit, natural moisture content and flow index of a soil specimen are obtained as 60%, 27%, 32% and 27, respectively. The corresponding toughness index and liquidity index of the soil specimen, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Index Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Liquid Limit (\(w_L\)): \(60\%\)
    • Plastic Limit (\(w_P\)): \(27\%\)
    • Natural Moisture Content (\(w_n\)): \(32\%\)
    • Flow Index (\(I_f\)): \(27\)
  • Aim: Determine the Toughness Index (\(I_T\)) and Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)) of the soil.

3. Core Concepts:

Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)): The range of moisture content over which the soil remains in a plastic state.\[I_P = w_L - w_P \]

Toughness Index (\(I_T\)): Ratio of plasticity index to flow index. It indicates the shear strength of soil at its plastic limit.\[I_T = \dfrac{I_P}{I_f} \]

Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)): Indicates the current state (consistency) of the soil based on its natural moisture content relative to its plastic and liquid limits.\[I_L = \dfrac{w_n - w_P}{I_P} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(I_P\) using the given \(w_L\) and \(w_P\).
  2. Calculate \(I_T\) by dividing \(I_P\) by \(I_f\).
  3. Calculate \(I_L\) using \(w_n\), \(w_P\), and the computed \(I_P\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)):\[I_P = 60\% - 27\% = 33\% \]
  2. Calculate Toughness Index (\(I_T\)):\[I_T = \dfrac{33}{27} = \dfrac{11}{9} \approx 1.22 \]
  3. Calculate Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)):\[I_L = \dfrac{32\% - 27\%}{33\%} = \dfrac{5}{33} \approx 0.15 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.22 and 0.15 | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A rectangular footing of size 2.8 m × 3.5 m is embedded in a clay layer and a vertical load is placed with an eccentricity of 0.8 m as shown in the figure (not to scale). Take Bearing capacity factors: \( N_c = 5.14 \), \( N_q = 1.0 \), and \( N_\gamma = 0.0 \); Shape factors: \( s_c = 1.16 \), \( s_q = 1.0 \) and \( s_\gamma = 1.0 \); Depth factors: \( d_c = 1.1 \), \( d_q = 1.0 \) and \( d_\gamma = 1.0 \); and Inclination factors: \( i_c = 1.0 \) and \( i_q = 1.0 \) and \( i_\gamma = 1.0 \).



Using Meyerhoff’s method, the load (in kN, round off to two decimal places) that can be applied on the footing with a factor of safety of 2.5 is ______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Footing dimensions: \(B = 2.8\text{ m}\), \(L = 3.5\text{ m}\)
    • Eccentricity of load: \(e = 0.8\text{ m}\) (along width direction)
    • Foundation depth: \(D_f = 1.5\text{ m}\)
    • Soil properties (Clay): \(\gamma = 18.2\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\phi = 0^\circ\), \(c = 40\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Bearing capacity factors: \(N_c = 5.14\), \(N_q = 1.0\), \(N_\gamma = 0.0\)
    • Shape factors: \(s_c = 1.16\), \(s_q = 1.0\), \(s_\gamma = 1.0\)
    • Depth factors: \(d_c = 1.1\), \(d_q = 1.0\), \(d_\gamma = 1.0\)
    • Inclination factors: \(i_c = 1.0\), \(i_q = 1.0\), \(i_\gamma = 1.0\)
    • Factor of Safety (FOS): \(2.5\)
  • Aim: Calculate the net safe vertical load (in kN) that can be applied to the footing.

3. Core Concepts:

Meyerhof's Effective Area Method: When a foundation is subjected to an eccentric load, effective dimensions must be used.

  • Effective width: \(B' = B - 2e\)
  • Effective length: \(L' = L\)
  • Effective area: \(A' = B' \times L'\)

Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_u\)):\[q_u = cN_c s_c d_c i_c + qN_q s_q d_q i_q + 0.5\gamma B' N_\gamma s_\gamma d_\gamma i_\gamma \]

Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_{nu}\)):\[q_{nu} = q_u - q \]

Net Safe Load (\(Q_{safe}\)):\[Q_{safe} = \dfrac{q_{nu}}{FOS} \times A' \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the effective footing dimensions (\(B',\, L'\)).
  2. Calculate the ultimate bearing capacity \(q_u\) using the provided factors.
  3. Find the net ultimate bearing capacity \(q_{nu}\) by subtracting overburden stress.
  4. Apply FOS to calculate net safe bearing capacity \(q_{ns}\).
  5. Multiply \(q_{ns}\) by effective area \(A'\) to get the safe load.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective Dimensions:\[B' = 2.8 - 2(0.8) = 1.2\text{ m}, \quad L' = 3.5\text{ m} \]\[A' = 1.2 \times 3.5 = 4.2\text{ m}^2 \]
  2. Surcharge Pressure (\(q\)):\[q = \gamma \times D_f = 18.2 \times 1.5 = 27.3\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_u\)):
    Since \(\phi = 0^\circ\), the \(N_\gamma\) term collapses to zero:\[q_u = (40 \times 5.14 \times 1.16 \times 1.1 \times 1.0) + (27.3 \times 1.0 \times 1.0 \times 1.0 \times 1.0) + 0 \]\[q_u = 262.3456 + 27.3 = 289.6456\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  4. Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_{nu}\)):\[q_{nu} = 289.6456 - 27.3 = 262.3456\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  5. Safe Applied Load (\(Q_{safe}\)):\[Q_{nu} = 262.3456 \times 4.2 = 1101.8515\text{ kN} \]\[Q_{safe} = \dfrac{1101.8515}{2.5} = 440.74\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 440.74 kN | Accepted key range: 439.00 to 442.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The soil profile at a road construction site is as shown in figure (not to scale). A large embankment is to be constructed at the site. The ground water table (GWT) is located at the surface of the clay layer, and the capillary rise in the sandy soil is negligible. The effective stress at the middle of the clay layer after the application of the embankment loading is 180 kN/m². Take unit weight of water, \( \gamma_w = 9.81 \) kN/m³.



The primary consolidation settlement (in m, round off to two decimal places) of the clay layer resulting from this loading will be ______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Top Sand Layer: \(H_1 = 2\text{ m}\), \(\gamma_{sand} = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\). GWT is at the sand-clay interface.
    • Bottom Clay Layer: \(H_0 = 6\text{ m}\)
    • Clay properties: \(G_s = 2.65\), \(w = 45\%\), \(C_c = 0.25\)
    • Final effective stress at middle of clay: \(\sigma'_f = 180\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the primary consolidation settlement (\(S_c\)) of the clay layer in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

Phase Relationships: Since the clay is below GWT, it is fully saturated (\(S = 1\)):\[e_0 = w \cdot G_s \]

Submerged Unit Weight (\(\gamma'\)):\[\gamma' = \left(\dfrac{G_s - 1}{1 + e_0}\right)\gamma_w \]

Consolidation Settlement (\(S_c\)):\[S_c = \dfrac{C_c}{1 + e_0}\, H_0\, \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{\sigma'_f}{\sigma'_0}\right) \]where \(\sigma'_0\) is the initial effective stress at the mid-depth of the clay layer.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the initial void ratio \(e_0\) using saturated phase relations.
  2. Calculate the submerged effective unit weight (\(\gamma'\)) for the clay layer.
  3. Compute the initial effective stress \(\sigma'_0\) at the center of the clay layer (2 m sand + 3 m clay).
  4. Apply Terzaghi's primary consolidation formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Void Ratio (\(e_0\)):\[e_0 = 0.45 \times 2.65 = 1.1925 \]
  2. Submerged Unit Weight of Clay (\(\gamma'_{clay}\)):\[\gamma'_{clay} = \left(\dfrac{2.65 - 1}{1 + 1.1925}\right) \times 9.81 = \left(\dfrac{1.65}{2.1925}\right) \times 9.81 = 7.383\text{ kN/m}^3 \]
  3. Initial Effective Stress at Mid-Depth (\(\sigma'_0\)):
    Mid-depth of the 6 m clay layer = 3 m below the sand-clay interface:\[\sigma'_0 = (\gamma_{sand} \times 2) + (\gamma'_{clay} \times 3) = (18.5 \times 2) + (7.383 \times 3) \]\[\sigma'_0 = 37.0 + 22.148 = 59.148\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  4. Primary Consolidation Settlement (\(S_c\)):\[S_c = \dfrac{0.25}{1 + 1.1925} \times 6 \times \log_{10}\left(\dfrac{180}{59.148}\right) \]\[S_c = \dfrac{1.5}{2.1925} \times \log_{10}(3.0432) = 0.68415 \times 0.48333 = 0.3306\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.33 m | Accepted key range: 0.32 to 0.34

questions.title: GATE CE 2021 Set 2 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The void ratio of a clay soil sample M decreased from 0.575 to 0.510 when the applied pressure is increased from 120 kPa to 180 kPa. For the same increment in pressure, the void ratio of another clay soil sample N decreases from 0.600 to 0.550. If the ratio of hydraulic conductivity of sample M to sample N is 0.125, then the ratio of coefficient of consolidation of sample M to sample N (round off to three decimal places) is ______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation (Rate)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Sample M: \(e_{M,initial} = 0.575\), \(e_{M,final} = 0.510\), \(\Delta\sigma' = 60\text{ kPa}\)
    • Sample N: \(e_{N,initial} = 0.600\), \(e_{N,final} = 0.550\), \(\Delta\sigma' = 60\text{ kPa}\)
    • Ratio of hydraulic conductivities: \(\dfrac{k_M}{k_N} = 0.125\)
  • Aim: Find the ratio of the coefficient of consolidation \(\left(\dfrac{c_{v,M}}{c_{v,N}}\right)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Coefficient of Volume Compressibility (\(m_v\)):\[m_v = \dfrac{\Delta e}{\Delta\sigma'\,(1 + e_0)} \]where \(e_0\) is the initial void ratio prior to the pressure increment.

Coefficient of Consolidation (\(c_v\)):\[c_v = \dfrac{k}{m_v\,\gamma_w} \]

Ratio of \(c_v\):\[\dfrac{c_{v,M}}{c_{v,N}} = \left(\dfrac{k_M}{k_N}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{m_{v,N}}{m_{v,M}}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(m_v\) for both Sample M and Sample N.
  2. Determine the ratio \(\dfrac{m_{v,N}}{m_{v,M}}\).
  3. Multiply the inverse \(m_v\) ratio by the given permeability ratio to obtain \(\dfrac{c_{v,M}}{c_{v,N}}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compressibility of Sample M (\(m_{v,M}\)):\[\Delta e_M = 0.575 - 0.510 = 0.065 \]\[m_{v,M} = \dfrac{0.065}{60 \times (1 + 0.575)} = \dfrac{0.065}{60 \times 1.575} = \dfrac{0.065}{94.5} = 6.878 \times 10^{-4}\text{ kPa}^{-1} \]
  2. Compressibility of Sample N (\(m_{v,N}\)):\[\Delta e_N = 0.600 - 0.550 = 0.050 \]\[m_{v,N} = \dfrac{0.050}{60 \times (1 + 0.600)} = \dfrac{0.050}{60 \times 1.600} = \dfrac{0.050}{96.0} = 5.208 \times 10^{-4}\text{ kPa}^{-1} \]
  3. Ratio of \(m_v\):\[\dfrac{m_{v,N}}{m_{v,M}} = \dfrac{0.050/96.0}{0.065/94.5} = \left(\dfrac{50}{65}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{94.5}{96}\right) = \dfrac{10}{13} \times 0.984375 = 0.75721 \]
  4. Ratio of \(c_v\):\[\dfrac{c_{v,M}}{c_{v,N}} = 0.125 \times 0.75721 = 0.09465 \approx 0.095 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.095 | Accepted key range: 0.090 to 0.105

At 3 m depth, the observed number of hammer blows for three successive 150 mm penetrations were 8, 6 and 9, respectively. The SPT N-value at 3 m depth, is

    • Hammer blows for three successive 150 mm penetrations: 8, 6, 9.
  • Aim: Calculate the officially recorded SPT N-value at that depth.

3. Core Concepts:

Standard Penetration Test (IS 2131): The sampler is driven 450 mm in three 150 mm increments.

Seating Drive: The first 150 mm is discarded — the soil at the borehole bottom is likely disturbed by drilling operations.

N-value: Sum of blows for the last two 150 mm increments (the penetration resistance for 300 mm).

IncrementBlowsStatus

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Velocity of flow is proportional to the first power of hydraulic gradient in Darcy’s law. This law is applicable to
options: laminar as well as turbulent flow in porous media

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: laminar as well as turbulent flow in porous media
structuredOptions.html: laminar as well as turbulent flow in porous media

questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics / Geotechnical Engineering | Flow Through Soils

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Darcy's law: \(V = k \cdot i\) (velocity proportional to first power of hydraulic gradient).
  • Aim: Identify the specific flow regime for which Darcy's law is valid.

3. Core Concepts:

Darcy's Law: Establishes a linear relationship between discharge velocity and hydraulic gradient in porous media.

Validity Constraint: This linear proportionality holds only when viscous forces dominate inertial forces, i.e., Reynolds number \(Re < 1\). At higher \(Re\), flow becomes turbulent and \(V \propto i^n\) where \(n \approx 0.5\) (non-linear).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

The condition \(Re < 1\) represents purely laminar flow. Therefore, Darcy's law is valid strictly for laminar flow in porous media.

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Laminar flow in porous media | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In a drained triaxial compression test, a sample of sand fails at deviator stress of 150 kPa under confining pressure of 50 kPa. The angle of internal friction (in degree, round off to the nearest integer) of the sample, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soil

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Test type: Drained triaxial compression test
    • Soil: Sand → cohesion \(c' = 0\)
    • Confining pressure: \(\sigma_3 = 50\) kPa
    • Deviator stress at failure: \(\sigma_d = 150\) kPa
  • Aim: Calculate the angle of internal friction (\(\phi'\)) of the sand sample.

3. Core Concepts:

Major Principal Stress at Failure: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 + \sigma_d\)

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion for Sand (\(c = 0\)):\[\sin\phi' = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3} \]

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Major Principal Stress

\[\sigma_1 = 50 + 150 = 200 \text{ kPa} \]

Step 2: Apply Mohr-Coulomb Criterion

\[\sin\phi' = \dfrac{200 - 50}{200 + 50} = \dfrac{150}{250} = 0.60 \]

Step 3: Solve for \(\phi'\)

\[\phi' = \arcsin(0.60) = 36.87° \approx \mathbf{37°} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 37° | Accepted key range: 36 to 38

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A fully submerged infinite sandy slope has an inclination of 30° with the horizontal. The saturated unit weight and effective angle of internal friction of sand are 18 kN/m³ and 38°, respectively. The unit weight of water is 10 kN/m³. Assume that the seepage is parallel to the slope. Against shear failure of the slope, the factor of safety (round off to two decimal places) is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stability of Slopes

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Slope type: Fully submerged infinite sandy slope
    • Slope inclination: \(\beta = 30°\)
    • Saturated unit weight: \(\gamma_{sat} = 18\) kN/m³
    • Effective friction angle: \(\phi' = 38°\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\) kN/m³
    • Condition: Seepage parallel to slope
  • Aim: Determine the Factor of Safety (FOS) against shear failure.

3. Core Concepts:

For an infinite slope with seepage parallel to the slope surface (water table flush with surface), the FOS formula is:\[FOS = \left(\dfrac{\gamma_{sub}}{\gamma_{sat}}\right) \dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta} \]where the driving force uses \(\gamma_{sat}\) and the resisting force uses \(\gamma_{sub}\) (due to pore water pressure reducing effective normal stress).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Submerged Unit Weight

\[\gamma_{sub} = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w = 18 - 10 = 8 \text{ kN/m}^3 \]

Step 2: Factor of Safety

\[FOS = \left(\dfrac{8}{18}\right) \times \dfrac{\tan 38°}{\tan 30°} = 0.4444 \times \dfrac{0.78128}{0.57735} \]\[= 0.4444 \times 1.3532 = \mathbf{0.60} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.60 | Accepted key range: 0.59 to 0.61

questions.question:
The total stress paths corresponding to different loading conditions, for a soil specimen under the isotropically consolidated stress state (O), are shown below

OPI - Compression loading (σ₁ – increasing; σ₃ – constant)

The correct match between the stress paths and the listed loading conditions, is
options: OP – I, OQ – II, OR – IV, OS – III
OP – IV, OQ – III, OR – I, OS – II
