structuredOptions.html: OP – I, OQ – III, OR – II, OS – IV

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stress Path

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Stress state equations: \(p = \dfrac{\sigma_1 + 2\sigma_3}{3}\) and \(q = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3\)
    • Graphical stress paths OP, OQ, OR, OS starting from an isotropic consolidated state 'O'.
    • Four loading conditions varying \(\sigma_1\) and \(\sigma_3\).
  • Aim: Match the given loading conditions (I, II, III, IV) to the corresponding graphical stress paths (OP, OQ, OR, OS) based on the changes in \(p\) and \(q\).

3. Core Concepts:

Stress Path: A locus of points representing the successive states of stress in a test specimen.

Changes in Stress Coordinates: The movement along the \(p\)-\(q\) plane depends on the incremental changes in major (\(\Delta\sigma_1\)) and minor (\(\Delta\sigma_3\)) principal stresses.

  • Change in horizontal axis: \(\Delta p = \dfrac{\Delta\sigma_1 + 2\Delta\sigma_3}{3}\)
  • Change in vertical axis: \(\Delta q = \Delta\sigma_1 - \Delta\sigma_3\)

4. Solution Method:

By evaluating the signs (positive or negative) of \(\Delta p\) and \(\Delta q\) for each loading condition, we determine the quadrant direction the stress path takes from origin 'O'.

Quadrant\(\Delta p\)\(\Delta q\)
Top-Right\(> 0\)\(> 0\)
Top-Left\(< 0\)\(> 0\)
Bottom-Left\(< 0\)\(< 0\)
Bottom-Right\(> 0\)\(< 0\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Condition I — Compression Loading (\(\Delta\sigma_1 > 0\), \(\Delta\sigma_3 = 0\)):
    \(\Delta p = \dfrac{+ve + 0}{3} = +ve\) (Moves Right)
    \(\Delta q = +ve - 0 = +ve\) (Moves Up)
    → Vector moves Up and Right → Path OR
  2. Condition II — Compression Unloading (\(\Delta\sigma_1 = 0\), \(\Delta\sigma_3 < 0\)):
    \(\Delta p = \dfrac{0 + 2(-ve)}{3} = -ve\) (Moves Left)
    \(\Delta q = 0 - (-ve) = +ve\) (Moves Up)
    → Vector moves Up and Left → Path OS
  3. Condition III — Extension Unloading (\(\Delta\sigma_1 < 0\), \(\Delta\sigma_3 = 0\)):
    \(\Delta p = \dfrac{-ve + 0}{3} = -ve\) (Moves Left)
    \(\Delta q = -ve - 0 = -ve\) (Moves Down)
    → Vector moves Down and Left → Path OQ
  4. Condition IV — Extension Loading (\(\Delta\sigma_1 = 0\), \(\Delta\sigma_3 > 0\)):
    \(\Delta p = \dfrac{0 + 2(+ve)}{3} = +ve\) (Moves Right)
    \(\Delta q = 0 - (+ve) = -ve\) (Moves Down)
    → Vector moves Down and Right → Path OP

Summary of Matches:

Stress PathLoading Condition
OPIV
OQIII
ORI
OSII

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: OP→IV, OQ→III, OR→I, OS→II | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The soil profile at a site up to a depth of 10 m is shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The soil is preloaded with a uniform surcharge (q) of 70 kN/m² at the ground level. The water table is at a depth of 3 m below ground level. The soil unit weight of the respective layers is shown in the figure. Consider unit weight of water as 9.81 kN/m³ and assume that the surcharge (q) is applied instantaneously.



Immediately after preloading, the effective stresses (in kPa) at points P and Q, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Effective Stress & Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Surcharge \(q = 70\) kN/m² (Instantaneous)
    • Depth 0–3 m: Sand, \(\gamma_{\text{bulk}} = 18\) kN/m³
    • Depth 3–7 m: Silty clay, \(\gamma_{\text{sat}} = 20\) kN/m³
    • Point P at 3 m depth (water table level, boundary of sand and silty clay)
    • Point Q at 7 m depth (boundary of silty clay and clay)
    • \(\gamma_w = 9.81\) kN/m³
  • Aim: Find effective stresses (\(\sigma'\)) at points P and Q immediately after preloading.

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Principle of Effective Stress: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\), where \(\sigma\) = Total stress and \(u\) = Pore water pressure.

Undrained Loading in Saturated Fine-Grained Soils: When an external load is applied instantaneously to a saturated low-permeability soil (like silty clay), water cannot drain immediately. The entire additional load is initially carried by the pore water:

\[\Delta u = \Delta \sigma = q \]

Therefore, the change in effective stress immediately after loading is zero:

\[\Delta \sigma' = \Delta \sigma - \Delta u = 0 \]

4. Solution Method:

Since both points P and Q are on/within saturated fine-grained soil under undrained conditions, their effective stresses do not change upon instantaneous loading. We calculate the initial in-situ effective stresses before the surcharge was applied.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Effective Stress at Point P (Depth = 3 m)

  • Total Stress: \(\sigma_P = 18 \times 3 = 54\) kPa
  • Pore Water Pressure: \(u_P = 0\) kPa (exactly at water table)
  • \(\sigma'_P = 54 - 0 = \mathbf{54 \text{ kPa}}\)

Step 2: Effective Stress at Point Q (Depth = 7 m)

  • Total Stress:\[\sigma_Q = (18 \times 3) + (20 \times 4) = 54 + 80 = 134 \text{ kPa} \]
  • Pore Water Pressure (4 m of water above Q):\[u_Q = 9.81 \times 4 = 39.24 \text{ kPa} \]
  • \(\sigma'_Q = 134 - 39.24 = 94.76 \approx \mathbf{95 \text{ kPa}}\)

Step 3: Immediate Loading Effects

ParameterPoint PPoint Q
Initial \(\sigma'\)54 kPa95 kPa
\(\Delta\sigma\)+70 kPa+70 kPa
\(\Delta u\)+70 kPa+70 kPa
\(\Delta\sigma'\)00
Final \(\sigma'\)54 kPa95 kPa

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 54 kPa and 95 kPa | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A vertical retaining wall of 5 m height has to support soil having unit weight of 18 kN/m³, effective cohesion of 12 kN/m², and effective friction angle of 30°. As per Rankine’s earth pressure theory and assuming that a tension crack has occurred, the lateral active thrust on the wall per meter length (in kN/m, round off to two decimal places), is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theories

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Height of wall: \(H = 5\) m
    • Unit weight of soil: \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³
    • Effective cohesion: \(c' = 12\) kN/m²
    • Effective friction angle: \(\phi' = 30°\)
    • Theory: Rankine's earth pressure theory
    • Assumption: Tension crack has occurred
  • Aim: Lateral active thrust per meter length of wall (kN/m), rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure (\(K_a\)):\[K_a = \dfrac{1 - \sin\phi'}{1 + \sin\phi'} \]

Depth of Tension Crack (\(z_c\)):\[z_c = \dfrac{2c'}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} \]

Lateral Active Thrust (\(P_a\)): Since tension crack has occurred, negative pressure in the zone 0 to \(z_c\) is completely ignored. Thrust is calculated from the positive triangular pressure distribution between \(z_c\) and \(H\):\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2}\, K_a\, \gamma\, (H - z_c)^2 \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute active earth pressure coefficient (\(K_a\)).
  2. Compute theoretical depth of tension crack (\(z_c\)).
  3. Calculate lateral active thrust from the positive pressure triangle between \(z_c\) and \(H\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Active Earth Pressure Coefficient

\[K_a = \dfrac{1 - \sin 30°}{1 + \sin 30°} = \dfrac{1 - 0.5}{1 + 0.5} = \dfrac{0.5}{1.5} = \dfrac{1}{3} \approx 0.333 \]

Step 2: Depth of Tension Crack

\[z_c = \dfrac{2 \times 12}{18 \times \sqrt{1/3}} = \dfrac{24}{18 \times 0.57735} = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 2.309 \text{ m} \]

Step 3: Active Pressure at Base and Thrust

Active pressure at the base (\(z = H\)):

\[p_a(H) = K_a\,\gamma\,H - 2c'\sqrt{K_a} = \left(\dfrac{1}{3} \times 18 \times 5\right) - \left(2 \times 12 \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \]\[= 30 - 13.856 = 16.144 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]

Lateral active thrust (area of positive pressure triangle from \(z_c\) to \(H\)):

\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2} \times p_a(H) \times (H - z_c) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 16.144 \times (5 - 2.309) \]\[= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 16.144 \times 2.691 = \mathbf{21.72 \text{ kN/m}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 21.72 kN/m | Accepted key range: 21.00 to 22.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Water flows in the upward direction in a tank through 2.5 m thick sand layer as shown in the figure. The void ratio and specific gravity of sand are 0.58 and 2.7, respectively. The sand is fully saturated. Unit weight of water is 10 kN/m³.



The effective stress (in kPa, round off to two decimal places) at point A, located 1 m above the base of tank, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage & Effective Stress

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Upward flow of water in a tank.
    • Sand layer thickness: \(L = 2.5\) m
    • Void ratio: \(e = 0.58\)
    • Specific gravity: \(G = 2.7\)
    • \(\gamma_w = 10\) kN/m³ (saturated sand layer)
    • Point A is 1 m above the tank base → depth from top of sand: \(z_A = 2.5 - 1.0 = 1.5\) m
    • Seepage driving head: \(\Delta h = 1.2\) m
  • Aim: Effective stress at point A (\(\sigma'_A\)) in kPa, rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Saturated and Submerged Unit Weight:\[\gamma_{sat} = \left(\dfrac{G + e}{1 + e}\right)\gamma_w \qquad \gamma' = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w \]

Hydraulic Gradient (\(i\)):\[i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L} \]

Effective Stress during Upward Flow: Seepage forces act upwards, reducing effective stress compared to static conditions.\[\sigma'_A = z_A\,(\gamma' - i\,\gamma_w) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate submerged unit weight of sand (\(\gamma'\)).
  2. Calculate the hydraulic gradient driving upward flow (\(i\)).
  3. Calculate effective stress at depth \(z_A\) accounting for the opposing seepage gradient.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Saturated and Effective Unit Weights

\[\gamma_{sat} = \dfrac{2.7 + 0.58}{1 + 0.58} \times 10 = \dfrac{3.28}{1.58} \times 10 = 20.759 \text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\gamma' = 20.759 - 10 = 10.759 \text{ kN/m}^3 \]

Step 2: Hydraulic Gradient

\[i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L} = \dfrac{1.2}{2.5} = 0.48 \]

Step 3: Effective Stress at Point A

\[\sigma'_A = z_A\,(\gamma' - i\,\gamma_w) = 1.5 \times (10.759 - 0.48 \times 10) \]\[= 1.5 \times (10.759 - 4.800) = 1.5 \times 5.959 = \mathbf{8.94 \text{ kPa}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8.94 kPa | Accepted key range: 8.70 to 9.30

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 1 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 10 m thick clay layer is resting over a 3 m thick sand layer and is submerged. A fill of 2 m thick sand with unit weight of 20 kN/m³ is placed above the clay layer to accelerate the rate of consolidation of the clay layer. Coefficient of consolidation of clay is 9×10⁻² m²/year and coefficient of volume compressibility of clay is 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ m²/kN. Assume Taylor’s relation between time factor and average degree of consolidation.



The settlement (in mm, round off to two decimal places) of the clay layer, 10 years after the construction of the fill, is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Thickness of clay layer: \(H_{clay} = 10\) m
    • Thickness of sand fill: \(H_{fill} = 2\) m
    • Unit weight of sand fill: \(\gamma_{fill} = 20\) kN/m³
    • Coefficient of consolidation: \(c_v = 9 \times 10^{-2}\) m²/year
    • Coefficient of volume compressibility: \(m_v = 2.2 \times 10^{-4}\) m²/kN
    • Time elapsed: \(t = 10\) years
  • Aim: Settlement of the clay layer after 10 years (\(\Delta H_t\)) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Surcharge Loading: \(\Delta\sigma = \gamma_{fill} \times H_{fill}\)

Ultimate Consolidation Settlement: \(\Delta H = H_{clay} \cdot m_v \cdot \Delta\sigma\)

Drainage Condition: Sand fill above and sand layer below the clay → double drainage condition, so drainage path \(d = H_{clay}/2\).

Time Factor: \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v t}{d^2}\)

Degree of Consolidation (Taylor's relation for \(U \le 60\%\)): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4} U^2\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Surcharge Load

\[\Delta\sigma = 20 \times 2 = 40 \text{ kN/m}^2 \]

Step 2: Ultimate Settlement

\[\Delta H = 10 \times 2.2 \times 10^{-4} \times 40 = 0.088 \text{ m} = 88 \text{ mm} \]

Step 3: Drainage Path (double drainage)

\[d = \dfrac{10}{2} = 5 \text{ m} \]

Step 4: Time Factor

\[T_v = \dfrac{9 \times 10^{-2} \times 10}{(5)^2} = \dfrac{0.9}{25} = 0.036 \]

Step 5: Average Degree of Consolidation

Since \(T_v = 0.036 < 0.282\) (boundary for \(U = 60\%\)), Taylor's relation applies:

\[0.036 = \dfrac{\pi}{4} U^2 \implies U = \sqrt{\dfrac{0.036 \times 4}{\pi}} = \sqrt{0.04584} = 0.2141 \quad (21.41\%) \]

Step 6: Settlement at 10 years

\[\Delta H_t = U \times \Delta H = 0.2141 \times 88 = \mathbf{18.84 \text{ mm}} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 18.84 mm | Accepted key range: 18.50 to 19.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A sample of 500 g dry sand, when poured into a 2 litre capacity cylinder which is partially filled with water, displaces 188 cm³ of water. The density of water is 1 g/cm³. The specific gravity of the sand is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Basic Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Dry mass of sand, \(M_s = 500\text{ g}\)
    • Volume of displaced water, \(V_d = 188\text{ cm}^3\)
    • Density of water, \(\rho_w = 1\text{ g/cm}^3\)
  • Aim: Compute the specific gravity (\(G_s\)) of the sand.

3. Core Concepts:

Specific Gravity: \[G_s = \dfrac{\rho_s}{\rho_w} = \dfrac{M_s / V_s}{\rho_w} \]

Archimedes' Principle: Volume of water displaced by dry soil = volume of solid particles (\(V_s\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Volume of Solids: \(V_s = 188\text{ cm}^3\)
  2. Solid Density: \(\rho_s = \dfrac{500}{188} = 2.6596\text{ g/cm}^3\)
  3. Specific Gravity: \(G_s = \dfrac{2.6596}{1.0} \approx 2.66\)

6. Final Answer:

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A soil has dry unit weight of 15.5 kN/m³, specific gravity of 2.65 and degree of saturation of 72%. Considering the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³, the water content of the soil (in %, round off to two decimal places) is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Properties | Phase Relationships

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Dry unit weight, \(\gamma_d = 15.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Specific gravity, \(G_s = 2.65\)
    • Degree of saturation, \(S = 0.72\)
    • \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Determine the water content (\(w\)) in %.

3. Core Concepts:

  • \(\gamma_d = \dfrac{G_s\,\gamma_w}{1 + e}\)
  • \(Se = wG_s\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Void Ratio (\(e\))

\[15.5 = \dfrac{2.65 \times 10}{1 + e} \implies 1 + e = \dfrac{26.5}{15.5} = 1.7097 \implies e = 0.7097 \]

Step 2: Water Content (\(w\))

\[w = \dfrac{Se}{G_s} = \dfrac{0.72 \times 0.7097}{2.65} = 0.1928 \approx 19.28\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 19.28% | Accepted key range: 19.00 to 19.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2020 Set 2 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A one-dimensional consolidation test is carried out on a standard 19 mm thick clay sample. The oedometer's deflection gauge indicates a reading of 2.1 mm, just before removal of the load, without allowing any swelling. The void ratio is 0.62 at this stage. The initial void ratio (round off to two decimal places) of the standard specimen is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation | Oedometer Test

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Initial thickness, \(H_0 = 19\text{ mm}\)
    • Change in thickness, \(\Delta H = 2.1\text{ mm}\)
    • Final void ratio, \(e_f = 0.62\)
  • Aim: Calculate the initial void ratio (\(e_0\)).

3. Core Concepts:

1D Consolidation Settlement: \[\dfrac{\Delta H}{H_0} = \dfrac{\Delta e}{1 + e_0} = \dfrac{e_0 - e_f}{1 + e_0} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

\[\dfrac{2.1}{19} = \dfrac{e_0 - 0.62}{1 + e_0} \] \[2.1(1 + e_0) = 19(e_0 - 0.62) \] \[2.1 + 2.1e_0 = 19e_0 - 11.78 \] \[13.88 = 16.9e_0 \implies e_0 = \dfrac{13.88}{16.9} \approx 0.82 \]

6. Final Answer:
