5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: High impact at start of loading | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q32
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 3 m high vertical earth retaining wall retains a dry granular backfill with angle of internal friction of 30° and unit weight of 20 kN/m³. If the wall is prevented from yielding (no movement), the total horizontal thrust (in kN per unit length) on the wall is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Lateral Earth Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Height of retaining wall (\(H\)) = 3 m
    • Unit weight of backfill (\(\gamma\)) = 20 kN/m³
    • Angle of internal friction (\(\phi\)) = 30°
    • Wall condition: "Prevented from yielding" (No movement)
  • Aim: To calculate the total horizontal thrust per unit length of the wall.

3. Core Concepts:

Earth Pressure Condition: When a retaining wall is strictly prevented from yielding or moving, the soil is in a state of Earth Pressure at Rest.

Coefficient of Earth Pressure at Rest (\(K_0\)): Estimated using Jaky's empirical formula for normally consolidated granular soils: \(K_0 = 1 - \sin\phi\).

Lateral Earth Pressure Distribution: Varies triangularly with depth \(z\), such that horizontal stress \(\sigma_h = K_0 \cdot \gamma \cdot z\).

Total Horizontal Thrust (\(P_0\)): The area of the triangular pressure distribution diagram:\[P_0 = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot K_0 \cdot \gamma \cdot H^2\]

4. Solution Method:

  • Calculate the at-rest coefficient \(K_0\) using the given friction angle.
  • Substitute \(K_0\), \(\gamma\), and \(H\) into the formula for total thrust.
  • Solve to find \(P_0\) in kN/m.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(K_0\):\[K_0 = 1 - \sin(30^\circ) = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5\]
  2. Calculate horizontal stress at the base of the wall (\(z = H\)):\[(\sigma_h)_{base} = K_0 \cdot \gamma \cdot H = 0.5 \times 20\text{ kN/m}^3 \times 3\text{ m} = 30\text{ kN/m}^2\]
  3. Calculate Total Thrust (\(P_0\)):
    The thrust is the area of the triangular stress block.\[P_0 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times (\text{Base Stress}) \times \text{Height}\]\[P_0 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 30\text{ kN/m}^2 \times 3\text{ m} = 45\text{ kN/m}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 45 kN/m | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q33
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Three soil specimens (Soil 1, Soil 2 and Soil 3), each 150 mm long and 100 mm diameter, are placed in series in a constant head flow set-up as shown in the figure. Suitable screens are provided at the boundaries of the specimens to keep them intact. The values of coefficient of permeability of Soil 1, Soil 2 and Soil 3 are 0.01, 0.003 and 0.03 cm/s, respectively.



The value of h in the set-up is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Permeability and Seepage

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Lengths of soil specimens: \(L_1 = L_2 = L_3 = 150\text{ mm}\)
    • Diameter of soil specimens: \(D = 100\text{ mm}\) (Cross-sectional area \(A\) is constant)
    • Permeability of Soil 1: \(k_1 = 0.01\text{ cm/s}\)
    • Permeability of Soil 2: \(k_2 = 0.003\text{ cm/s}\)
    • Permeability of Soil 3: \(k_3 = 0.03\text{ cm/s}\)
    • Total head difference between upstream (left) and downstream (right) reservoirs: \(\Delta H = 560\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(h\), which the diagram shows as the piezometric head difference between the standpipe at the entry of Soil 3 and the water level of the right reservoir. Thus, \(h\) equals the head loss across Soil 3 alone (\(\Delta h_3\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Darcy's Law: \(Q = k \cdot i \cdot A\)

Continuity Equation for Series Flow: For soils connected in series with a constant cross-sectional area, the discharge \(Q\) and the discharge velocity \(v\) are constant across all layers.\[v = k_1 i_1 = k_2 i_2 = k_3 i_3\]

Hydraulic Gradient: \(i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L}\)

Total Head Loss: \(\Delta H = \Delta h_1 + \Delta h_2 + \Delta h_3\)

4. Solution Method:

Since velocity \(v\) and length \(L\) are constant for all three soils, the head loss in each soil layer is inversely proportional to its permeability. Express the head loss of Soil 1 and Soil 2 in terms of the head loss of Soil 3 (\(\Delta h_3\)). Sum them up and equate to the total head loss (\(\Delta H = 560\text{ mm}\)) to solve for \(\Delta h_3\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish relationship between head losses:\[k_1 \dfrac{\Delta h_1}{L_1} = k_2 \dfrac{\Delta h_2}{L_2} = k_3 \dfrac{\Delta h_3}{L_3}\]Since \(L_1 = L_2 = L_3\):\[k_1 \Delta h_1 = k_2 \Delta h_2 = k_3 \Delta h_3\]
  2. Express \(\Delta h_1\) and \(\Delta h_2\) in terms of \(\Delta h_3\):\[\Delta h_1 = \dfrac{k_3}{k_1} \Delta h_3 = \dfrac{0.03}{0.01} \Delta h_3 = 3\,\Delta h_3\]\[\Delta h_2 = \dfrac{k_3}{k_2} \Delta h_3 = \dfrac{0.03}{0.003} \Delta h_3 = 10\,\Delta h_3\]
  3. Apply total head loss constraint:\[\Delta H = \Delta h_1 + \Delta h_2 + \Delta h_3 = 560\text{ mm}\]\[3\,\Delta h_3 + 10\,\Delta h_3 + 1\,\Delta h_3 = 560\text{ mm}\]\[14\,\Delta h_3 = 560\text{ mm}\]
  4. Solve for \(\Delta h_3\):\[\Delta h_3 = \dfrac{560}{14} = 40\text{ mm}\]Since \(h\) in the figure is the head loss across Soil 3, \(h = 40\text{ mm}\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 40 mm | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The compression curve (void ratio, e vs. effective stress, σ'v) for a certain clayey soil is a straight line in a semi-logarithmic plot and it passes through the points (e = 1.2; σ'v = 50 kPa) and (e = 0.6; σ'v = 800 kPa). The compression index (up to two decimal places) of the soil is ______
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Void ratio \(e_1 = 1.2\) at effective stress \(\sigma'_{v1} = 50\text{ kPa}\)
    • Void ratio \(e_2 = 0.6\) at effective stress \(\sigma'_{v2} = 800\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the compression index (\(C_c\)) of the soil (up to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

The compression curve (\(e\) vs. \(\log_{10} \sigma'_v\)) for normally consolidated clay is a straight line.

Compression Index (\(C_c\)): Defined as the slope of the virgin compression line on a semi-logarithmic plot.\[C_c = \dfrac{\Delta e}{\Delta \log_{10} \sigma'_v} = \dfrac{e_1 - e_2}{\log_{10} \left( \dfrac{\sigma'_{v2}}{\sigma'_{v1}} \right)}\]

4. Solution Method:

Directly apply the formula for the compression index using the given points on the straight line.

Sanity Check: \(C_c\) for clayey soils typically ranges between 0.1 and 0.8. The data provided reflects realistic values.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify parameters:
    \(e_1 = 1.2\), \(e_2 = 0.6\), \(\sigma'_{v1} = 50\text{ kPa}\), \(\sigma'_{v2} = 800\text{ kPa}\)
  2. Substitute into the formula:\[C_c = \dfrac{1.2 - 0.6}{\log_{10} \left( \dfrac{800}{50} \right)}\]
  3. Evaluate the denominator:\[\dfrac{800}{50} = 16 \implies \log_{10}(16) \approx 1.20412\]
  4. Calculate \(C_c\):\[C_c = \dfrac{0.60}{1.20412} = 0.49829\]
  5. Round off to two decimal places: \(C_c \approx 0.50\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.50 | Accepted key range: 0.45 to 0.55

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The total horizontal and vertical stresses at a point X in a saturated sandy medium are 170 kPa and 300 kPa, respectively. The static pore-water pressure is 30 kPa. At failure, the excess pore-water pressure is measured to be 94.50 kPa, and the shear stresses on the vertical and horizontal planes passing through the point X are zero. Effective cohesion is 0 kPa and effective angle of internal friction is 36°. The shear strength (in kPa, up to two decimal places) at point X is ______
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Total stresses: \(\sigma_h = 170\text{ kPa}\), \(\sigma_v = 300\text{ kPa}\)
    • Static pore-water pressure: \(u_0 = 30\text{ kPa}\)
    • Excess pore-water pressure at failure: \(\Delta u = 94.50\text{ kPa}\)
    • Shear stress on horizontal and vertical planes = 0 kPa (hence, these are principal planes)
    • Effective shear strength parameters: \(c' = 0\text{ kPa}\), \(\phi' = 36^\circ\)
  • Aim: Determine the shear strength (in kPa) at failure for point X.

3. Core Concepts:

Principal Stresses: Since there are no shear stresses on the vertical and horizontal planes, the applied normal stresses are the principal stresses (\(\sigma_1 = \sigma_v\), \(\sigma_3 = \sigma_h\)).

Effective Stress Principle: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u_{total}\), where total pore pressure at failure \(u_f = u_0 + \Delta u\).

Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion: The shear stress at tangency of the Mohr circle with the failure envelope:\[\tau_f = R \cos \phi'\]where radius \(R = \dfrac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2}\).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the total pore-water pressure at failure.
  2. Determine major (\(\sigma'_1\)) and minor (\(\sigma'_3\)) effective principal stresses.
  3. Compute the radius of the Mohr circle at failure.
  4. Calculate the shear strength on the failure plane using the radius and effective friction angle.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Pore Pressure (\(u_f\)):\[u_f = u_0 + \Delta u = 30 + 94.50 = 124.50\text{ kPa}\]
  2. Effective Principal Stresses:\[\sigma'_1 = \sigma_v - u_f = 300 - 124.50 = 175.50\text{ kPa}\]\[\sigma'_3 = \sigma_h - u_f = 170 - 124.50 = 45.50\text{ kPa}\]
  3. Mohr Circle Radius (\(R\)):\[R = \dfrac{\sigma'_1 - \sigma'_3}{2} = \dfrac{175.50 - 45.50}{2} = \dfrac{130.00}{2} = 65.00\text{ kPa}\]
  4. Calculate Shear Strength (\(\tau_f\)):\[\tau_f = R \cos \phi' = 65.00 \times \cos(36^\circ) = 65.00 \times 0.80902 = 52.586\text{ kPa}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 52.59 kPa | Accepted key range: 51.50 to 53.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q45
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A group of nine piles in a 3 × 3 square pattern is embedded in a soil strata comprising dense sand underlying recently filled clay layer, as shown in the figure. The perimeter of an individual pile is 126 cm. The size of pile group is 240 cm × 240 cm. The recently filled clay has undrained shear strength of 15 kPa and unit weight of 16 kN/m³.



The negative frictional load (in kN, up to two decimal places) acting on the pile group is ______
questions.explanation:
Foundation Engineering | Deep Foundations (Pile Groups)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Pile group: \(3 \times 3\) (\(n = 9\) piles)
    • Perimeter of one pile: \(p = 126\text{ cm} = 1.26\text{ m}\)
    • Size of pile group: \(B_g \times B_g = 240\text{ cm} \times 240\text{ cm} = 2.4\text{ m} \times 2.4\text{ m}\)
    • Recently filled clay layer thickness: \(L_c = 2\text{ m}\)
    • Clay properties: \(c_u = 15\text{ kPa}\), \(\gamma = 16\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total negative frictional load acting on the pile group.

3. Core Concepts:

Negative Skin Friction: Occurs when the surrounding soil (e.g., recently filled soft clay) settles more than the pile, applying a downward drag force.

IS 2911 / Standard Pile Group Guidelines: The design negative skin friction load (\(F_{ng}\)) is the maximum of:

  • Sum of drag forces on individual piles: \(F_{ng,\text{ind}} = n \times (\alpha \cdot c_u \cdot p \cdot L_c)\)
  • Block failure drag force: \(F_{ng,\text{block}} = c_u \cdot P_g \cdot L_c + \gamma \cdot A_g \cdot L_c\)

Standard Assumption: For soft/recently filled clay, the adhesion factor \(\alpha = 1.0\) unless otherwise specified.

4. Solution Method:

Calculate both failure mechanisms (individual vs. block). The pile group experiences the maximum of the two loads because negative skin friction is treated as an applied force, and safety dictates designing for the worst-case drag.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Individual Pile Failure Mechanism (\(F_{ng,\text{ind}}\)):\[F_{ng,ind} = n \times (\alpha \cdot c_u \cdot p \cdot L_c)\]\[F_{ng,ind} = 9 \times (1.0 \times 15\text{ kPa} \times 1.26\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m})\]\[F_{ng,ind} = 9 \times 37.8 = 340.20\text{ kN}\]
  2. Block Failure Mechanism (\(F_{ng,\text{block}}\)):
    • Area of group: \(A_g = 2.4 \times 2.4 = 5.76\text{ m}^2\)
    • Perimeter of group: \(P_g = 4 \times 2.4 = 9.6\text{ m}\)
    \[F_{ng,block} = (c_u \cdot P_g \cdot L_c) + (\gamma \cdot A_g \cdot L_c)\]\[F_{ng,block} = (15 \times 9.6 \times 2) + (16 \times 5.76 \times 2) = 288.00 + 184.32 = 472.32\text{ kN}\]
  3. Determine Final Design Load:\[F_{ng} = \max(340.20\text{ kN},\; 472.32\text{ kN}) = 472.32\text{ kN}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 472.32 kN | Accepted key range: 472.00 to 472.50

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q8
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Group I lists the type of gain or loss of strength in soils. Group II lists the property or process responsible for the loss or gain of strength in soils.
Group I
P. Regain of strength with time
Q. Loss of strength due to cyclic loading
R. Loss of strength due to upward seepage
S. Loss of strength due to remolding
Group II
1. Boiling
2. Liquefaction
3. Thixotropy
4. Sensitivity
The correct match between Group I and Group II is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Soil Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data:
    Group I (Phenomena)Group II (Mechanisms)
    P. Regain of strength1. Boiling
    Q. Loss due to cyclic loading2. Liquefaction
    R. Loss due to upward seepage3. Thixotropy
    S. Loss due to remolding4. Sensitivity
  • Aim: Correctly match Group I phenomena to Group II mechanisms.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Thixotropy: Soil, after remolding and losing strength, gradually regains strength over time at constant water content.
  • Liquefaction: In saturated loose sands, rapid cyclic loading raises pore pressure; effective stress drops to zero and the soil behaves like a liquid.
  • Boiling / Quicksand: Upward seepage forces equal the submerged weight of soil; effective stress becomes zero and particles move upward with water.
  • Sensitivity: Ratio of undisturbed to remolded unconfined compressive strength — measures strength loss due to remolding.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. P (Regain of strength) \(\rightarrow\) Thixotropy \(\rightarrow\) 3
  2. Q (Cyclic loading) \(\rightarrow\) Liquefaction \(\rightarrow\) 2
  3. R (Upward seepage) \(\rightarrow\) Boiling \(\rightarrow\) 1
  4. S (Remolding) \(\rightarrow\) Sensitivity \(\rightarrow\) 4

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P-3, Q-2, R-1, S-4  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q10
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A strip footing is resting on the ground surface of a pure clay bed having an undrained cohesion \(c_u\). The ultimate bearing capacity of the footing is equal to
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering / Bearing Capacity

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Footing type: Strip footing on the ground surface (\(D_f = 0\))
    • Soil: Pure clay (\(\phi = 0^\circ\)), undrained cohesion \(= c_u\)
  • Aim: Calculate the ultimate bearing capacity (\(q_u\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Terzaghi's General Bearing Capacity Equation:
    \[q_u = c N_c + q N_q + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma \]
  • Prandtl's Exact Plasticity Solution for strip footing on purely cohesive soil:
    \[N_c = \pi + 2 \approx 5.14 \]
  • Surface footing: \(D_f = 0 \implies q = \gamma D_f = 0\)
  • Pure clay (\(\phi = 0^\circ\)): \(N_\gamma = 0\), \(N_q = 1\)

4. Solution Method:

The second and third terms vanish. The equation reduces to \(q_u = c_u N_c\). The presence of \(\pi\) in the answer options indicates use of Prandtl's exact solution where \(N_c = \pi + 2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(q_u = c_u N_c + 0 + 0 = c_u N_c\)
  2. \(N_c = (\pi + 2)\) (Prandtl's exact plasticity solution)
  3. \(q_u = (\pi + 2)\,c_u\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \((\pi + 2)c_u\)  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A uniformly distributed line load of 500 kN/m is acting on the ground surface. Based on Boussinesq's theory, the ratio of vertical stress at a depth 2 m to that at 4 m, right below the line of loading, is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Stress Distribution in Soils

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Line load: \(q = 500\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Depth 1: \(z_1 = 2\text{ m}\), Depth 2: \(z_2 = 4\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Find the ratio of vertical stress at \(z_1\) to that at \(z_2\) directly below the line load (\(x = 0\)).

3. Core Concepts:

According to Boussinesq's theory, vertical stress at depth \(z\) and horizontal distance \(x\) from a line load \(q\):

\[ \sigma_z = \dfrac{2q}{\pi z}\left[\dfrac{1}{1+(x/z)^2}\right]^2 \]

Directly below the load (\(x = 0\)):

\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{2q}{\pi z} \]

So \(\sigma_z \propto \dfrac{1}{z}\).

4. Solution Method:

\[\dfrac{\sigma_{z1}}{\sigma_{z2}} = \dfrac{2q/(\pi z_1)}{2q/(\pi z_2)} = \dfrac{z_2}{z_1} \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(z_1 = 2\text{ m}\), \(z_2 = 4\text{ m}\)
  2. \[\dfrac{\sigma_{z1}}{\sigma_{z2}} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2.0 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 2.0  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q22
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 3 m thick clay layer is subjected to an initial uniform pore pressure of 145 kPa as shown in the figure.

For the given ground conditions, the time (in days, rounded to the nearest integer) required for 90% consolidation would be _______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering (Consolidation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Clay layer thickness: \(H = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Coefficient of consolidation: \(c_v = 3.0\text{ mm}^2/\text{min}\)
    • Time factor for 90% consolidation: \(T_{v(90)} = 0.85\)
    • Stratigraphy: Top = Sand (permeable), Bottom = Impermeable
  • Aim: Determine the time (in days) required for 90% consolidation.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Terzaghi's 1-D Consolidation:
    \[T_v = \dfrac{c_v \cdot t}{d^2} \implies t = \dfrac{T_v \cdot d^2}{c_v} \]
  • Drainage Path (\(d\)):
    • Double drainage (permeable both sides): \(d = H/2\)
    • Single drainage (permeable one side only): \(d = H\)
    Here, bottom is impermeable → single drainage, \(d = 3\text{ m}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Unit consistency:
    \(c_v = 3.0\text{ mm}^2/\text{min}\), \(d = 3\text{ m} = 3000\text{ mm}\)
  2. Solve for \(t\):
    \[t = \dfrac{0.85 \times (3000)^2}{3.0} = \dfrac{0.85 \times 9{,}000{,}000}{3.0} = 2{,}550{,}000\text{ min} \]
  3. Convert to days:
    \[t_{days} = \dfrac{2{,}550{,}000}{1440} = 1770.83 \approx \mathbf{1771}\text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1771 days  |  Accepted key range: 1765 to 1775

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q36
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The laboratory tests on a soil sample yields the following results: natural moisture content = 18%, liquid limit = 60%, plastic limit = 25%, percentage of clay sized fraction = 25%. The liquidity index and activity (as per the expression proposed by Skempton) of the soil, respectively, are
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics - Index Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Natural moisture content: \(w = 18\%\)
    • Liquid limit: \(w_L = 60\%\)
    • Plastic limit: \(w_P = 25\%\)
    • Percentage of clay-sized fraction (\(<2\,\mu\text{m}\)) \(= 25\%\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)) and Activity (\(A_c\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)): Range of moisture content over which soil remains plastic.
    \[I_P = w_L - w_P \]
  • Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)): Indicates proximity of natural water content to the liquid limit.
    \[I_L = \dfrac{w - w_P}{I_P} \]
  • Activity (\(A_c\)): Skempton's parameter measuring swelling/shrinkage potential of clay.
    \[A_c = \dfrac{I_P}{\%\text{ Clay Fraction}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(I_P\) using Atterberg limits.
  2. Substitute \(I_P\), \(w\), and \(w_P\) into the \(I_L\) formula.
  3. Substitute \(I_P\) and clay percentage into the \(A_c\) formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)):
    \[I_P = 60\% - 25\% = 35\% \]
  2. Calculate Liquidity Index (\(I_L\)):
    \[I_L = \dfrac{18\% - 25\%}{35\%} = \dfrac{-7}{35} = -0.2 \]A negative liquidity index indicates the soil is in a semi-solid state, which is valid since \(w < w_P\).
  3. Calculate Activity (\(A_c\)):
    \[A_c = \dfrac{35\%}{25\%} = 1.4 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(I_L = -0.2\) and \(A_c = 1.4\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: It is proposed to drive H-piles up to a depth of 7 m at a construction site. The average surface area of the H-pile is 3 m² per meter length. The soil at the site is homogeneous sand, having an effective friction angle of 32°. The ground water table (GWT) is at a depth of 2 m below the ground surface. The unit weights of the soil above and below the GWT are 16 kN/m³ and 19 kN/m³, respectively. Assume the earth pressure coefficient, K = 1.0, and the angle of wall friction, δ = 23°. The total axial frictional resistance (in kN, up to one decimal place) mobilized on the pile against the driving is _______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations (Pile Foundation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Pile length: \(L = 7\text{ m}\)
    • Pile perimeter: \(P = 3\text{ m}\) (surface area \(= 3\text{ m}^2/\text{m}\))
    • Depth of GWT \(= 2\text{ m}\)
    • Bulk unit weight above GWT: \(\gamma_{bulk} = 16\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Saturated unit weight below GWT: \(\gamma_{sat} = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Earth pressure coefficient: \(K = 1.0\)
    • Angle of wall friction: \(\delta = 23^\circ\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total axial frictional resistance (\(Q_s\)) along the pile shaft.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Skin Friction in Sand (IS 2911):
    \[Q_s = \sum_{i=1}^{n} (K \cdot \bar{\sigma}_{vi}' \cdot \tan\delta) \cdot (P \cdot \Delta L_i) \]where \(\bar{\sigma}_{vi}'\) = average vertical effective stress in layer \(i\).
  • Submerged unit weight: \(\gamma_{sub} = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w\), with \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\).

4. Solution Method:

Divide the soil profile into two layers at the GWT interface, compute average effective vertical stress for each layer, calculate frictional resistance, and sum them.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective stress at key depths:
    • At \(z = 0\text{ m}\): \(\sigma_v' = 0\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • At \(z = 2\text{ m}\): \(\sigma_v' = 16 \times 2 = 32\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • \(\gamma_{sub} = 19 - 9.81 = 9.19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • At \(z = 7\text{ m}\): \(\sigma_v' = 32 + (9.19 \times 5) = 32 + 45.95 = 77.95\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  2. Layer 1 (0 to 2 m):
    \[\bar{\sigma}_{v1}' = \dfrac{0 + 32}{2} = 16\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[f_{s1} = 1.0 \times 16 \times \tan(23^\circ) = 16 \times 0.42447 = 6.791\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[Q_{s1} = 6.791 \times (3 \times 2) = 6.791 \times 6 = 40.75\text{ kN} \]
  3. Layer 2 (2 to 7 m):
    \[\bar{\sigma}_{v2}' = \dfrac{32 + 77.95}{2} = 54.975\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[f_{s2} = 1.0 \times 54.975 \times \tan(23^\circ) = 54.975 \times 0.42447 = 23.335\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[Q_{s2} = 23.335 \times (3 \times 5) = 23.335 \times 15 = 350.03\text{ kN} \]
  4. Total frictional resistance:
    \[Q_s = Q_{s1} + Q_{s2} = 40.75 + 350.03 = 390.8\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 390.8 kN  |  Accepted key range: 385.0 to 392.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The infinite sand slope shown in the figure is on the verge of sliding failure. The ground water table coincides with the ground surface. Unit weight of water γ_w = 9.81 kN/m³.

The value of the effective angle of internal friction (in degrees, up to one decimal place) of the sand is _______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Slope Stability)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Slope inclination: \(\beta = 20^\circ\)
    • Slope on verge of sliding: \(FS = 1.0\)
    • Water table coincides with ground surface; seepage parallel to slope
    • \(\gamma_{sat} = 21\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the effective angle of internal friction (\(\phi'\)) of the sand.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Infinite Slope with Parallel Seepage: When seepage extends up to the ground surface, pore pressures reduce the effective normal stress on the failure plane. The factor of safety is:
    \[FS = \dfrac{\gamma_{sub}}{\gamma_{sat}} \cdot \dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta} \]where \(\gamma_{sub} = \gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w\).

4. Solution Method:

Enforce limiting equilibrium (\(FS = 1.0\)) and rearrange the infinite slope equation to solve directly for \(\phi'\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate submerged unit weight:
    \[\gamma_{sub} = 21 - 9.81 = 11.19\text{ kN/m}^3 \]
  2. Apply limiting equilibrium:
    \[1.0 = \dfrac{11.19}{21} \times \dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan 20^\circ} \]
  3. Solve for \(\phi'\):
    \[\tan 20^\circ = 0.36397 \]\[\tan\phi' = \dfrac{0.36397}{11.19/21} = \dfrac{0.36397}{0.53286} = 0.68305 \]\[\phi' = \arctan(0.68305) \approx 34.3^\circ \]
    Sanity Check: \(\phi' \approx 34^\circ\) is a typical realistic value for medium-dense sand. ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 34.3°  |  Accepted key range: 34.0 to 34.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A consolidated undrained (CU) triaxial compression test is conducted on a normally consolidated clay at a confining pressure of 100 kPa. The deviator stress at failure is 80 kPa, and the pore-water pressure measured at failure is 50 kPa. The effective angle of internal friction (in degrees, up to one decimal place) of the soil is _______________
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Test type: Consolidated Undrained (CU) triaxial test
    • Soil: Normally consolidated (NC) clay
    • Confining pressure: \(\sigma_3 = 100\text{ kPa}\)
    • Deviator stress at failure: \(\sigma_d = 80\text{ kPa}\)
    • Pore-water pressure at failure: \(u = 50\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Determine the effective angle of internal friction (\(\phi'\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Effective Stresses: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)
  • Principal Stresses: \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3 + \sigma_d\)
  • Mohr-Coulomb Criterion (NC clay, \(c' = 0\)):
    \[\sin\phi' = \dfrac{\sigma_1' - \sigma_3'}{\sigma_1' + \sigma_3'} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate total major principal stress \(\sigma_1\).
  2. Calculate effective principal stresses \(\sigma_1'\) and \(\sigma_3'\).
  3. Apply the effective stress Mohr-Coulomb criterion for \(c' = 0\) to solve for \(\phi'\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total principal stresses:
    \[\sigma_3 = 100\text{ kPa}, \quad \sigma_1 = 100 + 80 = 180\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Effective principal stresses:
    \[\sigma_3' = 100 - 50 = 50\text{ kPa}, \quad \sigma_1' = 180 - 50 = 130\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Calculate \(\phi'\):
    \[\sin\phi' = \dfrac{130 - 50}{130 + 50} = \dfrac{80}{180} = \dfrac{4}{9} = 0.4444 \]\[\phi' = \arcsin(0.4444) \approx 26.4^\circ \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 26.4°  |  Accepted key range: 25.5 to 27.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q4
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Let \( G \) be the specific gravity of soil solids, \( w \) the water content in the soil sample, \( \gamma_w \) the unit weight of water, and \( \gamma_d \) the dry unit weight of the soil. The equation for the zero air voids line in a compaction test plot is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Compaction)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall / Application
  • Given Data: \(G\) = Specific gravity of soil solids, \(w\) = Water content, \(\gamma_w\) = Unit weight of water, \(\gamma_d\) = Dry unit weight of soil.
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship representing the Zero Air Voids (ZAV) line on a compaction curve.

3. Core Concepts:

The fundamental phase relation for dry unit weight:\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1 + e} \]

The degree of saturation (\(S\)) relates void ratio (\(e\)), water content (\(w\)), and specific gravity (\(G\)):\[S \cdot e = w \cdot G \]

The Zero Air Voids (ZAV) line represents the maximum possible dry density for a given water content when the soil is 100% saturated (\(S = 1\)).

4. Solution Method:

Substitute the ZAV condition \(S = 1\) into the saturation equation to isolate \(e\), then substitute into the dry unit weight equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply ZAV condition (\(S = 1\)):\[1 \cdot e = w \cdot G \implies e = wG \]
  2. Substitute into the \(\gamma_d\) equation:\[\gamma_d = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1 + wG} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\gamma_d = \dfrac{G\,\gamma_w}{1 + Gw}\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q5
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Consider the following statements related to the pore pressure parameters, \( A \) and \( B \):
P. \( A \) always lies between 0 and 1.0
Q. \( A \) can be less than 0 or greater than 1.0
R. \( B \) always lies between 0 and 1.0
S. \( B \) can be less than 0 or greater than 1.0
For these statements, which one of the following options is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Effective Stress)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Analysis
  • Given Data: Statements regarding Skempton's pore pressure parameters \(A\) and \(B\).
  • Aim: Determine the physical bounds/ranges for parameters \(A\) and \(B\).

3. Core Concepts:

Skempton's pore water pressure equation:\[ \Delta u = B\left[\Delta\sigma_3 + A(\Delta\sigma_1 - \Delta\sigma_3)\right] \]

  • Parameter \(B\) (Isotropic behavior): Depends on the degree of saturation. For dry soil, \(B \approx 0\); for 100% saturated soil, \(B \approx 1\). Therefore: \(0 \le B \le 1\).
  • Parameter \(A\) (Shear behavior): Depends on OCR and tendency to dilate or contract.
    • Normally consolidated (NC) soils: \(A\) ranges from 0.5 to 1.0.
    • Highly sensitive clays: \(A > 1\).
    • Heavily overconsolidated (OC) clays or dense sands: soil dilates during shear → negative pore pressure → \(A < 0\).

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate each statement:

  • P. \(A\) always lies between 0 and 1.0 → False (violates dilation/sensitive clay mechanics).
  • Q. \(A\) can be less than 0 or greater than 1.0 → True.
  • R. \(B\) always lies between 0 and 1.0 → True (dictated by saturation limits).
  • S. \(B\) can be less than 0 or greater than 1.0 → False.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Correct combination comprises statements Q and R.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Q and R | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q6
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Consider a rigid retaining wall with partially submerged cohesionless backfill with a surcharge. Which one of the following diagrams closely represents the Rankine's active earth pressure distribution against this wall?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering (Earth Pressure)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Rigid retaining wall retaining a partially submerged, cohesionless (\(c = 0\)) backfill with a surface surcharge (\(q\)).
  • Aim: Identify the correct Rankine's active earth pressure diagram.

3. Core Concepts & Error Detection:

Expected Correct Pressure Profile:

  • At \(z = 0\) (Surface): \(p_a = K_a q\). The diagram must start with a non-zero positive value (surcharge effect).
  • Above Water Table: \(p_a = K_a q + K_a \gamma_{bulk} z\). Diagram slopes linearly with slope \(= K_a \gamma_{bulk}\).
  • Below Water Table: \(p_a = K_a \sigma'_v + u\). Total pressure slope \(= K_a \gamma' + \gamma_w\), which is much steeper than above the WT.

Using typical values (\(\gamma_{bulk} \approx 18 \text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\gamma' \approx 10 \text{ kN/m}^3\), \(\gamma_w \approx 10 \text{ kN/m}^3\), \(K_a \approx 0.33\)):

  • Slope above WT \(= 0.33 \times 18 \approx 6 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Slope below WT \(= 0.33 \times 10 + 10 \approx 13.3 \text{ kN/m}^3\)

The diagram must show a sharp outward bend at the water table level.

4. Solution Method:

  • Diagram (A): Starts from zero — missing the surcharge effect.
  • Diagram (B): Single trapezoid — fails to account for the sudden slope change at the water table.
  • Diagram (C): Strictly vertical right boundary at top — implies \(\gamma_{bulk} = 0\), which is physically impossible.
  • Diagram (D): Starts from zero at the top — missing the surcharge effect.

None of the diagrams correctly represent the described scenario.

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Flawed question — all diagrams are mechanically incorrect | Correct option: Mark to all

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q17
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The plate load test was conducted on a clayey strata by using a plate of \( 0.3 \text{ m} \times 0.3 \text{ m} \) dimensions, and the ultimate load per unit area for the plate was found to be 180 kPa. The ultimate bearing capacity (in kPa) of a 2 m wide square footing would be
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations (Bearing Capacity)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Plate shape: Square, dimensions \(0.3 \text{ m} \times 0.3 \text{ m}\)
    • Soil type: Clayey strata
    • Ultimate bearing capacity of plate: \(q_{up} = 180 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Footing shape: Square, width \(B_f = 2 \text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Find the ultimate bearing capacity of the square footing (\(q_{uf}\)) in kPa.

3. Core Concepts:

For purely cohesive soils (clay, \(\phi = 0^\circ\)) with a surface footing (\(D_f = 0\)), the bearing capacity reduces to:\[q_u = 1.3 \cdot c \cdot N_c \]

Key Takeaway: The ultimate bearing capacity for a footing on pure clay is completely independent of the footing width. It depends only on cohesion (\(c\)) and the shape of the footing.

4. Solution Method:

Since both the plate and the footing are square, their shape factors are identical. Because bearing capacity in pure clay is independent of width, \(q_{uf} = q_{up}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Bearing capacity of the square plate:\[q_{up} = 1.3 \cdot c \cdot N_c = 180 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Bearing capacity of the square footing:\[q_{uf} = 1.3 \cdot c \cdot N_c \]
  3. Equating the two expressions:\[q_{uf} = q_{up} = 180 \text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 180 kPa | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A sheet pile has an embedment depth of 12 m in a homogeneous soil stratum. The coefficient of permeability of soil is \( 10^{-6} \) m/s. Difference in the water levels between the two sides of the sheet pile is 4 m. The flow net is constructed with five number of flow lines and eleven number of equipotential lines. The quantity of seepage (in cm\(^3\)/s per m, up to one decimal place) under the sheet pile is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Seepage & Flow Nets)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Coefficient of permeability: \(k = 10^{-6} \text{ m/s}\)
    • Head difference: \(\Delta H = 4 \text{ m}\)
    • Number of flow lines = 5
    • Number of equipotential lines = 11
    • Embedment depth = 12 m (extraneous — not needed)
  • Aim: Calculate seepage per unit length in \(\text{cm}^3/\text{s per m}\) (1 decimal place).

3. Core Concepts:

Flow Net Characteristics:

  • Number of flow channels: \(N_f = \text{flow lines} - 1\)
  • Number of equipotential drops: \(N_d = \text{equipotential lines} - 1\)

Seepage Discharge Formula:\[q = k \cdot \Delta H \cdot \dfrac{N_f}{N_d} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine \(N_f\) and \(N_d\) from given lines.
  2. Compute seepage in base SI units, then convert to \(\text{cm}^3/\text{s per m}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(N_f = 5 - 1 = 4\),   \(N_d = 11 - 1 = 10\),   Shape factor \(= \dfrac{4}{10} = 0.4\)
  2. Seepage in SI units:\[q = 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 0.4 = 1.6 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3/\text{s per m} \]
  3. Convert \(\text{m}^3\) to \(\text{cm}^3\) (since \(1 \text{ m}^3 = 10^6 \text{ cm}^3\)):\[q = 1.6 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^6 = 1.6 \text{ cm}^3/\text{s per m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.6 cm³/s per m | Accepted key range: 1.6 to 1.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q34
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Two identical concrete piles having the plan dimensions \( 50 \text{ cm} \times 50 \text{ cm} \) are driven into a homogeneous sandy layer as shown in the figures. Consider the bearing capacity factor \( N_q \) for \( \phi = 30° \) as 24.


If \( Q_{p1} \) and \( Q_{p2} \) represent the ultimate point bearing resistances of the piles under dry and submerged conditions, respectively, which one of the following statements is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Plan dimensions of identical concrete piles: \(B \times B = 50 \text{ cm} \times 50 \text{ cm} = 0.5 \text{ m} \times 0.5 \text{ m}\)
    • Embedded Length: \(L = 20 \text{ m}\)
    • Bearing capacity factor: \(N_q = 24\), Friction angle: \(\phi = 30^\circ\)
    • Pile 1 (Dry sand): \(\gamma = 18 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Pile 2 (Submerged): \(\gamma_{sat} = 19 \text{ kN/m}^3\), Water table at ground level
  • Aim: Determine the relationship between the ultimate point bearing resistances \(Q_{p1}\) (dry) and \(Q_{p2}\) (submerged).

3. Core Concepts:

Ultimate Point Bearing Resistance in Sand:\[Q_p = q_p \cdot A_b = (\sigma_v' \cdot N_q) \cdot A_b \]where \(q_p\) is unit point bearing capacity, \(\sigma_v'\) is the effective vertical stress at the pile tip, and \(A_b\) is the base area.

Effective Stress (\(\sigma_v'\)):

  • Dry soil: \(\sigma_v' = \gamma \cdot L\)
  • Submerged soil: \(\sigma_v' = \gamma' \cdot L = (\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w) \cdot L\)

Standard unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w \approx 9.81 \text{ kN/m}^3\)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the effective stress at the tip of both piles. Since \(N_q\) and \(A_b\) are identical for both, the ratio of their point bearing capacities equals the ratio of their effective vertical stresses:\[\dfrac{Q_{p1}}{Q_{p2}} = \dfrac{\sigma_{v1}'}{\sigma_{v2}'} \]Then, determine the percentage by which \(Q_{p1}\) exceeds \(Q_{p2}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective stress for Pile 1 (Dry):\[\sigma_{v1}' = \gamma \cdot L = 18 \text{ kN/m}^3 \times 20 \text{ m} = 360 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Effective stress for Pile 2 (Submerged):
    Submerged unit weight: \(\gamma' = 19 - 9.81 = 9.19 \text{ kN/m}^3\)\[\sigma_{v2}' = \gamma' \cdot L = 9.19 \times 20 = 183.8 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Ratio and Percentage Difference:\[\dfrac{Q_{p1}}{Q_{p2}} = \dfrac{360}{183.8} = 1.958 \]\[\text{Percentage increase} = \left( \dfrac{Q_{p1} - Q_{p2}}{Q_{p2}} \right) \times 100 = (1.958 - 1) \times 100 = 95.8\% \approx 100\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(Q_{p1} > Q_{p2}\) by about 100% | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q35
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Following are the statements related to the stress paths in a triaxial testing of soils:
P. If \( \sigma_1 = \sigma_3 \), the stress point lies at the origin of the p-q plot.
Q. If \( \sigma_1 = \sigma_3 \), the stress point lies on the p-axis of the p-q plot.
R. If \( \sigma_1 > \sigma_3 \), both the stress points p and q are positive.

For the above statements, the correct combination is
options: P – False; Q – True; R – True
P – True; Q – False; R – True
P – False; Q – True; R – False
P – True; Q – False; R – False

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: P – False; Q – True; R – True
structuredOptions.html: P – False; Q – True; R – True

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: P – True; Q – False; R – True
structuredOptions.html: P – True; Q – False; R – True

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: P – False; Q – True; R – False
structuredOptions.html: P – False; Q – True; R – False

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: P – True; Q – False; R – False
structuredOptions.html: P – True; Q – False; R – False

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Three statements related to stress paths in triaxial testing.
  • Aim: Identify the correct True/False combination for statements P, Q, and R.

3. Core Concepts:

MIT Stress Path Parameters (p-q space):

  • \(p\) = Mean normal stress in 2D \(= \dfrac{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3}{2}\)
  • \(q\) = Maximum shear stress \(= \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{2}\)

Sign Convention in Geotechnics: Compressive stresses are considered positive (\(\sigma_1 \ge 0\), \(\sigma_3 \ge 0\)).

Hydrostatic / Isotropic State: When cell pressure equals axial pressure (\(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3\)).

4. Solution Method:

  • Evaluate P: If \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3\), then \(p = \sigma_1\) and \(q = 0\). The coordinate is \((\sigma_1, 0)\). This point lies on the p-axis, but not at the origin (unless \(\sigma_1 = 0\)). Therefore, P is False.
  • Evaluate Q: If \(\sigma_1 = \sigma_3\), the stress point coordinates are \((p, 0)\). By definition, any point with \(q = 0\) lies precisely on the p-axis. Therefore, Q is True.
  • Evaluate R: If \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_3\) and \(\sigma_3 > 0\), then \(p = \dfrac{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3}{2} > 0\) and \(q = \dfrac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{2} > 0\). Both coordinates are positive. Therefore, R is True.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Statement P claims the stress point is at the origin \((0,0)\). Reality is \((p, 0)\) where \(p \neq 0\). \(\rightarrow\) False
  2. Statement Q claims the point lies on the p-axis. Point is \((p, 0)\). \(\rightarrow\) True
  3. Statement R claims both coordinates are positive if \(\sigma_1 > \sigma_3\). Since \(p > 0\) and \(q > 0\). \(\rightarrow\) True
  4. Resulting combination: P – False; Q – True; R – True.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: P – False; Q – True; R – True | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q37
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
For the construction of a highway, a cut is to be made as shown in the figure.


The soil exhibits \( c' = 20 \) kPa, \( \phi' = 18° \), and the undrained shear strength = 80 kPa. The unit weight of water is 9.81 kN/m³. The unit weights of the soil above and below the ground water table are 18 and 20 kN/m³, respectively. If the shear stress at Point A is 50 kPa, the factors of safety against the shear failure at this point, considering the undrained and drained conditions, respectively, would be
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Undrained shear strength: \(S_u = 80 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Drained parameters: \(c' = 20 \text{ kPa}\), \(\phi' = 18^\circ\)
    • Unit weight above WT: \(\gamma = 18 \text{ kN/m}^3\) (Thickness = 2 m)
    • Unit weight below WT: \(\gamma_{sat} = 20 \text{ kN/m}^3\) (Thickness to point A = 4 m)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 9.81 \text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Applied shear stress at Point A: \(\tau = 50 \text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Factors of Safety (FOS) against shear failure at Point A for both undrained and drained conditions.

3. Core Concepts:

Factor of Safety (FOS):\[FOS = \dfrac{\text{Shear Strength } (\tau_f)}{\text{Applied Shear Stress } (\tau)} \]

Undrained Strength: Dictated completely by cohesion in short-term analysis: \(\tau_{f,u} = S_u\)

Drained Strength (Mohr-Coulomb): \(\tau_{f,d} = c' + \sigma_n' \tan \phi'\)

Normal Stress on Failure Plane (\(\sigma_n'\)): Point A represents the lowest tangential point of the potential circular shear surface. At this exact trough point, the failure plane is horizontal. Therefore, the effective normal stress (\(\sigma_n'\)) equals the effective vertical stress (\(\sigma_v'\)).

Effective Vertical Stress: \(\sigma_v' = \sigma_{v(\text{total})} - u\)

4. Solution Method:

  • Undrained FOS: Directly divide \(S_u\) by the applied shear stress.
  • Drained FOS: Calculate total vertical stress (\(\sigma_v\)) at Point A. Subtract pore water pressure (\(u\)) to get \(\sigma_v'\). Feed \(\sigma_v'\) into the Mohr-Coulomb equation to find \(\tau_{f,d}\). Divide \(\tau_{f,d}\) by applied shear stress.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Undrained FOS:\[FOS_{\text{undrained}} = \dfrac{S_u}{\tau} = \dfrac{80}{50} = 1.6 \]
  2. Total Vertical Stress (\(\sigma_v\)) at Point A:\[\sigma_v = (\gamma \times h_{\text{dry}}) + (\gamma_{sat} \times h_{\text{sub}}) = (18 \times 2) + (20 \times 4) = 36 + 80 = 116 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Pore Water Pressure (\(u\)) at Point A:\[u = \gamma_w \times h_{\text{sub}} = 9.81 \times 4 = 39.24 \text{ kPa} \]
  4. Effective Vertical Stress (\(\sigma_v'\)):\[\sigma_v' = \sigma_v - u = 116 - 39.24 = 76.76 \text{ kPa} \]
  5. Drained Shear Strength (\(\tau_{f,d}\)):\[\tau_{f,d} = c' + \sigma_v' \tan \phi' = 20 + 76.76 \times \tan(18^\circ) \]\[\tau_{f,d} = 20 + 76.76 \times 0.3249 \approx 20 + 24.94 = 44.94 \text{ kPa} \]
  6. Drained FOS:\[FOS_{\text{drained}} = \dfrac{\tau_{f,d}}{\tau} = \dfrac{44.94}{50} \approx 0.9 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(FOS_{\text{undrained}} = 1.6\) and \(FOS_{\text{drained}} = 0.9\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Consider a square-shaped area ABCD on the ground with its centre at M as shown in the figure. Four concentrated vertical loads of P = 5000 kN are applied on this area, one at each corner.


The vertical stress increment (in kPa, up to one decimal place) due to these loads according to the Boussinesq’s equation, at a point 5 m right below M, is ___________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Stress Distribution in Soil

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Square area ABCD with side \(a = 4 \text{ m}\)
    • Four concentrated vertical loads: \(P = 5000 \text{ kN}\) at each corner
    • Point of interest: depth \(z = 5 \text{ m}\) below the center \(M\)
  • Aim: Calculate the vertical stress increment (\(\Delta\sigma_z\)) at the specified point using Boussinesq's equation.

3. Core Concepts:

Boussinesq's Vertical Stress Increment:\[ \Delta\sigma_z = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi z^2} \left[1 + \left(\dfrac{r}{z}\right)^2 \right]^{-5/2} \]where \(r\) = radial horizontal distance from load to the point of interest.

Principle of Superposition: Total stress from multiple loads = algebraic sum of individual stresses.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine radial distance \(r\) from any corner load to the center point \(M\).
  2. Compute the single stress increment from one corner load at \(z = 5 \text{ m}\).
  3. Multiply by 4 (due to exact symmetry) to get the total stress increment.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Radial Distance (\(r\)):
    Distance from corner to center of a square with side \(a = 4 \text{ m}\):\[r = \dfrac{\sqrt{a^2 + a^2}}{2} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2.828 \text{ m} \]
  2. Boussinesq's Equation for One Load:
    \((r/z)^2 = (\sqrt{8}/5)^2 = 8/25 = 0.32\)
    \((1 + 0.32)^{-2.5} = (1.32)^{-2.5} \approx 0.49953\)\[\Delta\sigma_{z1} = \dfrac{3 \times 5000}{2\pi \times 25} \times 0.49953 = \dfrac{300}{\pi} \times 0.49953 \approx 47.702 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Superposition for All Four Loads:\[\Delta\sigma_z = 4 \times 47.702 = 190.8 \text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 190.8 kPa | Accepted key range: 187.0 to 192.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In the consolidated undrained triaxial test on a saturated soil sample, the pore water pressure is zero
options: at the end of consolidation stage only
both at the end of consolidation and during shearing stages
under none of the above conditions

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: at the end of consolidation stage only
structuredOptions.html: at the end of consolidation stage only

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: both at the end of consolidation and during shearing stages
structuredOptions.html: both at the end of consolidation and during shearing stages

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: under none of the above conditions
structuredOptions.html: under none of the above conditions

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soils — CU Triaxial Test

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: A consolidated undrained (CU) triaxial test on a saturated soil sample.
  • Aim: Identify the stage(s) at which pore water pressure is zero.

3. Core Concepts:

StageDrainage ValvePore Water Pressure
Consolidation StageOpen — water expelled until excess pore pressure dissipates\(u = 0\) at end
Shearing StageClosed — drainage prevented\(u \neq 0\) develops

4. Step-by-Step Execution:
