  2. At the end of Consolidation: Drainage is complete, all excess pore pressure has dissipated → \(u = 0\).

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Pore water pressure is zero at the end of the consolidation stage only | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A fine grained soil is found to be plastic in the water content range of 26-48%. As per Indian Standard Classification System, the soil is classified as
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Classification — IS 1498-1970

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Plastic Limit: \(w_P = 26\%\)
    • Liquid Limit: \(w_L = 48\%\)
  • Aim: Classify the soil per the Indian Standard Classification System (IS 1498-1970).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Plasticity Index: \(I_P = w_L - w_P\)
  • Compressibility suffix based on \(w_L\):
    • Low (L): \(w_L < 35\%\)
    • Intermediate (I): \(35\% \le w_L \le 50\%\)
    • High (H): \(w_L > 50\%\)
  • A-line equation: \(I_{P,\text{A-line}} = 0.73(w_L - 20)\)
    Soil above A-line → Clay (C); below → Silt/Organic (M or O)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compressibility suffix: \(w_L = 48\%\); since \(35\% \le 48\% \le 50\%\) → Intermediate (I)
  2. Actual \(I_P\): \(I_P = 48 - 26 = 22\%\)
  3. A-line \(I_P\): \(I_{P,\text{A-line}} = 0.73(48 - 20) = 0.73 \times 28 = 20.44\%\)
  4. Comparison: Actual \(I_P\) (22%) \(>\) A-line \(I_P\) (20.44%) → soil plots above the A-line → Clay (C)
  5. Classification: Prefix C + Suffix I = CI (Clay of Intermediate Compressibility)

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: CI | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A vertical cut is to be made in a soil mass having cohesion c, angle of internal friction φ, and unit weight γ. Considering Ka and Kp as the coefficients of active and passive earth pressures, respectively, the maximum depth of unsupported excavation is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theory — Maximum Depth of Unsupported Excavation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Cohesion \(= c\), angle of friction \(= \phi\), unit weight \(= \gamma\), active and passive coefficients \(K_a\) and \(K_p\).
  • Aim: Find the expression for the maximum depth of an unsupported vertical excavation.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Rankine's Active Earth Pressure at depth \(z\):\[p_a = K_a\gamma z - 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]
  • Depth of tension crack (\(z_c\)): Depth where \(p_a = 0\):\[z_c = \dfrac{2c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} \]
  • Maximum unsupported depth (\(H_c\)): Net active thrust = 0 at \(H_c = 2z_c\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \[H_c = 2z_c = 2 \times \dfrac{2c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}} \]
  2. This matches Option (D) exactly.
    Note: Since \(K_a = 1/K_p\), this can also be written as \(\dfrac{4c\sqrt{K_p}}{\gamma}\), but the direct standard form is \(\dfrac{4c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}}\).

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(H_c = \dfrac{4c}{\gamma\sqrt{K_a}}\) | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The porosity (n) and the degree of saturation (S) of a soil sample are 0.7 and 40%, respectively. In a 100 m3 volume of the soil, the volume (expressed in m3) of air is _______________
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Basic Properties of Soil

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Porosity: \(n = 0.7\)
    • Degree of saturation: \(S = 40\% = 0.4\)
    • Total volume of soil: \(V = 100\text{ m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the volume of air (\(V_a\)) in the soil sample.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Phase System of Soil:
    • \(V = V_s + V_v\) (Total volume = Solids + Voids)
    • \(V_v = V_w + V_a\) (Voids = Water + Air)
  • Porosity: \(n = \dfrac{V_v}{V}\)
  • Degree of Saturation: \(S = \dfrac{V_w}{V_v}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute total volume of voids (\(V_v\)) from porosity and total volume.
  2. Compute volume of water (\(V_w\)) from degree of saturation and \(V_v\).
  3. Subtract to find volume of air (\(V_a\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Volume of Voids (\(V_v\)):\[V_v = n \times V = 0.7 \times 100 = 70\text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Volume of Water (\(V_w\)):\[V_w = S \times V_v = 0.4 \times 70 = 28\text{ m}^3 \]
  3. Volume of Air (\(V_a\)):\[V_a = V_v - V_w = 70 - 28 = 42\text{ m}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 42 m³ | Accepted key range: [41.0, 43.0]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A homogeneous gravity retaining wall supporting a cohesionless backfill is shown in the figure. The lateral active earth pressure at the bottom of the wall is 40 kPa.



The minimum weight of the wall (expressed in kN per m length) required to prevent it from overturning about its toe (Point P) is
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Earth Pressure and Retaining Walls

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Wall height: \(H = 6\text{ m}\), Base width: \(B = 4\text{ m}\)
    • Active earth pressure at bottom: \(p_a = 40\text{ kPa}\)
    • Backfill is cohesionless → triangular pressure distribution (zero at top)
  • Aim: Calculate the minimum weight of the wall (\(W\) in kN/m run) for the wall to be on the verge of overturning about its toe (Point P), i.e. FOS against overturning = 1.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total Active Earth Pressure (\(P_a\)): Area of triangular pressure diagram:\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot p_a \cdot H \]
  • Overturning Moment (\(M_o\)): \(P_a\) acts at \(H/3\) from the base:\[M_o = P_a \times \dfrac{H}{3} \]
  • Restoring Moment (\(M_r\)): Wall self-weight \(W\) acts at \(B/2\) from the toe (centroid of rectangular section):\[M_r = W \times \dfrac{B}{2} \]
  • Limiting Condition: FOS = 1 \(\implies M_r = M_o\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate total horizontal active thrust \(P_a\).
  2. Calculate overturning moment \(M_o\) about the toe.
  3. Set restoring moment \(M_r\) equal to \(M_o\) and solve for minimum \(W\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Active Thrust (\(P_a\)):\[P_a = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 40 \times 6 = 120\text{ kN/m} \]
  2. Overturning Moment (\(M_o\)):
    Lever arm from toe \(= \dfrac{H}{3} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2\text{ m}\)\[M_o = 120 \times 2 = 240\text{ kNm/m} \]
  3. Minimum Wall Weight (\(W\)):
    Lever arm of wall weight from toe \(= \dfrac{B}{2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\text{ m}\)\[M_r = W \times 2 \]Setting \(M_r = M_o\):\[W \times 2 = 240 \implies W = 120\text{ kN/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 120 kN/m | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
An undisturbed soil sample was taken from the middle of a clay layer (i.e., 1.5 m below GL), as shown in figure. The water table was at the top of clay layer. Laboratory test results are as follows:

Natural water content of clay:25%
Preconsolidation pressure of clay:60 kPa
Compression index of clay:0.50
Recompression index of clay:0.05
Specific gravity of clay:2.70
Bulk unit weight of sand:17 kN/m3

A compacted fill of 2.5 m height with unit weight of 20 kN/m3 is placed at the ground level.



Assuming unit weight of water as 10 kN/m3, the ultimate consolidation settlement (expressed in mm) of the clay layer is _______________
questions.explanation:
Soil Mechanics | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data (from diagram and text):
    • Soil Profile: 1.0 m Sand (GL to GWT) + 1.0 m Clay (GWT to Hard Stratum); sample from middle of clay = 1.5 m below GL
    • Sand: \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Clay: water content \(w = 25\%\), specific gravity \(G = 2.70\), preconsolidation pressure \(\sigma'_c = 60\text{ kPa}\), compression index \(C_c = 0.50\), recompression index \(C_r = 0.05\)
    • Applied load: compacted fill of height \(= 2.5\text{ m}\), \(\gamma_{fill} = 20\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate ultimate consolidation settlement (\(S_c\)) of the clay layer in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Phase Relations for Saturated Clay (\(S = 1\)):\[e_0 = \dfrac{w \cdot G}{S}, \quad \gamma_{sat} = \dfrac{G + e}{1 + e}\,\gamma_w \]
  • Consolidation State: If \(\sigma'_{v0} < \sigma'_c\), soil is Overconsolidated (OC). If final stress \(\sigma'_{vf} > \sigma'_c\), settlement involves both recompression (\(C_r\)) and virgin compression (\(C_c\)) phases.
  • Dual-Index Settlement Equation:\[ S_c = H\left[\dfrac{C_r}{1+e_0}\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{\sigma'_c}{\sigma'_{v0}}\right) + \dfrac{C_c}{1+e_0}\log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{\sigma'_{vf}}{\sigma'_c}\right)\right] \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate void ratio (\(e_0\)) and saturated unit weight (\(\gamma_{sat}\)) for clay.
  2. Compute initial effective stress (\(\sigma'_{v0}\)) at mid-clay (depth = 1.5 m).
  3. Compare \(\sigma'_{v0}\) with \(\sigma'_c\) to verify OC state.
  4. Compute applied stress increment (\(\Delta\sigma\)) from fill and find final effective stress (\(\sigma'_{vf}\)).
  5. Apply the dual-index settlement equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Clay Volumetrics:\[e_0 = \dfrac{0.25 \times 2.70}{1.0} = 0.675 \]\[\gamma_{sat,clay} = \dfrac{2.70 + 0.675}{1 + 0.675} \times 10 = \dfrac{3.375}{1.675} \times 10 \approx 20.149\text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\gamma'_{clay} = 20.149 - 10 = 10.149\text{ kN/m}^3 \]
  2. Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_{v0}\)) at mid-clay (\(z = 1.5\text{ m}\)):
    • From 1.0 m sand (bulk): \(17 \times 1.0 = 17\text{ kPa}\)
    • From 0.5 m clay (submerged): \(10.149 \times 0.5 = 5.075\text{ kPa}\)
    \[\sigma'_{v0} = 17 + 5.075 = 22.075\text{ kPa} \]
  3. State Verification and Final Stress:
    Since \(\sigma'_{v0} = 22.075\text{ kPa} < \sigma'_c = 60\text{ kPa}\) → Clay is Overconsolidated.
    Surcharge from fill: \(\Delta\sigma = 2.5 \times 20 = 50\text{ kPa}\)
    \[\sigma'_{vf} = 22.075 + 50 = 72.075\text{ kPa} \]Since \(72.075 > 60\), the stress crosses into the virgin compression zone.
  4. Consolidation Settlement (\(S_c\)):
    Clay thickness \(H = 1.0\text{ m} = 1000\text{ mm}\)
    \[\dfrac{H}{1+e_0} = \dfrac{1000}{1.675} \approx 597.015\text{ mm} \]
    Recompression segment (\(\sigma'_{v0}\) to \(\sigma'_c\)):\[\Delta H_1 = 597.015 \times 0.05 \times \log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{60}{22.075}\right) = 29.851 \times \log_{10}(2.718) \approx 29.851 \times 0.4343 \approx 12.96\text{ mm} \]Virgin compression segment (\(\sigma'_c\) to \(\sigma'_{vf}\)):\[\Delta H_2 = 597.015 \times 0.50 \times \log_{10}\!\left(\dfrac{72.075}{60}\right) = 298.507 \times \log_{10}(1.2012) \approx 298.507 \times 0.07963 \approx 23.77\text{ mm} \]Total Ultimate Settlement:\[S_c = \Delta H_1 + \Delta H_2 = 12.96 + 23.77 = 36.73\text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 36.73 mm | Accepted key range: [36.0, 38.0]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A seepage flow condition is shown in the figure. The saturated unit weight of the soil \( \gamma_{sat} = 18 \) kN/m3. Using unit weight of water, \( \gamma_w = 9.81 \) kN/m3, the effective vertical stress (expressed in kN/m2) on plane X-X is _______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Seepage & Effective Stress

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Saturated unit weight of soil: \(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Length of soil block: \(L = 5 + 1 = 6\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of plane X-X from top of soil: \(z = 5\text{ m}\)
    • Head difference across soil: \(\Delta H = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Height of free water above soil: \(H_w = 4\text{ m}\) (from diagram)
  • Aim: Find the effective vertical stress (\(\sigma'\)) on plane X-X in kN/m².

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total Stress (\(\sigma\)): Total weight of all material (soil + water) per unit area above the plane.
  • Pore Water Pressure (\(u\)): Hydrostatic pressure from water in soil voids; in seepage, based on pressure head at that point.
  • Effective Stress Principle (Terzaghi): \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)
  • Head Loss in Seepage: Head is lost linearly across the length of soil in steady flow.\[i = \dfrac{\Delta H}{L} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine flow direction and hydraulic gradient.
  2. Calculate total stress (\(\sigma\)) at plane X-X.
  3. Calculate pore water pressure (\(u\)) at plane X-X by tracking head loss.
  4. Compute effective stress (\(\sigma'\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Flow Analysis:
    Set datum at the top of the soil (\(Z = 0\)).
    Total head at top boundary: \(H_{top} = +4\text{ m}\)
    Total head at bottom boundary: \(H_{bot} = +1\text{ m}\)
    Since \(H_{top} > H_{bot}\), flow is downward.\[i = \dfrac{\Delta H}{L} = \dfrac{4 - 1}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5 \]
  2. Total Stress (\(\sigma\)) at X-X:
    Plane X-X carries 4 m of free water + 5 m of saturated soil above it.\[\sigma = (\gamma_w \times H_w) + (\gamma_{sat} \times z) = (9.81 \times 4) + (18 \times 5) = 39.24 + 90 = 129.24\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Pore Water Pressure (\(u\)) at X-X:
    Head loss from top of soil to plane X-X (\(z = 5\text{ m}\)):\[h_{loss} = i \times z = 0.5 \times 5 = 2.5\text{ m} \]Total head at X-X:\[H_x = H_{top} - h_{loss} = 4 - 2.5 = 1.5\text{ m} \]Elevation head at X-X (5 m below datum): \(Z_x = -5\text{ m}\)
    Pressure head at X-X:\[H_x = h_p + Z_x \implies 1.5 = h_p + (-5) \implies h_p = 6.5\text{ m} \]\[u = h_p \times \gamma_w = 6.5 \times 9.81 = 63.765\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Effective Stress (\(\sigma'\)):\[\sigma' = \sigma - u = 129.24 - 63.765 = 65.475\text{ kPa} \]
    Alternative check via seepage force:\[\sigma' = z\gamma' + iz\gamma_w = 5(18-9.81) + 0.5(5)(9.81) = 40.95 + 24.525 = 65.475\text{ kPa} \checkmark \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 65.475 kPa | Accepted key range: [65.3, 65.6]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A drained triaxial compression test on a saturated clay yielded the effective shear strength parameters as \( c' = 15 \) kPa and \( \phi' = 22^\circ \). Consolidated Undrained triaxial test on an identical sample of this clay at a cell pressure of 200 kPa developed a pore water pressure of 150 kPa at failure. The deviator stress (expressed in kPa) at failure is _______________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Effective cohesion: \(c' = 15\text{ kPa}\)
    • Effective friction angle: \(\phi' = 22^\circ\)
    • Cell pressure (total minor principal stress): \(\sigma_3 = 200\text{ kPa}\)
    • Pore water pressure at failure: \(u_f = 150\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Find the deviator stress (\(\sigma_d\)) at failure in kPa.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Effective Stress: \(\sigma' = \sigma - u\)
  • Deviator Stress: \(\sigma_d = \sigma_1 - \sigma_3 = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3'\) (same in total and effective stress terms)
  • Mohr-Coulomb Failure Criterion (effective stress):\[\sigma_1' = \sigma_3'\tan^2\!\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi'}{2}\right) + 2c'\tan\!\left(45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi'}{2}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine effective minor principal stress (\(\sigma_3'\)).
  2. Calculate flow value \(N_\phi = \tan^2(45^\circ + \phi'/2)\).
  3. Use Mohr-Coulomb equation to compute effective major principal stress (\(\sigma_1'\)).
  4. Find deviator stress \(\sigma_d = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3'\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Effective Minor Principal Stress:\[\sigma_3' = \sigma_3 - u_f = 200 - 150 = 50\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Flow Value (\(N_\phi\)):\[45^\circ + \dfrac{\phi'}{2} = 45^\circ + 11^\circ = 56^\circ \]\[\sqrt{N_\phi} = \tan(56^\circ) = 1.48256 \]\[N_\phi = \tan^2(56^\circ) \approx 2.198 \]
  3. Effective Major Principal Stress:\[\sigma_1' = (50 \times 2.198) + (2 \times 15 \times 1.48256) = 109.9 + 44.477 = 154.377\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Deviator Stress:\[\sigma_d = \sigma_1' - \sigma_3' = 154.377 - 50 = 104.377\text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 104.38 kPa | Accepted key range: [100, 110]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q46
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
Seepage is occurring through a porous media shown in the figure. The hydraulic conductivity values (\( k_1, k_2, k_3 \)) are in m/day.



The seepage discharge (m3/day per m) through the porous media at section PQ is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics — Permeability & Seepage

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Horizontal confined flow through three soil zones in series
    • Aquifer thickness: \(D = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Zone 1: \(k_1 = 2\text{ m/day}\), \(L_1 = 20\text{ m}\)
    • Zone 2: \(k_2 = 3\text{ m/day}\), \(L_2 = 30\text{ m}\)
    • Zone 3: \(k_3 = 1\text{ m/day}\), \(L_3 = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Total head drop: \(\Delta H = 15 - 10 = 5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Determine steady seepage discharge per meter width (\(q\)) through section PQ in m³/day/m.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Continuity: In steady-state flow, discharge through any cross-section is constant.
  • Darcy's Law: \(Q = k_{eq} \cdot i \cdot A\)
  • Equivalent Permeability for Layers in Series (flow perpendicular to strata):\[k_{eq} = \dfrac{\sum L_i}{\sum \left(\dfrac{L_i}{k_i}\right)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute equivalent hydraulic conductivity (\(k_{eq}\)) for series flow.
  2. Compute the global hydraulic gradient (\(i\)).
  3. Apply Darcy's law for discharge per unit width.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Equivalent Permeability:\[\sum L_i = 20 + 30 + 10 = 60\text{ m} \]\[\sum\dfrac{L_i}{k_i} = \dfrac{20}{2} + \dfrac{30}{3} + \dfrac{10}{1} = 10 + 10 + 10 = 30\text{ days} \]\[k_{eq} = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2\text{ m/day} \]
  2. Hydraulic Gradient:\[i = \dfrac{\Delta H}{L} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12} \]
  3. Seepage Discharge per Meter Width:
    Area of flow per meter width: \(A = 3 \times 1 = 3\text{ m}^2/\text{m}\)\[q = k_{eq} \times i \times A = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{12} \times 3 = \dfrac{6}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{ m}^3/\text{day/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(q = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{ m}^3/\text{day/m}\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q11
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A strip footing is resting on the surface of a purely clayey soil deposit. If the width of the footing is doubled, the ultimate bearing capacity of the soil
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Bearing Capacity of Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Strip footing on purely clayey deposit (\(\phi = 0^\circ\)). Width of the footing (\(B\)) is doubled.
  • Aim: Determine the effect of doubling the width on the ultimate bearing capacity (\(q_u\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity Theory for a strip footing:

\[q_u = cN_c + qN_q + 0.5\gamma B N_\gamma \]

where \(N_c, N_q, N_\gamma\) are bearing capacity factors depending purely on \(\phi\).

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate Terzaghi's equation for the specific condition of purely cohesive clay (\(\phi = 0^\circ\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Bearing capacity factors at \(\phi = 0^\circ\):
    \(N_c = 5.14\), \(N_q = 1.0\), \(N_\gamma = 0\)
  2. Simplified bearing capacity equation:\[q_u = 5.14c + q + 0.5\gamma B(0) = 5.14c + q \]
  3. Effect of width:
    The simplified equation contains no variable \(B\). Doubling the width has no effect on \(q_u\). The ultimate bearing capacity remains unchanged.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: remains the same | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q12
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The relationship between the specific gravity of sand \((G)\) and the hydraulic gradient \((i)\) to initiate quick condition in the sand layer having porosity of 30% is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage & Quick Sand Condition

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Sand with porosity \(n = 0.30\).
  • Aim: Establish the relationship between specific gravity (\(G\)) and critical hydraulic gradient (\(i\)) for the quicksand condition.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Quick Sand Condition: Occurs when upward seepage force nullifies the submerged weight of the soil (effective stress → zero).
  • Critical Hydraulic Gradient:\[i_c = \dfrac{G - 1}{1 + e} \]
  • Porosity to Void Ratio: \(e = \dfrac{n}{1 - n}\)

4. Solution Method:

Find void ratio from porosity, substitute into the critical hydraulic gradient expression, and rearrange for \(G\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate void ratio (\(e\)):\[e = \dfrac{0.3}{1 - 0.3} = \dfrac{0.3}{0.7} = \dfrac{3}{7} \]
  2. Substitute into the critical gradient formula:\[i = \dfrac{G - 1}{1 + \dfrac{3}{7}} = \dfrac{G - 1}{\dfrac{10}{7}} = 0.7(G - 1) \]
  3. Rearrange to solve for \(G\):\[G - 1 = \dfrac{i}{0.7} \implies G = 1.43i + 1 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(G = 1.43i + 1\) | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
The results of a consolidation test on an undisturbed soil, sampled at a depth of 10 m below the ground level are as follows:

Saturated unit weight      :      16 kN/m³
Pre-consolidation pressure      :      90 kPa

The water table was encountered at the ground level. Assuming the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³, the over-consolidation ratio of the soil is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Compressibility & Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Depth of sample \(z = 10\text{ m}\)
    • Saturated unit weight \(\gamma_{sat} = 16\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Pre-consolidation pressure \(\sigma_c' = 90\text{ kPa}\)
    • Water table at ground level
    • \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Over-Consolidation Ratio (OCR).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Effective Stress: \(\sigma_0' = (\gamma_{sat} - \gamma_w) \times z = \gamma' \times z\)
  • Over-Consolidation Ratio: \(OCR = \dfrac{\sigma_c'}{\sigma_0'}\)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate in-situ effective stress at 10 m depth, then divide the pre-consolidation pressure by this value.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Submerged unit weight (\(\gamma'\)):\[\gamma' = 16 - 10 = 6\text{ kN/m}^3 \]
  2. In-situ effective vertical stress (\(\sigma_0'\)):\[\sigma_0' = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ kPa} \]
  3. OCR:\[OCR = \dfrac{90}{60} = 1.50 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.50 | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q40
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The seepage occurring through an earthen dam is represented by a flownet comprising of 10 equipotential drops and 20 flow channels. The coefficient of permeability of the soil is 3 mm/min and the head loss is 5 m. The rate of seepage (expressed in cm³/s per m length of the dam) through the earthen dam is _________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage & Flownets

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Equipotential drops: \(N_d = 10\)
    • Flow channels: \(N_f = 20\)
    • Coefficient of permeability: \(k = 3\text{ mm/min}\)
    • Total head loss: \(\Delta H = 5\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the seepage rate in \(\text{cm}^3/\text{s}\) per meter length of the dam.

3. Core Concepts:

Darcy's Law applied to Flownets: The total discharge per unit length of the dam (\(q\)) is:

\[q = k \cdot \Delta H \cdot \dfrac{N_f}{N_d} \]

Total rate for a specific length \(L\) is \(Q = q \cdot L\).

4. Solution Method:

Convert all input parameters into a consistent unit system (centimeters and seconds) to arrive directly at the required final units (\(\text{cm}^3/\text{s}\) per m).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert \(k\) to cm/s:\[k = 3\text{ mm/min} = \dfrac{0.3\text{ cm}}{60\text{ s}} = 0.005\text{ cm/s} \]
  2. Convert \(\Delta H\) to cm:\[\Delta H = 5\text{ m} = 500\text{ cm} \]
  3. Calculate flow per unit length (\(q\)) in \(\text{cm}^2/\text{s}\):\[q = 0.005 \times 500 \times \dfrac{20}{10} = 2.5 \times 2 = 5\text{ cm}^2/\text{s} \]
  4. Calculate total flow (\(Q\)) per meter (\(L = 100\text{ cm}\)) length:\[Q = q \times L = 5 \times 100 = 500\text{ cm}^3/\text{s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 500 cm³/s | Accepted key range: 495 to 505

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q41
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: The soil profile at a site consists of a 5 m thick sand layer underlain by a c-φ soil as shown in figure. The water table is found 1 m below the ground level. The entire soil mass is retained by a concrete retaining wall and is in the active state. The back of the wall is smooth and vertical. The total active earth pressure (expressed in kN/m²) at point A as per Rankine's theory is _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure Theory

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Water table at \(1\text{ m}\) below GL. \(\gamma_w = 9.81\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Layer 1 (0–1 m): Dry Sand, \(\gamma_{bulk} = 16.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Layer 2 (1–5 m): Saturated Sand, \(\gamma_{sat} = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Layer 3 (5–8 m): \(c\)-\(\phi\) soil, \(\gamma_{sat} = 18.5\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(c' = 25\text{ kN/m}^2\), \(\phi' = 24^\circ\)
  • Aim: Find the total active earth pressure at Point A (depth = \(8\text{ m}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Rankine's Active Earth Pressure for \(c\)-\(\phi\) soil:

\[p_a' = k_a \sigma_v' - 2c'\sqrt{k_a} \]\[k_a = \tan^2\left(45^\circ - \dfrac{\phi'}{2}\right) \]

Total Earth Pressure: \(p_{\text{total}} = p_a' + u\) (where \(u\) is the pore water pressure)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the effective vertical stress (\(\sigma_v'\)) at point A.
  2. Calculate the active earth pressure coefficient (\(k_a\)) for the \(c\)-\(\phi\) soil.
  3. Determine the effective active earth pressure (\(p_a'\)).
  4. Add the hydrostatic pore water pressure (\(u\)) to get the total active earth pressure.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Pore Water Pressure (\(u\)) at \(8\text{ m}\):\[u = 9.81 \times (8 - 1) = 68.67\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  2. Effective Vertical Stress (\(\sigma_v'\)) at \(8\text{ m}\):\[\gamma_{\text{sub, sand}} = 19 - 9.81 = 9.19\text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\gamma_{\text{sub, }c\text{-}\phi} = 18.5 - 9.81 = 8.69\text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\sigma_v' = (1 \times 16.5) + (4 \times 9.19) + (3 \times 8.69) = 16.5 + 36.76 + 26.07 = 79.33\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  3. Active Earth Pressure Coefficient (\(k_a\)):\[k_a = \tan^2(45^\circ - 12^\circ) = \tan^2(33^\circ) \approx 0.42173 \]\[\sqrt{k_a} = \tan(33^\circ) \approx 0.64941 \]
  4. Effective Active Pressure (\(p_a'\)):\[p_a' = (0.42173 \times 79.33) - (2 \times 25 \times 0.64941) = 33.456 - 32.470 = 0.986\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  5. Total Active Earth Pressure (\(p_A\)):\[p_A = p_a' + u = 0.986 + 68.67 = 69.656\text{ kN/m}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 69.66 kN/m² | Accepted key range: 69.0 to 70.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q42
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: OMC-SP and MDD-SP denote the optimum moisture content and maximum dry density obtained from standard Proctor compaction test, respectively. OMC-MP and MDD-MP denote the optimum moisture content and maximum dry density obtained from the modified Proctor compaction test, respectively. Which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Compaction of Soils

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall & Comprehension
  • Given Data: OMC and MDD for Standard Proctor (SP) and Modified Proctor (MP) tests.
  • Aim: Identify the correct relationship between the parameters of the two tests.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Standard vs Modified Proctor: The Modified Proctor test utilizes a significantly higher compactive effort (4.89 kg rammer / 450 mm drop / 5 layers) compared to the Standard Proctor test (2.6 kg rammer / 310 mm drop / 3 layers).
  • Effect on Soil State: An increase in compactive energy forces soil particles closer together. This achieves a higher Maximum Dry Density (MDD) while requiring slightly less water lubrication, thus dropping the Optimum Moisture Content (OMC).

4. Solution Method:

  • Higher Energy → Higher density → MDD-MP > MDD-SP
  • Higher Energy → Lower required moisture → OMC-MP < OMC-SP

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

OptionMDD RelationshipOMC RelationshipCorrect?
(A)MDD-SP < MDD-MP ✓OMC-SP < OMC-MP ✗No
(B)MDD-SP < MDD-MP ✓OMC-SP > OMC-MP ✓Yes
(C)MDD-SP > MDD-MP ✗—No
(D)MDD-SP > MDD-MP ✗—No

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: OMC-SP > OMC-MP and MDD-SP < MDD-MP | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q43
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Water flows from P to Q through two soil samples, Soil 1 and Soil 2, having cross sectional area of 80 cm² as shown in the figure. Over a period of 15 minutes, 200 ml of water was observed to pass through any cross section. The flow conditions can be assumed to be steady state. If the coefficient of permeability of Soil 1 is 0.02 mm/s, the coefficient of permeability of Soil 2 (expressed in mm/s) would be _________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Permeability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Cross-sectional area \(A = 80\text{ cm}^2 = 8000\text{ mm}^2\)
    • Volume of water collected \(V = 200\text{ ml} = 200 \times 10^3\text{ mm}^3\)
    • Time interval \(t = 15\text{ min} = 900\text{ s}\)
    • Lengths of soils: \(L_1 = 150\text{ mm}\), \(L_2 = 150\text{ mm}\)
    • Permeability of Soil 1: \(k_1 = 0.02\text{ mm/s}\)
    • Head at P (upstream): \(H_P = 600\text{ mm}\)
    • Head at Q (downstream): \(H_Q = 300\text{ mm}\)
  • Aim: Find the coefficient of permeability of Soil 2 (\(k_2\)) in mm/s.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Darcy's Law: \(Q = k_{eq} \cdot i_{eq} \cdot A\)
  • Flow through Stratified Soils (Series): When flow is perpendicular to the soil interfaces:
    • Discharge (\(q\)) is constant across all layers.
    • Total head loss is the sum of individual losses: \(\Delta H = \Delta h_1 + \Delta h_2\).
    • Equivalent permeability: \(k_{eq} = \dfrac{L_{\text{total}}}{\dfrac{L_1}{k_1} + \dfrac{L_2}{k_2}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the steady-state discharge (\(q = V/t\)) in mm³/s.
  2. Determine total head loss and compute equivalent permeability (\(k_{eq}\)) using Darcy's law.
  3. Substitute \(k_{eq}\) into the series-flow formula to solve for \(k_2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Discharge (\(q\)):\[q = \dfrac{200 \times 10^3}{900} = 222.22\text{ mm}^3/\text{s} \]
  2. Calculate Equivalent Permeability (\(k_{eq}\)):
    Total length \(L = 300\text{ mm}\), Total head loss \(\Delta H = 300\text{ mm}\)
    Hydraulic gradient \(i_{eq} = 300/300 = 1\)\[222.22 = k_{eq} \times 1 \times 8000 \implies k_{eq} = 0.027778\text{ mm/s} \]
  3. Solve for \(k_2\):\[0.027778 = \dfrac{300}{\dfrac{150}{0.02} + \dfrac{150}{k_2}} \]\[7500 + \dfrac{150}{k_2} = \dfrac{300}{0.027778} = 10800 \]\[\dfrac{150}{k_2} = 3300 \implies k_2 = \dfrac{150}{3300} = 0.04545\text{ mm/s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.045 mm/s | Accepted key range: 0.04 to 0.05

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q44
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 4 m wide strip footing is founded at a depth of 1.5 m below the ground surface in a c-φ soil as shown in the figure. The water table is at a depth of 5.5 m below ground surface. The soil properties are: \( c' = 35 \text{ kN/m}^2 \), \( \phi' = 28.63^\circ \), \( \gamma_{sat} = 19 \text{ kN/m}^3 \), \( \gamma_{bulk} = 17 \text{ kN/m}^3 \) and \( \gamma_w = 9.81 \text{ kN/m}^3 \). The values of bearing capacity factors for different \( \phi' \) are given below.

\( \phi' \)\( N_c \)\( N_q \)\( N_\gamma \)
15°12.94.42.5
20°17.77.45.0
25°25.112.79.7
30°37.222.519.7



Using Terzaghi's bearing capacity equation and a factor of safety \( F_s = 2.5 \), the net safe bearing capacity (expressed in kN/m²) for local shear failure of the soil is _________
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Width of strip footing \(B = 4\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of foundation \(D_f = 1.5\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of Water Table (WT) from surface \(= 5.5\text{ m}\)
    • Soil cohesion \(c' = 35\text{ kN/m}^2\), Friction angle \(\phi' = 28.63^\circ\)
    • Saturated unit weight \(\gamma_{sat} = 19\text{ kN/m}^3\), Bulk unit weight \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Factor of safety \(F_s = 2.5\)
  • Aim: Calculate the net safe bearing capacity (\(q_{ns}\)) for local shear failure.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Local Shear Failure Modification: Mobilized strength parameters are reduced:\[c'_m = \dfrac{2}{3}c' \quad \text{and} \quad \phi'_m = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\tan\phi'\right) \]
  • Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity Equation (Strip Footing):\[q_{nu} = c'_m N_c' + \gamma_1 D_f (N_q' - 1) + 0.5\,\gamma_2 B N_\gamma' \]
  • Water Table Correction: If the water table depth from the base (\(d_w\)) is \(\ge B\), the WT has no effect and \(\gamma_{bulk}\) is used throughout.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the reduced shear strength parameters (\(c'_m, \phi'_m\)) and find corresponding bearing capacity factors from the given table.
  2. Check WT depth relative to the foundation base.
  3. Compute the net ultimate bearing capacity (\(q_{nu}\)) using Terzaghi's equation.
  4. Divide \(q_{nu}\) by the factor of safety to find \(q_{ns}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mobilized Shear Strength Parameters:\[c'_m = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 35 = 23.333\text{ kN/m}^2 \]\[\tan\phi'_m = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \tan(28.63^\circ) = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 0.5459 = 0.3639 \implies \phi'_m \approx 20^\circ \]From the table for \(\phi' = 20^\circ\): \(N_c' = 17.7,\; N_q' = 7.4,\; N_\gamma' = 5.0\)
  2. Water Table Consideration:
    Depth of WT below base: \(d_w = 5.5 - 1.5 = 4.0\text{ m}\).
    Since \(d_w = 4.0\text{ m} = B\), the WT is at the boundary of the influence zone. Use \(\gamma_{bulk} = 17\text{ kN/m}^3\) for all terms.
  3. Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_{nu}\)):\[q_{nu} = (23.333 \times 17.7) + (17 \times 1.5 \times (7.4 - 1)) + (0.5 \times 17 \times 4 \times 5.0) \]\[q_{nu} = 413.00 + 163.2 + 170.0 = 746.2\text{ kN/m}^2 \]
  4. Net Safe Bearing Capacity (\(q_{ns}\)):\[q_{ns} = \dfrac{q_{nu}}{F_s} = \dfrac{746.2}{2.5} = 298.48\text{ kN/m}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 298.48 kN/m² | Accepted key range: 298 to 300

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A tracer takes 100 days to travel from Well-1 to Well-2 which are 100 m apart. The elevation of water surface in Well-2 is 3 m below that in Well-1. Assuming porosity equal to 15%, the coefficient of permeability (expressed in m/day) is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage and Permeability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Travel time of tracer: \(t = 100\text{ days}\)
    • Seepage path length: \(L = 100\text{ m}\)
    • Head difference: \(\Delta h = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Soil porosity: \(n = 0.15\)
  • Aim: Find the coefficient of permeability (\(k\)) in m/day.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Seepage Velocity vs. Discharge Velocity: A tracer measures the actual physical speed of water traveling through the void spaces — the seepage velocity (\(v_s\)). Darcy's Law uses discharge velocity (\(v\)), which assumes flow through the entire cross-sectional area.
  • Relation: \(v = n \cdot v_s\)
  • Darcy's Law: \(v = k \cdot i\), where \(i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute seepage velocity (\(v_s\)) using distance over time.
  2. Convert to Darcy's discharge velocity (\(v\)) using soil porosity.
  3. Calculate hydraulic gradient (\(i\)).
  4. Compute permeability (\(k\)) using Darcy's equation.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Seepage Velocity (\(v_s\)):\[v_s = \dfrac{L}{t} = \dfrac{100}{100} = 1\text{ m/day} \]
  2. Discharge Velocity (\(v\)):\[v = n \cdot v_s = 0.15 \times 1 = 0.15\text{ m/day} \]
  3. Hydraulic Gradient (\(i\)):\[i = \dfrac{\Delta h}{L} = \dfrac{3}{100} = 0.03 \]
  4. Permeability Coefficient (\(k\)):\[k = \dfrac{v}{i} = \dfrac{0.15}{0.03} = 5.00\text{ m/day} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 5.00 m/day | Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q21
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A fine-grained soil has 60% (by weight) silt content. The soil behaves as semi-solid when water content is between 15% and 28%. The soil behaves fluid-like when the water content is more than 40%. The ‘Activity’ of the soil is
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Index Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension & Application
  • Given Data:
    • Soil type: Fine-grained
    • Silt content = 60% (by weight)
    • Semi-solid state water content range = 15% to 28%
    • Fluid-like state water content > 40%
  • Aim: Calculate the Activity of the soil.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Atterberg Limits:
    • Plastic Limit (\(w_P\)): Boundary between semi-solid and plastic states
    • Liquid Limit (\(w_L\)): Boundary between plastic and liquid (fluid-like) states
  • Plasticity Index: \(I_P = w_L - w_P\)
  • Activity of Soil: \[A = \frac{I_P}{\%\text{ Clay fraction}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify \(w_P\) and \(w_L\) from the given state boundaries.
  2. Calculate Plasticity Index (\(I_P\)).
  3. Determine clay content fraction.
  4. Calculate Activity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify Limits:
    Semi-solid range ends at 28% → \(w_P = 28\%\)
    Fluid-like state starts at 40% → \(w_L = 40\%\)
  2. Calculate \(I_P\):
    \[I_P = 40\% - 28\% = 12\% \]
  3. Determine Clay Fraction:
    Fine-grained soil consists of silt and clay:
    \[\%\text{ Clay} = 100\% - 60\%\text{ (Silt)} = 40\% \]
  4. Calculate Activity:
    \[A = \frac{12}{40} = 0.30 \]

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (C)

questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE for the relation between discharge velocity and seepage velocity?
options: Seepage velocity is always smaller than discharge velocity
Seepage velocity can never be smaller than discharge velocity
Seepage velocity is equal to the discharge velocity

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Seepage and Permeability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Conceptual relationship between discharge velocity (\(v\)) and seepage velocity (\(v_s\)).
  • Aim: Identify the true statement comparing \(v\) and \(v_s\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Discharge Velocity (\(v\)): Apparent velocity of water flowing through the total cross-sectional area of the soil mass.
  • Seepage Velocity (\(v_s\)): Actual velocity of water flowing through the void spaces only.
  • Relationship: \(v_s = \dfrac{v}{n}\), where \(n\) is the porosity of the soil.
  • Porosity Bounds: For any soil mass, \(0 < n < 1\).

4. Solution Method:

Since \(n < 1\), dividing \(v\) by \(n\) yields a number larger than \(v\). Therefore \(v_s > v\) always.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • \(v_s = \dfrac{v}{n}\) and \(n < 1 \implies v_s > v\)
  • (A) — False: \(v_s\) is larger, not smaller.
  • (B) — True: \(v_s\) can never be smaller than \(v\).
  • (C) — False: \(n \neq 1\) for real soils.
  • (D) — False: the relationship does exist.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (B)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Options correlating sampler dimensions with the degree of disturbance.
  • Aim: Identify the correct statement regarding soil sample disturbance.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Area Ratio (\(A_r\)): The primary metric governing sample disturbance: \[A_r = \left(\frac{D_e^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2}\right) \times 100\% \] where \(D_e\) = external diameter, \(D_i\) = internal diameter.
  • Design Principle: A higher \(A_r\) indicates a thicker wall → displaces more soil → higher disturbance. For an undisturbed sample, \(A_r\) should be less than 10%.

4. Solution Method:

A thinner wall → smaller \(D_e\) relative to \(D_i\) → lower \(A_r\) → less soil displaced → lower disturbance.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • (A) "Thinner the sampler wall, lower the degree of disturbance" → True: \(A_r\) is minimized.
  • (B) "Thicker the sampler wall, lower..." → False: Thicker walls displace more soil.
  • (C) "Unrelated" → False.
  • (D) "Proportional to the inner diameter" → False: It relates to the area ratio (difference of squares).

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q24
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In an unconsolidated undrained triaxial test, it is observed that an increase in cell pressure from 150 kPa to 250 kPa leads to a pore pressure increase of 80 kPa. It is further observed that, an increase of 50 kPa in deviatoric stress results in an increase of 25 kPa in the pore pressure. The value of Skempton’s pore pressure parameter B is:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength of Soil

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Unconsolidated Undrained (UU) triaxial test:
    StageApplied Stress IncrementPore Pressure Increase
    Stage 1 (Cell pressure)\(\Delta\sigma_3 = 250 - 150 = 100\text{ kPa}\)\(\Delta u_c = 80\text{ kPa}\)
    Stage 2 (Shearing)\(\Delta\sigma_d = 50\text{ kPa}\)\(\Delta u_d = 25\text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Calculate Skempton's pore pressure parameter \(B\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Skempton's Pore Pressure Equation: \[ \Delta u = B\left[\Delta\sigma_3 + A(\Delta\sigma_1 - \Delta\sigma_3)\right] \]
  • Cell Pressure Stage (deviatoric stress = 0): simplifies to \(\Delta u_c = B\,\Delta\sigma_3\)
  • Shearing Stage (cell pressure constant): simplifies to \(\Delta u_d = B \cdot A \cdot \Delta\sigma_d\)

4. Solution Method:

Since only parameter \(B\) is required, use only Stage 1 data.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Isolate relevant equation:
    \[\Delta u_c = B\,\Delta\sigma_3 \]
  2. Substitute values:
    \[80\text{ kPa} = B \times 100\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Calculate B:
    \[B = \frac{80}{100} = 0.8 \]
    Note: Parameter A can be found as \(25 = 0.8 \times A \times 50 \implies A = 0.625\), but is not required here.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (C)

questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Loose sand exhibits contractive behavior upon shearing
Dense sand when sheared under undrained condition, may lead to generation of negative pore pressure
Black cotton soil exhibits expansive behavior
Liquefaction is the phenomenon where cohesionless soil near the downstream side of dams or sheet-piles loses its shear strength due to high upward hydraulic gradient

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: Loose sand exhibits contractive behavior upon shearing
structuredOptions.html: Loose sand exhibits contractive behavior upon shearing

structuredOptions.label: B

structuredOptions.html: Dense sand when sheared under undrained condition, may lead to generation of negative pore pressure

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Black cotton soil exhibits expansive behavior
structuredOptions.html: Black cotton soil exhibits expansive behavior

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Liquefaction is the phenomenon where cohesionless soil near the downstream side of dams or sheet-piles loses its shear strength due to high upward hydraulic gradient
structuredOptions.html: Liquefaction is the phenomenon where cohesionless soil near the downstream side of dams or sheet-piles loses its shear strength due to high upward hydraulic gradient

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength & Deep Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Four statements describing various soil mechanics phenomena.
  • Aim: Identify the statement that is NOT correct.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Contractive/Dilative Behavior: Loose sands contract (decrease in volume) on shearing. Dense sands dilate (increase in volume). Under undrained conditions, dilation causes negative pore pressures.
  • Expansive Soils: Soils rich in montmorillonite (e.g., Black cotton soil) exhibit severe volume changes (swelling/shrinkage) upon wetting/drying.
  • Piping / Quick Sand Condition: Loss of shear strength due to upward seepage forces (high hydraulic gradient) counteracting effective stress — common near downstream toes of dams.
  • Liquefaction: Complete loss of shear strength in saturated, loose cohesionless soils due to rapid pore pressure build-up during dynamic or cyclic loading (e.g., earthquakes) — not due to an upward hydraulic gradient.

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate the factual accuracy of each statement based on fundamental soil mechanics principles.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • (A) Loose sand exhibits contractive behavior → True.
  • (B) Dense sand sheared under undrained conditions may generate negative pore pressure → True (due to dilation tendency).
  • (C) Black cotton soil exhibits expansive behavior → True.
  • (D) "Liquefaction is the phenomenon... due to high upward hydraulic gradient" → False. This describes piping/quick sand. Liquefaction requires dynamic/cyclic loading, not merely an upward seepage gradient.

6. Final Answer:

Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A water tank is to be constructed on the soil deposit shown in the figure below. A circular footing of diameter 3 m and depth of embedment 1 m has been designed to support the tank. The total vertical load to be taken by the footing is 1500 kN. Assume the unit weight of water as 10 kN/m³ and the load dispersion pattern as 2V:1H. The expected settlement of the tank due to primary consolidation of the clay layer is __________ mm.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Consolidation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Diameter of circular footing: \(D = 3\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of embedment: \(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Vertical load on footing: \(Q = 1500\text{ kN}\)
    • Load dispersion pattern: \(2V:1H\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Soil Profile:
      Depth (m)Soil TypeProperties
      0 to 2Silty Sand\(\gamma_{bulk} = 15\text{ kN/m}^3\) (GWT at 2 m)
      2 to 8Sand\(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
      8 to 18NC Clay\(\gamma_{sat} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(C_c = 0.3\), \(e_0 = 0.7\)
  • Aim: Calculate the primary consolidation settlement of the clay layer in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma_0'\)): Calculated at mid-depth of the clay layer. \[\sigma_0' = \sum(\gamma \cdot z) - u\]
  • Stress Increment (\(\Delta\sigma'\)): Using \(2V:1H\) dispersion: \[\Delta\sigma' = \frac{Q}{A_z} = \frac{Q}{\dfrac{\pi}{4}(D+z)^2}\] where \(z\) = depth from footing base to center of clay layer.
  • Primary Settlement (\(S_c\)): \[S_c = \frac{C_c H_0}{1+e_0}\log_{10}\left(\frac{\sigma_0' + \Delta\sigma'}{\sigma_0'}\right)\]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Locate the center of the clay layer:
    Thickness: \(H_0 = 18 - 8 = 10\text{ m}\)
    Depth to center from GL \(= 8 + \dfrac{10}{2} = 13\text{ m}\)
  2. Calculate Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma_0'\)) at 13 m depth:
    \[\Delta\sigma_1' = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ kPa} \quad (0\text{ to }2\text{ m, Silty Sand}) \]\[\Delta\sigma_2' = (18-10) \times 6 = 48\text{ kPa} \quad (2\text{ to }8\text{ m, Sand}) \]\[\Delta\sigma_3' = (18-10) \times 5 = 40\text{ kPa} \quad (8\text{ to }13\text{ m, Clay half-depth}) \]\[\sigma_0' = 30 + 48 + 40 = 118\text{ kPa} \]
  3. Calculate Stress Increment (\(\Delta\sigma'\)) at 13 m depth:
    Distance from footing base to center of clay: \(z = 13 - 1 = 12\text{ m}\)
    \[D_z = D + z = 3 + 12 = 15\text{ m} \]\[A_z = \frac{\pi}{4}(15)^2 = 176.715\text{ m}^2 \]\[\Delta\sigma' = \frac{1500}{176.715} = 8.488\text{ kPa} \]
  4. Calculate Consolidation Settlement (\(S_c\)):
    \(H_0 = 10\text{ m} = 10000\text{ mm}\)
    \[S_c = \frac{0.3 \times 10000}{1+0.7}\log_{10}\left(\frac{118 + 8.488}{118}\right) \]\[S_c = \frac{3000}{1.7}\log_{10}(1.0719) = 1764.706 \times 0.03016 = 53.23\text{ mm} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 53.23 mm  |  Accepted key range: 50.0 to 55.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A 20 m thick clay layer is sandwiched between a silty sand layer and a gravelly sand layer. The layer experiences 30 mm settlement in 2 years.

Given:
\[T_v = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\pi}{4} \left( \dfrac{U}{100} \right)^2 & \text{for } U \le 60\% \\ 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - U) & \text{for } U > 60\% \end{cases} \]

where \(T_v\) is the time factor and \(U\) is the degree of consolidation in %.

If the coefficient of consolidation of the layer is 0.003 cm²/s, the deposit will experience a total of 50 mm settlement in the next __________ years.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Consolidation Time)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Thickness of clay: \(H = 20\text{ m}\) (sandwiched between sand layers → double drainage)
    • Settlement at \(t_1 = 2\text{ years}\): \(S_1 = 30\text{ mm}\)
    • Coefficient of consolidation: \(c_v = 0.003\text{ cm}^2/\text{s} = 3 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}\)
  • Aim: Find the additional time required to reach a total settlement \(S_2 = 50\text{ mm}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Drainage path length: \(d = H/2 = 10\text{ m}\)
  • Time Factor: \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v t}{d^2}\)
  • For \(U \leq 60\%\): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{U}{100}\right)^2\)
  • For \(U > 60\%\): \(T_v = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100-U)\)

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(T_{v1}\) at \(t_1 = 2\) years:
    \(t_1 = 2 \times 365 \times 24 \times 3600 = 6.3072 \times 10^7\text{ s}\)
    \[T_{v1} = \frac{(3 \times 10^{-7}) \times (6.3072 \times 10^7)}{(10)^2} = \frac{18.9216}{100} = 0.1892 \]
  2. Find Degree of Consolidation \(U_1\) and Ultimate Settlement \(S_f\):
    Since \(T_{v1} = 0.1892 < 0.282\), use: \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\left(\dfrac{U}{100}\right)^2\)
    \[\frac{U_1}{100} = \sqrt{\frac{0.1892 \times 4}{\pi}} = 0.4908 \implies U_1 = 49.08\% \]\[S_f = \frac{S_1}{U_1} = \frac{30}{0.4908} = 61.12\text{ mm} \]
  3. Find Time \(t_2\) for total settlement \(S_2 = 50\) mm:
    \[U_2 = \frac{50}{61.12} = 0.818 = 81.8\% \]
    Since \(U_2 > 60\%\), use the logarithmic equation:
    \[T_{v2} = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - 81.8) = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(18.2) \]\[T_{v2} = 1.781 - 0.933(1.260) = 1.781 - 1.1756 = 0.6054 \]\[t_2 = \frac{T_{v2}\,d^2}{c_v} = \frac{0.6054 \times 100}{3 \times 10^{-7}} = 20.18 \times 10^7\text{ s} = 6.40\text{ years} \]
  4. Calculate additional time:
    \[\Delta t = t_2 - t_1 = 6.40 - 2.0 = 4.40\text{ years} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.40 years  |  Accepted key range: 4.0 to 5.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A non-homogeneous soil deposit consists of a silt layer sandwiched between a fine-sand layer at top and a clay layer below. Permeability of the silt layer is 10 times the permeability of the clay layer and one-tenth of the permeability of the sand layer. Thickness of the silt layer is 2 times the thickness of the sand layer and two-third of the thickness of the clay layer. The ratio of equivalent horizontal and equivalent vertical permeability of the deposit is __________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics (Permeability)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • 3 layers: Fine Sand (Top), Silt (Middle), Clay (Bottom)
    • Permeability relations: \(k_{silt} = 10\,k_{clay}\) and \(k_{silt} = 0.1\,k_{sand}\)
    • Thickness relations: \(H_{silt} = 2\,H_{sand}\) and \(H_{silt} = \dfrac{2}{3}\,H_{clay}\)
  • Aim: Find the ratio \(k_h / k_v\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Equivalent Horizontal Permeability (parallel to bedding): \[k_h = \frac{\sum(k_i H_i)}{\sum H_i} \]
  • Equivalent Vertical Permeability (perpendicular to bedding): \[k_v = \frac{\sum H_i}{\sum(H_i / k_i)} \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Establish Relative Variables:
    Let \(k_{clay} = k\), then: \(k_{silt} = 10k\), \(k_{sand} = 10 \times k_{silt} = 100k\)
    Let \(H_{sand} = H\), then: \(H_{silt} = 2H\), \(H_{clay} = \dfrac{3}{2}(2H) = 3H\)
    Total thickness \(= H + 2H + 3H = 6H\)
  2. Calculate \(k_h\):
    \[k_h = \frac{(100k \cdot H) + (10k \cdot 2H) + (k \cdot 3H)}{6H} = \frac{100k + 20k + 3k}{6} = \frac{123k}{6} = 20.5k \]
  3. Calculate \(k_v\):
    \[k_v = \frac{6H}{\dfrac{H}{100k} + \dfrac{2H}{10k} + \dfrac{3H}{k}} = \frac{6H}{H\left(\dfrac{1 + 20 + 300}{100k}\right)} = \frac{6 \times 100k}{321} = \frac{600k}{321} = 1.869k \]
  4. Calculate the Ratio:
    \[\frac{k_h}{k_v} = \frac{20.5k}{1.869k} = 10.97 \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10.97  |  Accepted key range: 10.0 to 12.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A square footing (2 m x 2 m) is subjected to an inclined point load, P as shown in the figure below. The water table is located well below the base of the footing. Considering one-way eccentricity, the net safe load carrying capacity of the footing for a factor of safety of 3.0 is __________ kN.

The following factors may be used:

Bearing capacity factors: \(N_q = 33.3, N_\gamma = 37.16\); Shape factors: \(F_{qs} = F_{\gamma s} = 1.314\); Depth factors: \(F_{qd} = F_{\gamma d} = 1.113\); Inclination factors: \(F_{qi} = 0.444, F_{\gamma i} = 0.02\)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering (Bearing Capacity)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application & Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Square footing: \(2\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m}\) (\(B = 2\text{ m}\), \(L = 2\text{ m}\))
    • Depth of embedment: \(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)
    • Eccentricity: Load applied at \(0.85\text{ m}\) from edge \(\implies e = 1.0 - 0.85 = 0.15\text{ m}\)
    • \(\gamma = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\), \(c = 0\), \(\phi = 35^\circ\)
    • Load inclined at \(\alpha = 30^\circ\) to vertical
    • Bearing capacity, shape, depth, and inclination factors are provided.
    • Factor of Safety: \(\text{FOS} = 3.0\)
  • Aim: Determine the net safe load carrying capacity (kN).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Meyerhof's Effective Area Method: For eccentric loading, modified dimensions: \(B' = B - 2e\), \(L' = L\), \(A' = B' \times L'\)
  • Ultimate Bearing Capacity: \[q_u = \bar{q}\,N_q\,F_{qs}\,F_{qd}\,F_{qi} + \frac{1}{2}\gamma B'\,N_\gamma\,F_{\gamma s}\,F_{\gamma d}\,F_{\gamma i} \]
  • Net Safe Load: \[q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f, \quad q_{ns} = \frac{q_{nu}}{\text{FOS}}, \quad Q_{ns} = q_{ns} \times A' \]

4. Solution Method & Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Effective Dimensions:
    \[B' = 2 - 2(0.15) = 1.7\text{ m}, \quad L' = 2\text{ m} \]\[A' = 1.7 \times 2 = 3.4\text{ m}^2 \]\[\bar{q} = \gamma D_f = 18 \times 1 = 18\text{ kPa} \]
  2. Calculate Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_u\)):
    • \(q\)-term: \(18 \times 33.3 \times 1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.444 = 389.28\text{ kPa}\)
    • \(\gamma\)-term: \(0.5 \times 18 \times 1.7 \times 37.16 \times 1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.02 = 16.63\text{ kPa}\)
    • \(q_u = 389.28 + 16.63 = 405.91\text{ kPa}\)
  3. Calculate Net Safe Vertical Load:
    \[q_{nu} = 405.91 - 18 = 387.91\text{ kPa} \]\[q_{ns} = \frac{387.91}{3} = 129.30\text{ kPa} \]\[Q_{ns} = 129.30 \times 3.4 = 439.63\text{ kN} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 439.63 kN  |  Accepted key range: 434 to 444

questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: If the water content of a fully saturated soil mass is 100%, the void ratio of the sample is:
options: less than specific gravity of soil
equal to specific gravity of soil
greater than specific gravity of soil
independent of specific gravity of soil

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: less than specific gravity of soil
structuredOptions.html: less than specific gravity of soil

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: equal to specific gravity of soil
structuredOptions.html: equal to specific gravity of soil

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: greater than specific gravity of soil
structuredOptions.html: greater than specific gravity of soil

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: independent of specific gravity of soil
structuredOptions.html: independent of specific gravity of soil

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics Properties

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Fully saturated soil mass \(\Rightarrow\) Degree of saturation, \(S = 100\%\) or \(1.0\)
    • Water content, \(w = 100\%\) or \(1.0\)
  • Aim: Determine the void ratio (\(e\)) of the sample and its relationship to the specific gravity (\(G\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Fundamental phase relationship in soil mechanics relating degree of saturation (\(S\)), void ratio (\(e\)), water content (\(w\)), and specific gravity of soil solids (\(G\)):\[S \cdot e = w \cdot G \]

4. Solution Method:

Substitute the given values of \(S\) and \(w\) (as decimals) into the standard equation and solve for \(e\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Step 1: Write the foundational relation:\[S \cdot e = w \cdot G \]
  2. Step 2: Insert \(S = 1.0\) and \(w = 1.0\):\[(1.0) \cdot e = (1.0) \cdot G \]
  3. Step 3: Simplify:\[e = G \]The void ratio is exactly equal to the specific gravity of the soil.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Equal to specific gravity of soil  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q23
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: In friction circle method of slope stability analysis, if r defines the radius of the slip circle, the radius of friction circle is:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Slope Stability

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data:
    • Slip circle radius \(= r\)
    • Method of analysis: Friction circle method
  • Aim: Define the radius of the friction circle.

3. Core Concepts:

Friction Circle Method: Used for analyzing the stability of finite slopes in \(c\)-\(\phi\) soils. It assumes that the resultant intergranular (frictional) force along the failure surface is entirely tangential to a smaller, concentric "friction circle" inside the main slip circle. The radius of this inner friction circle (\(R_f\)) is determined using the mobilized angle of internal friction (\(\phi\)) and the slip circle radius (\(r\)).

4. Solution Method:

By trigonometric geometry of the forces assumed in the method, the lever arm of the cohesive and frictional forces acting on the slip surface forms a right angle with the radius vector at an angle \(\phi\). The perpendicular distance from the center of rotation to the line of action of the resultant frictional force equals the friction circle radius:\[R_f = r \cdot \sin\phi \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Recognized formula directly: \(R_f = r\sin\phi\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(r\sin\phi\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q24
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Net ultimate bearing capacity of a footing embedded in a clay stratum
options: increases with depth of footing only
increases with size of footing only
increases with depth and size of footing
is independent of depth and size of footing

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: increases with depth of footing only
structuredOptions.html: increases with depth of footing only

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: increases with size of footing only
structuredOptions.html: increases with size of footing only

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: increases with depth and size of footing
structuredOptions.html: increases with depth and size of footing

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: is independent of depth and size of footing
structuredOptions.html: is independent of depth and size of footing

questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: A footing embedded in a cohesive clay stratum.
  • Aim: Determine the dependence of the "net ultimate bearing capacity" on footing depth and size.

3. Core Concepts:

For pure clay under undrained conditions, the angle of internal friction \(\phi = 0\).

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity Theory: The ultimate bearing capacity is given by:\[q_u = c N_c + \gamma D_f N_q + 0.5\, \gamma B N_\gamma \]For \(\phi = 0\), the bearing capacity factors are: \(N_c = 5.7\), \(N_q = 1\), and \(N_\gamma = 0\).

Net Ultimate Bearing Capacity (\(q_{nu}\)):\[q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f \]Note: While Skempton's equations introduce shape and depth factors making \(q_{nu}\) dependent on \(B\) and \(D_f\), standard Terzaghi assumptions — which represent baseline textbook theory often tested for this specific conclusion — yield a constant \(N_c\).

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate Terzaghi's expression for \(\phi = 0\):\[q_{nu} = (c N_c + \gamma D_f \cdot 1 + 0) - \gamma D_f \]\[q_{nu} = c N_c = 5.7c \]Because \(5.7c\) contains neither \(D_f\) (depth) nor \(B\) (size), it is mathematically independent of both parameters.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate \(q_u\): \(q_u = c N_c + \gamma D_f\)
  2. Find \(q_{nu}\): \(q_{nu} = q_u - \gamma D_f = c N_c\)
  3. Conclude that for purely cohesive soil using classic Terzaghi theory, \(q_{nu}\) is solely a function of cohesion \(c\) and factor \(N_c\). It does not change with varying \(D_f\) or \(B\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Is independent of depth and size of footing  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q25
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Surcharge loading required to be placed on the horizontal backfill of a smooth retaining vertical wall so as to completely eliminate tensile crack is:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Smooth, vertical retaining wall.
    • Horizontal backfill of cohesive soil (cohesion \(c\)).
    • Active earth pressure coefficient: \(K_a\).
  • Aim: Calculate the magnitude of the uniform surcharge load (\(q\)) needed at the surface to completely prevent tension crack formation.

3. Core Concepts:

Active Earth Pressure in Cohesive Soil (\(c\)-\(\phi\) soil):\[p_a = K_a \sigma_v - 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]where \(\sigma_v\) is the total vertical stress at depth \(z\).

Tensile Crack Formation: Near the surface, if \(p_a\) becomes negative, the soil goes into tension, causing cracks. To completely eliminate the tension crack, the active pressure at the very top (\(z = 0\)) must be at least zero (\(p_a \ge 0\)).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Express \(\sigma_v\) at depth \(z = 0\) under a surcharge load \(q\).
  2. Substitute \(\sigma_v\) into the active earth pressure equation.
  3. Set \(p_a = 0\) at the surface to find the minimum required surcharge \(q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Evaluate vertical stress at \(z = 0\):\[\sigma_v = \gamma(0) + q = q \]

Step 2: Formulate active pressure at the surface:\[p_a = K_a \cdot q - 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]

Step 3: Set \(p_a = 0\) to find the threshold where tension is completely eradicated:\[K_a \cdot q - 2c\sqrt{K_a} = 0 \]\[K_a \cdot q = 2c\sqrt{K_a} \]

Step 4: Solve for surcharge loading \(q\):\[q = \frac{2c\sqrt{K_a}}{K_a} = \frac{2c}{\sqrt{K_a}} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{2c}{\sqrt{K_a}}\)  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q47
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 588 cm³ volume of moist sand weighs 1010 gm. Its dry weight is 918 gm and specific gravity of solids, G is 2.67. Assuming density of water as 1 gm/cm³, the void ratio is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total volume: \(V = 588\) cm³
    • Moist weight: \(W_{moist} = 1010\) gm
    • Dry weight of solids: \(W_s = 918\) gm
    • Specific gravity: \(G = 2.67\)
    • \(\rho_w = 1\) gm/cm³
  • Aim: Void ratio \(e\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Dry Density: \(\gamma_d = \dfrac{W_s}{V}\)
  • Void Ratio Relationship: \(\gamma_d = \dfrac{G \cdot \gamma_w}{1 + e}\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compute the dry density:\[\gamma_d = \frac{918}{588} = 1.5612 \text{ gm/cm}^3 \]
  2. Substitute into the specific gravity–void ratio relationship:\[1.5612 = \frac{2.67 \times 1.0}{1 + e} \implies 1 + e = \frac{2.67}{1.5612} = 1.7102 \]
  3. Solve for void ratio:\[e = 1.7102 - 1 = 0.7102 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.71  |  Accepted key range: 0.70 to 0.72

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q48
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 4 m thick layer of normally consolidated clay has an average void ratio of 1.30. Its compression index is 0.6 and coefficient of consolidation is 1 m²/yr. If the increase in vertical pressure due to foundation load on the clay layer is equal to the existing effective overburden pressure, the change in the thickness of the clay layer is _____________ mm
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Clay thickness: \(H_0 = 4000\) mm
    • Initial void ratio: \(e_0 = 1.30\)
    • Compression index: \(C_c = 0.6\)
    • Added pressure equals existing effective overburden pressure: \(\Delta\sigma' = \sigma'_0\)
  • Aim: Change in thickness \(\Delta H\) in mm.

3. Core Concepts:

Primary consolidation settlement equation for Normally Consolidated (NC) clay:\[\Delta H = H_0 \left(\frac{C_c}{1 + e_0}\right) \log_{10}\left(\frac{\sigma'_0 + \Delta\sigma'}{\sigma'_0}\right) \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate the stress ratio term:
    Since \(\Delta\sigma' = \sigma'_0\), final stress \(\sigma'_f = 2\sigma'_0\).\[\frac{\sigma'_f}{\sigma'_0} = 2 \]
  2. Compute the settlement:\[\Delta H = 4000 \times \left(\frac{0.6}{1 + 1.30}\right) \times \log_{10}(2) \]\[\Delta H = 4000 \times \frac{0.6}{2.3} \times 0.30103 \]\[\Delta H = 1043.478 \times 0.30103 = 314.12 \text{ mm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 314.12 mm  |  Accepted key range: 313.0 to 316.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A pile of diameter 0.4 m is fully embedded in a clay stratum having 5 layers, each 5 m thick as shown in the figure below. Assume a constant unit weight of soil as 18 kN/m³ for all the layers. Using λ-method (λ = 0.15 for 25 m embedment length) and neglecting the end bearing component, the ultimate pile capacity (in kN) is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Foundation Engineering (Pile Capacity)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pile diameter: \(D = 0.4\) m
    • Fully embedded length: \(L = 25\) m in 5 clay layers of 5 m each.
    • Unit weight: \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³ throughout.
    • \(c_u\) array: 40, 50, 60, 70, 80 kPa (layer by layer).
    • \(\lambda = 0.15\). Neglect end bearing.
  • Aim: Ultimate pile capacity using the \(\lambda\)-method.

3. Core Concepts:

According to Vijayvergiya and Focht's \(\lambda\)-method, the average unit skin friction is:\[f_{av} = \lambda(\bar{\sigma}'_v + 2\bar{c}_u) \]where \(\bar{\sigma}'_v\) is the mean effective vertical stress and \(\bar{c}_u\) is the mean undrained shear strength.
Pile capacity: \(Q_u \approx Q_s = f_{av} \times (\pi \cdot D \cdot L)\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mean Effective Vertical Stress (\(\bar{\sigma}'_v\)):
    Stress at surface \(= 0\). Stress at bottom \(= 18 \times 25 = 450\) kPa.\[\bar{\sigma}'_v = \frac{0 + 450}{2} = 225 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Mean Undrained Shear Strength (\(\bar{c}_u\)):\[\bar{c}_u = \frac{40 + 50 + 60 + 70 + 80}{5} = 60 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Average Unit Skin Friction (\(f_{av}\)):\[f_{av} = 0.15 \times (225 + 2 \times 60) = 0.15 \times 345 = 51.75 \text{ kPa} \]
  4. Ultimate Capacity (\(Q_u\)):\[Q_u = 51.75 \times \pi \times 0.4 \times 25 = 51.75 \times 10\pi = 1625.77 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1625.77 kN  |  Accepted key range: 1620.0 to 1630.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: Stress path equation for tri-axial test upon application of deviatoric stress is, \(q = 10\sqrt{3} + 0.5 p\). The respective values of cohesion, c (in kPa) and angle of internal friction, φ are:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shear Strength

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Equation for stress path: \(q = 10\sqrt{3} + 0.5p\)
  • Aim: Find cohesion (\(c\)) and angle of internal friction (\(\phi\)).

3. Core Concepts:

In triaxial compression stress paths, the geometric parameters \((p, q)\) relate to Mohr-Coulomb parameters \((c, \phi)\) via:\[p = \frac{\sigma_1 + \sigma_3}{2}, \quad q = \frac{\sigma_1 - \sigma_3}{2} \]The failure envelope in the \(p\)-\(q\) plane is expressed as:\[q = p\sin\phi + c\cos\phi \]

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Compare \(q = 0.5p + 10\sqrt{3}\) with the standard equation \(q = p\sin\phi + c\cos\phi\).
  2. Angle of Internal Friction (\(\phi\)):\[\sin\phi = 0.5 \implies \phi = \arcsin(0.5) = 30^\circ \]
  3. Cohesion (\(c\)):\[c\cos(30^\circ) = 10\sqrt{3} \]\[c \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 10\sqrt{3} \implies c = 20 \text{ kPa} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(c = 20\) kPa, \(\phi = 30^\circ\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A 6 m high retaining wall having a smooth vertical back face retains a layered horizontal backfill. Top 3 m thick layer of the backfill is sand having an angle of internal friction, φ = 30° while the bottom layer is 3 m thick clay with cohesion, c = 20 kPa. Assume unit weight for both sand and clay as 18 kN/m³. The total active earth pressure per unit length of the wall (in kN/m) is:
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Earth Pressure

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: 6 m retaining wall.
    • Top 3 m: Sand, \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³, \(c = 0\), \(\phi = 30^\circ\).
    • Bottom 3 m: Clay, \(\gamma = 18\) kN/m³, \(c = 20\) kPa, \(\phi = 0^\circ\).
  • Aim: Total active earth pressure per unit length.

3. Core Concepts:

Active Earth Pressure Equation: \(p_a = K_a\sigma_v - 2c\sqrt{K_a}\)

Coefficient of Active Earth Pressure: \(K_a = \dfrac{1 - \sin\phi}{1 + \sin\phi}\)

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Top Sand Layer (0 to 3 m):\[K_{a1} = \frac{1 - \sin 30^\circ}{1 + \sin 30^\circ} = \frac{0.5}{1.5} = \frac{1}{3} \]\(p_a\) at top (\(z = 0\)): \(0\)
    \(p_a\) at bottom of sand (\(z = 3\) m): \(\dfrac{1}{3} \times 18 \times 3 = 18\) kPa\[P_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 3 = 27 \text{ kN/m} \]
  2. Bottom Clay Layer (3 to 6 m):\[\phi = 0^\circ \implies K_{a2} = 1 \]Overburden at \(z = 3\) m: \(\sigma_v = 18 \times 3 = 54\) kPa\[p_a \text{ at top of clay} = 1(54) - 2(20) = 14 \text{ kPa} \]Overburden at \(z = 6\) m: \(\sigma_v = 54 + 54 = 108\) kPa\[p_a \text{ at bottom of clay} = 1(108) - 2(20) = 68 \text{ kPa} \]\[P_2 = \frac{14 + 68}{2} \times 3 = 41 \times 3 = 123 \text{ kN/m} \]
  3. Total Force:\[P_{total} = P_1 + P_2 = 27 + 123 = 150 \text{ kN/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 150 kN/m  |  Correct option: (A)
